author: Miss Print

title: Became too profit driven, deleting the app
body:
Once an app gets too big, the app starts to lose focus of the app’s main purpose. That’s what happened to Forest. 

It used to be so straight forward, which is just to track your study time and you get a digital tree in your forest for studying. Now, it’s all about trying to make you buy coins, pop ups after pop ups, and trying to get you to get this type of tree and plant. It’s so silly to me. Do they not know the demographics of their users? 

Are people really paying for “coins”? And for what? JUST focus on studying and passing your class/exams. 

The last straw for me was the app removing the total focus  time of the day on the main screen. what?? That’s literally the whole point of a study app…. To track your total time spent studying. 

I know they see their growing user base and now all they think about is how to extract money from each of them. It’s literally just a study app.. what kind of big money do y’all really think you will eventually make? 

Farewell. I’ll be using another study app from now on.

author: SeanHatz

title: Too much AI, which is a shame.
body: I bought forest a while ago and it really improved my study sessions. It’s genuinely an amazing app and I love that you can buy the customizations for free if you just focus enough and grow enough trees. I also think the in-game coins to real life trees system is amazing! If only you didn’t immediately kill those trees by promoting the use of AI. I stopped using the app a few years ago and picked it back up for college, and everything changed. The user interface is TERRIBLE. It’s slow when trying to go anywhere but the main planting menu. And when you are done with a session, you click like 5 times on a button that says go home. I clicked “Go home” already, let me go. Other people have tried emailing support with complaints about ads (since I was an early supporter, I get an ad free experience) and they got a fully generative AI response which included the AI thinking process, of which included the AI not furthering the request for a refund because the user said they “wished” they could request a refund instead of saying “I would like to request a refund.” It’s insane to me that a company who promotes trees and understands that people do, in fact, like trees, doesn’t understand that using AI to generate and manage your entire app is scummy. This company should be ashamed.

title: Love with caveats
body: I use this app every day. I mostly use it for writing my novel because it creates structure and prevents me from drifting off into ADHD land. It takes me three clicks to get back to the screen where I can restart it. It sounds like a small thing, but it shifts my thinking to the app rather than my writing. Please please please restore the ability to restart the timer with one click!

title: It’s nice!
body:
So let me start with, I really like this app. It’s improved a lot! I love how the tree’s is growth process is no longer inside a circle. I also really like how you can plant real trees! I bought this app about 2-4 years ago, so not much ago, but I am a pro user. I was a bit disappointed because it went free, but most of all, it started having a subscription. Then, I quit the app. This year, about a week or two ago I finally downloaded it again. I’m still really disappointed that there’s a subscription even for people who payed for it first, but it’s still a nice app. Also, I couldn’t find the actual prices of the subscription in the app. Just a trial. I would like to at least know how much it costs before I have a trial! Overall, I recommend this. There have been ways it’s been disappointing but I get it, and this app has really improved in the time I left it. It’s clean, and kids and teens and adults can use it. (I do have ad-blocker though, so I’m not sure if this app has ads, and if appropriate, but the app itself is clean!) Thanks for reading my long review!
EDIT: I put my tree and then worked in Quizlet. I went back to the app to check on it. The screen was white, so I just got out and in, then it said I killed my tree, and it died. I didn’t do anything, though? That was 50 minutes lost. :(

author: gogli11

title: Retro User
body:
I first downloaded this app about 6 years ago and used it with a friend. We both loved it; it was a simple way to keep us both off our phones and on task. Each of us even bought a subscription. 

These past few months, the UI updates and AI integration have made this app so, so clunky. It breaks my heart to say that it's an eyesore now. The designs feel so much less simple and human-made. Clicking through a series of prompts makes the planting feature less efficient to use. 

Please, please offer some settings to help us go back to the way things were. Cut the AI garbage and cumbersome UI. For an app that espouses the value of getting off screen and going out into the world to do good (planting trees irl, getting your work done and be a functioning person), the AI integration is such a big disappointment. 

I've been actively searching for better apps to use. Please Forest, listen to those of us posting here and online.

author: Saud11333

title: Favorite Studying Tool
body: If you’re someone who loves to game-ify the mundane, this app should be right up your alley. I didn’t think this would be my holy grail study tool, but that’s what it’s become. Being able to look back and see all the progress I’ve made studying for my Associates and now my Bachelors is so reaffirming and inspiring. I really love the newer “stopwatch” feature, as instead of having the pressure of meeting a certain time, I’m able to just go with the incentive that if I hit that 2-hour make, the tree will surely come into full bloom. I’d recommend this app to anyone who wants a gentle nudge away from their phone for any reason, and I’m seriously considering upgrading to Premium because I just love the app, and they have an incredible mission behind them (which is what drew me in to begin with)!
author: SalemIsScreaming

title: Stop asking for money
body:
Stop monetizing everything. Stop pushing the subscription onto everyone. I already paid you, I’m not giving you more. And a lot of users are probably students who should be pressured into paying for features that should be free. Trend analysis as tags aren’t exactly special features that should be behind a paywall. 

It’s so obvious that you only care for the people who pay the subscription. Everything good goes to them. They get bonus daily tasks for gems. They get new trees. I have thousands of coins and absolutely nothing to spend them on because you’re only focusing on things for your subscription. And that’s after the shop got “fixed.” Which it didn’t, not really. You got rid of bundles, which I was saving for since they were a little discounted. You have to hope you’re lucky and get a gem tree that you want when you finally saved enough. We wanted more trees, not whatever this is. 

Just stop. You’ve pushed so many people away from your app because you keep ruining it. You made it take so long just to get to the Home Screen after a session. My app glitched on me today and the alert that the session stopped and rewards came an hour after I stopped it. You made an entire event on a feature that so many people couldn’t find at first since finding it isn’t intuitive. 

Please, for the love of God, stop making this app worse. Stop asking for money when people have already paid.

body:

title: New Update Very Frustrating
body:
I’ve used and enjoyed this app for years, but this new update made sometime in September or October of 2026 has significantly reduced my satisfaction and compelled me to write this review. 

In some apparent effort to make the app something more profitable or inspiring more engagement, they have added all sorts of “events” and continued to focus on the coin shop. Worst of all, though, is they changed the UI so now I have to tap roughly 4 times to exit a timer I just set, when it used to be once. The app also no longer displays my total focus time for the day without having to tap 3-4 times to go see it on a separate screen. Why? They’ve also made many overtures to get me to “relax” as if this is a meditation app or something.

I bought this years ago just to time my focus and track my progress, as well as have a motivator in the form of the tree. Please just keep this simple or give me the option to strip away the excessive features that don’t serve that purpose and make this app more convoluted. I will have to move to a different method in the future, otherwise, and that saddens me since I’ve used this for 5+ years without issue until now.

title: New UI Has Some Pros, But I Haaaaate the Popups
body:

What I like:

What I don’t like:
- Annoying popups flash across my screen when I finish planting a tree and want to back to the home screen! This app is supposed to reduce distractions, not create them. 
- Some of the trees displayed are not purchasable in the store, yet clicking on them still takes me to the store. 
- There are still very few tag colors. Other people and I specifically submitted a feedback request asking for more tag colors, but there are still just a handful. 

What I feel mixed about:
- The trees bounce up and down, and the coin icon shimmers. It’s kind of cool, but also very distracting.



Edit; I changed my review to one star. They’re now deleting trees from the regular store and making you rebuy them for a much higher price only on certain days when they happen to appear in the temporary store that refreshes daily. This is so stupid. It’s clear that they’re creating a scarcity mindset to pressure people to check the app often. That goes against the whole point of making an app to get you off your phone!

title: Downhill Slide
body: I’ve used this app since 2016 and have been a huge advocate for it since early days. While I can’t think of any period of time in the past decade where the Forest app has maintained excellent stability free of glitches, the overall usefulness of the app has allowed me to look past that. In the past 12-18 months, things have been going downhill. The devs keep pushing out excessive updates that prioritize gamification in the app and focus on money-making capacity of the app. All the while, stability in the app for users like myself and my friends has decreased and glitches have increased to the point of a non-functional app. Sharing session links, planting together, and Deep Focus mode are all useless now with the rollout of a new UI and the retirement of “classic” mode. It’s a real shame. I’ve accumulated over 275 days of planting time in this app, the majority of which were logged in Plant Together mode with friends. I’ll be sad to leave the app and my land of virtual trees behind, but it may be the natural course of things if the devs continue to ignore prioritization of the function and stability of the Forest app.

title: I love this app, but…
body:
I really love this app. I’ve been using it for years and have found it very helpful to focus and track my writing time. However, since the introduction of focus challenge I have been annoyed by the implementation. My biggest issue is the fact that I have to reset my focus timer each time I want to “plant a tree” for the challenge. If I do 2 hours in the app, it says I planted 4 trees in my forest but only one tree for the daily challenge. If the daily challenge says “plant any tree 4 times” I have to start and stop my focus timer four times (once every 30 minutes) in order for the trees to count. Why? The fact that I have to interrupt my focus time to stop and reset in order to achieve the daily challenge is ridiculous. It’s actually the opposite of focus, enough that I may have to switch to a different app because it is distracting me trying to keep my trees and focus time to match. 

Please fix this. Make it so that when I focus for a number of hours, the daily challenge counts my trees planted, not by the number of times I started focusing. It feels like a bug, but it’s been present since the focus challenge released. Thanks!

title: New look and streamlined-ness kind of terrible, otherwise love it
body:
Been using this app for years and love it. Don’t seem to have the glitches every other review talks about. But they keep changing the look of the app, and where buttons are, and what direction you need to scroll to pick a tree or a focus title you have, and they do this like every 2-3 months it seems. It makes it feel extremely inconsistent, and when I’ve finally gotten the muscle memory down for the app to feel streamlined and easy to use and find everything in, they suddenly change all of it again, and it becomes frustrating. Pick a look that works and stick with it. Why change the look if it’s not broken? This most recent look/button/scrolling update is so bad it makes me not want to use the app. Everything got enlarged so huge, text runs off the edge of the menu. Buttons are huge, yet for any function I need to go through hoops of multiple buttons or menus, when before it was just one button or everything in one menu. I need to click stop, then collect reward, when before it just collected reward automatically no extra button press needed. Now I need to pick a focus and a tree in two separate menus, tap to enter tree select menu, tap to exit, tap to enter focus title menu, tap to exit. Before these things were in the same menu. What was two buttons to enter and then exit menu, is now 4, since it’s been split into two menus. The way to scroll through trees vertically instead of horizontally feels wrong…who thinks of trees as being stacked on top of each other? No one. It feels kind of unintuitive and unnatural. And now because text is huge, scrolling vertically to pick a focus title out of many that I have is just a hassle and very ugly looking. Maybe this works for people used to reading text vertically, and could be used in those regions, or an option to switch between one or the other for those who prefer that direction of reading, but scrolling vertically through theses feels unnatural to me as well. When reading my eyes want to move left to right, the way it was horizontally scrolling before. But now my brain has to stop and start and stop and start as it jumps up and down the vertical list. 
The extra buttons and menus, and the new scrolling format makes using the app take twice as much time as it did before, which is taking away from the time people want to be focusing on whatever they’re getting set up to focus on. It just feels like twice as much work to use the app now. And everything in the app seems extra large now, like I accidentally bought an extra large print book. I’m not sure who they were making this update for, but it feels like it is not for students or young adults anymore.

title: Recommended by OT but not quite doing the job.
body:
I have AUDHD with some OCD, anxiety and exhaustion. I am dealing with physical disability as well from nervous system and autoimmune issues. I’m in occupational therapy for speech, physical rehab, and soon will be adding visual OT. My speech therapist thinks that the root of a lot of my problems is actually exhaustion from excessive screen time. My screen time has become an escape hatch from my preexisting issues, but it worsens them so it’s an endless feedback loop. We are using this app to try stepping down from my usage of social media in particular. 


Most of us have multiple devices. I have an iPad, MacBook, iPhone and Apple Watch and the app doesn’t automatically sync across these devices. It doesn’t automatically lock down all my devices, I have to grow a tree separately on each even after syncing them. 

It doesn’t reliably block access to apps when in focus mode. It says I’m in focus right now and I can access all my apps without killing my tree. 

I don’t like the stats board. I have premium and it is showing me whatever I’ve tagged my usage as, instead of using existing Apple analytics to populate that chart. Rocket money and Mint seem to be able to create good pie charts and graphs based off access to account info, so wondering why this isn’t the same. 

I find the current description key for the charts comparing one day against another a bit vague. More concise wording is needed to provide a key to understanding that one. Is this even a helpful metric? Why not something more simple and engaging like “wow, you did it! Your break from screens lasted 20% longer than yesterday, with a total of 4.5 hours!” The way it’s set up now is very flat and boring and tbh hard to tell if it’s a positive or negative comparison. 

The daily challenge always has one goal I can’t meet without cashing in all my coins on a plant I don’t have to unlock it. Not a fan of that as a premium user. 

I did like being able to set focus to run from a set time in morning to a set time in evening. I didn’t like that it doesn’t automatically remember this setting and do it every day Monday through Friday (or whatever you prefer). It did it well for my first day, and then wasn’t in place the next morning. I really need the features to run for consecutive days in order for this to work. Relying on me to remember or have the willpower to do this every day in the beginning is not helpful. I have adhd, this is not accounting for how our disability shows up. We are more prone to addiction to screens, and have more difficulty creating new habits, especially when the new habit is in conflict with an established maladaptive ritual. A setting where I can explain what level assistance I need, and then consent to a time frame or schedule for the week/month would work better than what it’s doing now. 


I’d love to see a journal of symptoms and encouragement/coping strategies  included in the app. Other addiction apps provide structured support for the hard parts of cycle breaking. Since I’m doing this on the recommendation of a doctor, would be cool to be able to log symptoms and share that kind of chart with them over time. To view my progress that way. 
For example, I experienced a lot of anxiety and agitation my first day. I had observations about my energy levels, and would like to have stored what I did with my time instead on the app for a productivity chart or something. I also experienced insomnia my first night, and would have benefitted from charting that, sleep as a metric is useful, and possibly links to resources to help fall asleep. 


I hate the “take a break” options. The breathing animation and “peaceful sounds” are awful. They’re loud and distracting, and without sound pretty useless. The breathing is way too fast for calming down. 

And last, I much prefer setting up the app to block my access to specific things for a set time period, vs checking it every 20 minutes or so to get a tree. Why cant we still get trees and coins for the time we are in deep focus for hours? I get ONE tree no matter how long the break is. Repeatedly checking the app is defeating the purpose of staying off the device. Picking it up to do that makes me want to check social media. I’m trying to wean off the default of looking at my phone during my more functional hours when I should be doing IRL things.

I liked Forest because it was a pay-once kind of app, and not subscription based the way most things are nowadays. But now in order to cultivate any sort of beautiful forest or garden on this app, you have to pay exorbitant amounts of money for fake trees and shrubs (any amount of money is exorbitant for fake trees and shrubs on an app i’ve already paid for 🙄). title: Shout out to the Forest team for caring about user satisfaction! 💯
body:
I’m really impressed by how quickly the team addressed the issues I mentioned in a previous review (they were fixed within hours).

In that review, I also suggested bringing back more flexibility with pauses, since some users need short breaks when they notice their attention starting to fade. Being able to pause when needed makes it easier to stay focused during longer sessions and helps Forest better support users who have difficulty concentrating for extended periods.

The app is great as it is, in my opinion, but to better accommodate different users’ needs and study styles without making it too tempting to pause constantly, one suggestion would be to add a setting that lets users toggle between one pause per session and unlimited pauses. Giving users the option to choose their preferred pause setting would make Forest more flexible and supportive for different attention spans and routines.

Overall, I really enjoy Forest and value that the developers listen to user feedback. Thank you for continuing to improve Forest and for creating a functional platform that helps us stay focused and reach our goals.

I understand the need for profit and nothing is for free, but it feels like this update was a little ridiculous.

Inclusion of adds: Fair.

Removal of previously earned trees. : less fair

Tags are now behind a paywall.

Timeline statistics are now only pro. 

Extra bells and whistles like pausing your timer: unneeded.

Seriously, was there a corporate takeover? This is a wild and drastic shift.

title: Это невероятно
body: Помимо того, что приложение имеет серьезное проблемы с уведомлениями, из за которых ты не контролируешь окончание цикла и активацию нового. Вечером приходится буквально сидеть и считать через вкладку «история» время и складывать вручную. После покупки Forest Plus, приложение стало просто фантастически непредсказуемо себя вести. Уведомления приходят случайным образом в разное время в течение активированного цикла по несколько раз. А запущенные циклы на 180 минут потом в конечном итоге показывают во вкладке «история» совершенно другие, ложные! В моем случае это были 8 минут и 12, без прерываний, что уже невозможно! Нет таких опций при выборе времени запуска цикла. В итоге окончательное время в конце рабочего/учебного дня критично разнится с реальными затраченными часами сосредоточенности. Это невероятно, нет слов. Приложение - вакханалия и дилетантство. Так же, иногда приложение само запускает цикл на 30 минут. Вопрос, что с вами не так. Не рекомендую. Не тратьте время и нервы. Это очень сильно раздражает и выводит из себя.хотите стать нервным, вперед!

title: No longer: My favorite app since childhood
body:
I have used this app for roughly 10 years. Forest is part of my life now.

Update 2025:
This app used to be so simple and graphically pleasing. Work flow was straightforward: open app, plant, view your forest. 

But now, it expanded and developed AI assisted features, meditations, events, extra plant purchases.  I used it because it is pleasing and it limits distractions. 

There are SO MANY DISTRACTIONS that it feels a burden to use. 

The graphic design is also INCONSISTENT and even UGLY. We don’t need so many new trees updates if their qualities are low. The new plants seem to be made by AI. What has happened to the company?

I was a loyal user for so many years. I loved the app for its simplicity and beautiful design. But not anymore. I am writing this long review for the hope that things can be changed.

title: Mis-taps & a Hassle to Exit + No Shortcut Support
body:
Originally, after planting a tree, the Rest button was the most prominent at the bottom, making it simple to end the session, and back to main screen. Now Forest has replaced this with its Rest & Breathing Timer, since that button is still the most prominent one on the screen, it’s way too easy to mis-tap by accident. To make it even more frustrating, you have to long-press just to exit the Rest & Breathing Timer once you’ve mis-tapped it, which is such a counterintuitive, annoying design.

What’s more, I really dislike that Forest requires you to open the app directly for all actions. I much prefer launching focus timers via Shortcuts, as it lets me start a session without any distractions. If Forest won’t add support for Shortcuts for a seamless start, it should at the very least polish the basic in-app experience—but this forced update only ruins it with poor design choices.

title: Features I PAID for were removed
body:
I’m really upset because about two months after I paid to download this app, multiple core features were removed and are now locked behind a monthly subscription.

I have no issue with the app introducing a subscription for additional features. The problem is that I specifically paid for this app with the understanding that these features were included. Removing functionality that paying users already purchased feels lazy and scummy, especially when the alternative would be to simply add new premium features instead.

Some features that were removed include:
	•	The ability to choose which apps are blocked during a focus period
	•	Viewing detailed focus stats (such as which days and times you focus most)
	•	Creating and editing custom tags to label and group study sessions

On top of this, ads were added, and the app constantly pushes the subscription.

I genuinely enjoyed this app and found it helpful, but it has now become a source of frustration. All I’m asking is that the features I paid for be returned, and that subscriptions enhance the experience for subscribers rather than restrict it for everyone else.

	•	Monday is displayed as Friday
	•	Similarly, the months are reversed:
	•	Month 1 is shown as 12
	•	Month 2 is shown as 11, and so on.

It seems that the calendar/time indexing is inverted, which causes incorrect labeling of days and months.

I would appreciate it if you could look into this issue and fix the reversed sequence.

author: Rosie Likeli

title: This Changes Everything
body:
As someone who has always struggled with attention for repetitive or boring work tasks (paperwork, documentation, etc.) This has been a godsend. I was racking up way too much work time watching YT Shorts or TikTok, not because I wanted to, but because I’d get sucked into the vortex anytime I picked up my phone.

Well no more! I’ve enabled Deep Focus and locked out virtually every app that could distract me, and having something that depends on me staying focused completely reshaped my relationship with these tasks. 

I now WANT to spend time on them so I can keep growing trees and earning coins. I know gamification doesn’t work for a lot of people, but as a life-long millennial gamer, it has become an essential feature of any app I purchase. It keeps enabling me to stick to things I normally would’ve given up on in a few days (just passed one year of daily German lessons via Duolingo and now Busuu). If gamification works for you too, then just stop reading and buy the app already! 

The reason I dinged a star is due to how many microtransactions the app contains. I get it, it’s one of the only profitable ways to sustain an app company, but it feels like it’s nudging you to spend or buy on every page of the app except for study time. Even then, it’ll remind you how you could be getting 3x the coins if you sign up for Plus. Keep in mind, you have to pay $4 to use this app, making it a premium purchase. I get plastering that stuff everywhere when you offer a free membership option, but that’s not the case here. If the company is struggling to make ends meet, then start charging more, but whatever you do, lighten up on the gacha mechanics. Not saying they need to go, just that they shouldn’t be up in my face on every window.

title: Fantastic way to gamify focusing
body: I’ve used this app for years now, and it’s the best one I’ve used to help me stay focused and off my phone. I have ADHD, so being able to turn boring tasks into little games really helps a lot, and this app is perfect for that. title: Thanks!!!
body:
I’ve tried several apps to help me stay focused while studying, but Forest is the only one that truly transformed how I learn. As someone who used to struggle with attention and often felt frustrated for not “giving my all,” Forest helped me turn my perfectionism into a healthy motivation.

The ability to “plant trees” that grow based on how long I stay focused pushes me to beat my own record every day, and that has boosted my productivity like nothing else. Now I can maintain long study sessions (7 to 8 hours or more in a day) with steady focus that used to feel impossible.

Plus, seeing my progress visually reflected in a growing forest gives me a real, tangible sense of achievement. Forest has helped me not only study faster but also process and digest information better, moving past the anxiety of immediate perfection to focus on steady progress.

For anyone struggling with concentration or motivation, Forest isn’t just an app—it’s a companion that helps you reprogram your mind and build habits that actually work.

Suggestions: I would love to see a widget for iPhone standby mode to make tracking even easier. Also, giving users more opportunities to earn or buy trees would be awesome—because who wouldn’t want a bigger, greener forest?

title: I feel like I can’t complain about the App’s actual problems bc the basic concept is so effective
body:
I own two physical pomodoro timers. They were more expensive than this app and this app is way more effective. I really thought it wouldn’t work after I’ve tried everything to help my screen time problem only to weasel around them and eventually go back to my old ways. This app is amazing because it actually:
1- locks you out of distracting apps
2- guilt trips you if you try to weasel around it in a way that’s more effective than other guilt trip methods (think Duolingo’s reminders). If you give up, your plants die. And I don’t want my plants to die :(
3- you get an awesome visual representation of how long you’ve focused in a day unlike conventional pomodoro timers, which is really motivating
However, the pricing of the plants and the events leave something to be desired.
I don’t mind how long it takes to accumulate coins, it fits right in with the app’s “you reap what you sow, so work hard” ethos.
However, there’s so many missed opportunities for the game-like nature of the app. 
For starters there’s so many awesome limited-time plants you just can’t get if you join the app now because they’re not made available in the time crystal shop. And the plants that are in the time crystal shop are mostly seasonal holiday-themed decorations I have no interest in. So there’s this whole in-game currency that’s useless to me, and it could so easily become useful to me if the developers put more limited-time plants in the time crystal shop
There are also accomplishments/awards for focusing x number of hours that will gift you x number of coins for completing them. I think there should be more of these accomplishments because after a certain point you complete them all and it takes some of the freshness out of the game for people who have been playing longer. I think some new accomplishments could be awards for completing sets of plants. For example, in the shop there are plants that can be categorized together like fruit trees, plants indigenous to Africa and Asia, and tropical plants. If collecting all the plants in these groups came with an achievement and coin reward, it could be motivating for long-time players to collect more plants.
I like the monthly challenge, I think that’s great and they should never take it out.

title: Dislike the “Pay-to-Play”
body: The concept behind these focus apps is to hijack our brain’s reward systems to be productive rather than distracting. You get dopamine from focusing and getting a tree planted. But when the “reward” (planting a tree, unlocking trees, etc) becomes the goal in itself, then the app becomes a distraction in itself.  The first time I stopped using this app, I stopped because I had become obsessed with growing a beautiful forest. I notice there’s a lot of “pay-to-play” that takes advantage of this misdirected reward system, where you can pay to get more coins or diamonds to get more rewards. It would be good if these options were not so visible on the app and could be turned off and only accessible in the settings. This takes advantage of our brain’s reward systems for the developers’ profit rather than helping us direct it towards becoming productive.

title: Great for one-time purchase
body:
I’ve had this app since 2017 and used it on and off through college and my working life. It’s one of the best apps on my phone, and I don’t regret paying for it back then. 

Pros: the tree variety is great, especially within the past year with the new monthly challenge plant varieties. The ambient sounds are good. The graphs are great if you use tags and unobtrusive if you don’t. It has a lot of small quality of life features that are really great, like the ability to keep the screen on so you can see the timer running, the ability to run a whitelist of apps in case you need to consult something on your phone quickly without your plant dying, and the fact that you can set the app to keep counting time length. The achievement system helps newbies quickly diversify tree species available to them. The new daily challenges award a small amount of the paid currency so with patience you can unlock previous time limited trees. It’s also significantly spread up collecting gold, which is nice for a casual like me. Most of the tree species have stages of growth depending on how long you plant them, so even with only a few trees to start with you can get some visual interest going. I like planting a variety of the more realistic trees so my little monthly forest is biodiverse, but I appreciate there’s also weird and whimsical trees. There really is a tree or two for everyone.

Cons: The company behind this app has decided to monetize it more, in the form of a paid subscription model instead of a one-time purchase. I understand why they’re doing this, and I think it’s going to be good for the app, but on principle I won’t be using it as I dislike subscription models for productivity apps. Hopefully the free version won’t be too inaccessible. Also, the daily challenge prize collection glitches sometimes, and it’s not actually clear on the screen where to tap to collect it and move on.

Wishlist: Like another commenter, I’d really like the ability to set a little chime when a planting is done that makes it through silent mode. I always have my phone on silent though so maybe this is on me! Other than that, some more water based plants would be nice. I’d love the ability to put a little pond on my forest. The app also has some integration with the Apple Watch but I’d also love something like a quick replant button on the watch that starts the same tree and timer combo again.

title: Too many bugs in the forest
body:
I use this app to track the time I spend on tasks for school. I love the added challenges feature because it motivates me to spend more time on what I need to do. A scroll function to plant the trees would be desired and a pomodoro type function to track breaks too would be perfect. 

The app is a great idea but the usability and especially the constant bugs need an improvement. 

I’ve used forest since 2020 and it has been really interesting to see what times of the day I’m most productive and what I spend the most time on. 
However, within these past few months the app has consistently been crashing. It forces my iPad to restart. 
At times it removes my progress/I lose the coins I earned. Reopening the app usually fixes it, but this is now a glaring concern and makes me lose faith in the system. 

✅ I like that it tracks my time. 
✅ I like all the trees designs I can un clock with coins. It helps with motivation.
✅ The new monthly challenges are amazing! 

❌ Many glitches and bugs that make me worried about the app saving my progress. 
❌ Missing the ability to set the timer using the pomodoro method of taking a small break between sessions max
❌ Could improve the usability of the menu to be clearer, especially with regards to the store.

title: Great app!
body:
Forest has been great so far! I’ve literally completed hours worth of cleaning this week. I love the little trees and being able to plant with my friend. I also love the count up timer as I hate normal timer focus options that force me to break focus but this is great!

I have some issues with the allow list (customizable lists of apps you’re allowed to use while focusing). The main thing is my app freezes whenever I try to add anything from the education section or search for particular apps. That’s my only sincere problem with the app though. 

The following are just some possible suggestions I’ve thought of:
I would appreciate the ability to change allow lists and/or task tags partway through a session. 
A pause/break option (with allow list still functioning) because sometimes things do come up or maybe you get tired
Honestly that’s it. I really like this app so far though

title: So much potential
body: I usually never write app reviews but I really wanted to give my feedback on this one! I love this app but it would be so much more fun and fulfilling to use if it had a feature that allowed you to visualize the focus time you give to certain categories. For me, I use a specific type of tree for each project im working on,etc. so that when I look at my garden I can kind of visualize where my energy is going. It would be amazing if the app incorporated one of those matching puzzle type of game elements to grow a larger tree by combining trees of a certain type. I think it would be really fun to be able to earn 3 small trees then combine those into a bigger tree, then earn 3 of those and make an even bigger tree, you get the idea. It would be more visually appealing to see the trees with more drastic size differences too. Also i think there’s a nice metaphorical reminder in there that the plant you water most will grow the tallest. Please consider adding these features !

title: Pursuing a graduate degree with this app…
body: I never leave comments but I’m so extremely grateful for this app, I just have to share. I have ADHD-like tendencies (not diagnosed), and pursuing a graduate degree seemed like a big jump. Thanks to this app, the amount of time that I can focus increased from 15 minutes at a time to one hour! I added a widget to my Home Screen that shows my forest everyday, as well as how many minutes I’ve studied. It’s a huge motivation to sit down and focus for even just a short time everyday to see some trees on the Home Screen page. I feel proud at the end of the day/week/month looking back at my lush forest. Also, thank you also for adding the challenges! I usually finish them pretty quickly but they help me to start my month off right, and I can ride the momentum even after I’ve completed the challenge. I use the app in conjunction with the finch app, and also study with me videos on YouTube. :)

title: Upset with new changes
body:
I’ve been a long time user of the app forest for around 4 years now when I bought the app. I feel as if the core of the app really does improve focus through creating good habits. However when I was made aware of the paid subscription update as well as the addition of AI I was very upset. I believe there are 4 big problems with these changes. 1). AI is bad for the environment and and for an app that prides itself on its environmental impacts it seems like implementing ai is just a way to be “trendy” and doesn’t follow the apps core values. On the website forest states “At Forest, we believe that better selves build a better world.” Building a better world does not include implementing AI when it is unnecessary and unhelpful. 2). Forest is a very simple app that works to break your phone addiction so adding all these bits and bobs are not helpful/useful and most of the time annoying. 3). Forest is already very buggy. For being around for years I feel as if there are big bugs that should be worked on instead of rolling out new features that no one asked for or wanted. 4). My final complaint is that I already spent the money to buy the app and asking its users to now pay for a subscription model is just another money grab. If I am asked to buy the subscription I will be switching to another app. 
Once again forest used to be my favorite focus app but now seeing the changes coming I fear I may need to choose another option that values its users.

title: An OK pomodoro app with poor Apple Watch support
body:
Update 12/2024: the app has become very unstable, with extremely long loading times, frequent crashes, and the inability to start sessions. 

Some frustrating bugs remain unfixed. One is example is that if you start a session with deep focus enabled, and immediately cancel it, your apps will still be blocked.

Would be nice after a year of planting trees to be able to zoom in on the forest instead of viewing at an extreme distance.

The most frustrating aspect of Forest is the limited Apple Watch support. If users could start focus sessions without using their phones, they would look at their phones less. Which is the whole point of using the app. But that feature isn’t available. Instead, all you can do is look at your forest.

Other annoyances are some questionable UI choices, like the annoying pop up on the view Forest screen that can’t be turned off. 

Balanced against this is the clever tree planting system which gives users a stake in completing through on their focus sessions. Also valuable are the statistics, competitions, and ability to acquire more flora through sweat equity. These features make Forest one of the best pomodor apps. It’s just unfortunate to miss on something as basic and useful as Apple Watch support.

title: Love the Focus Challenge! Keep it!
body:
I’m not sure I’ve written a review for an app but I feel passionately enough to write this. 
First I’ve been a forest user for 7 years now. I’ve only really started relying on it in the past 2 years but I’ve always enjoyed how the app functions. The UI is easy to navigate, it’s easy to designate apps that won’t be turned off. Getting coins for each focus session to unlock new trees is always a treat. And it’s really fun to do longer sessions to grow bigger trees/plants! 

But I think that this focus challenge mode will be a game changer for me. It’s enticing me to want to use the app every single day even when I may not need to focus. I love that it gives you crystals if you do a particularly hard challenge, which are otherwise locked behind a paywall. And I love that the daily challenges change and are building toward a reward at the end of the month! What a GREAT ADDITION! 
Please, keep it! DON’T change ANYTHING, particularly the crystals cause that’s just corporate scumminess. We’re only getting five and I’m SO OKAY with that. 
But in general, keep the challenges, it inspires attention to what you’re planting and can entice the user to get new trees. GREAT ADDITION again, continue doing great things!

title: Best Productivity App
body: I started using this app in high school and I am now in law school. It truly helps keep you focused. I am motivated by not killing my tree and to continue planting so I can get coins to buy more trees. I love how you can plant real trees. I really like the focus challenge they are currently doing; I like having a different way to get a new species and it provides an outside motivation to get your work done. I love how in December it turns to a winter theme, but you do have the option to turn that off. I like being able to choose between stopwatch and timer because sometimes I don’t know how long I want to work for but I don’t want to kill my tree if I need to work for less than I set the timer for. I also think it is great you can customize your allow list. I also love being able to look at your forest as days, weeks, months, or years. It is interesting going back to see what I was focusing on, what months I focus the most, and even what years I was most focused. I have never had a problem with this app! I think it would be cool if different seasons and holidays get decorations like December does. For example, spider webs and bats for October or sparkles and hearts for Valentine’s Day. I also would love more species to buy or win through future focus challenges. I wonder if you could add a pomodoro timer to the app so you can have scheduled breaks.

title: Data Wipe and Lack of Communication
body:
I’ve loved and used Forest for a couple of years and it was at the center of my daily productivity routines. It was truly one of the only productivity apps I’ve ever had sustained success with. It was a gentle motivation that gave great insights on what I was spending my focused time on. I used it so much that it was right beside my texting and emailing apps in my phone’s app dock!

However, like many other users, my account’s historical data was wiped with a previous update. With the most recent update(s), Forest has stickied a note in the Support section of the App saying how to re-integrate your data to your account. Although it has worked for many users, this has not worked for me at all. Talking with other Forest users online has shown me that I’m not the only one still encountering this.

Last Thursday, when the account data first went missing for me, I sent in-app support messages to try to get more information (only to actually find that information elsewhere on Reddit by other users). On Monday, those messages still hadn’t been marked as “seen”, so I sent an email to the support address listed on their website. On Tuesday, I finally received a message in the app asking me what email was associated with my account (which makes me wonder if my data is irretrievable since I use my Apple ID and an Apple-assigned private relay email), but after I replied I still haven’t heard anything from Forest.

It has been a full week now since I’ve been dealing with this issue, and it has been discouraging to have next to nothing customer support on the matter. At the time the data was wiped, I even had an active “Sunshine Elixir” paid subscription (as a way of showing support to the developers of an app that I used so frequently), but that active paid feature has obviously been unusable and wasteful at this point (with no indications of it being compensated in any way due to this outage).

I’m at my wit’s end with trying to get any sort of indication of if my data can even be restored at this point, and (if it can be restored) a vague timeline or any acknowledgment that it is even still being looked into. I’m really asking for the bare minimum here but I’m still getting radio silence. A little over a week ago, I would have had nothing bad to say about this app, but now I wouldn’t recommend it at all.

title: The most effective app I’ve ever used.
body:
I’ve been using Forest for probably eight years or so. It might be the only app I’ve ever used consistently and that actually has a positive impact. The way it’s designed to incentivize productivity with all the cool plant species and “punish” us for not following through with a dead tree is incredibly effective. This is a fantastic app for a person with ADHD, or someone just looking to disconnect more intentionally. It’s not got enough going on to occupy much of your time on its own and somehow, I absolutely NEVER want to have a dead tree. It’s quite shocking even all these years later that this still works at keeping me off my phone, even now that you can allow all sorts of apps to be used simultaneously, whereas before you couldn’t leave the screen at all without killing your tree. 

The plant and tree species are very aesthetically appealing, and being able to visually see progress and the novelty of working towards earning new tree species is exactly what I need as an ADHD user. 

I am just a regular schmuck, but I hope you believe me when I say this app changed my life. I recommend it to anyone who ever mentions overusing their phone. I mention it to anyone who will listen. 

And to the developers: thank you so much for this creation. Truly, this has gotten me so much further in life than I could have done on my own. Please never change anything about this app, ESPECIALLY the aesthetic and ACTUAL tree species. I was fortunate enough to try that new beta a year or two ago and was terrified that the original Forest would leave. I left an emotional response over why nothing needed to change and I’m so happy to see that the original Forest is still going strong and new species get added regularly. The app is flawless. Perfect amount of features.

I would love to see a “to-do” style app from these developers. I 100% do not think Forest should have any such added capabilities, but I have faith that these developers are very well versed in the aesthetic experience (very important), useful features with just the right amount of bells and whistles, and a niche functionality that is rare to find elsewhere.

This app is worth it. Moreso than any app I know.

title: Great on Phone, Better with Apple Watch
body:
I’ve been using the Forest app on my phone, and while it works well for keeping me focused, I believe it could be significantly improved by adding a timer feature to the Apple Watch. The whole point of the Pomodoro technique is to minimize distractions, and having to rely on my phone somewhat defeats this purpose.

If Forest had a timer on the Apple Watch that synced with the trees I plant in the app, it would be amazing. This way, I could easily keep track of my focused work periods without the temptation of checking my phone. The convenience of glancing at my wrist to see the countdown would enhance my productivity and help me stay on task more effectively.

Forest is already a great app for boosting focus and productivity, but an Apple Watch integration would make it even better.

title: Apple Watch App
body:
I really liked this phone app in the beginning and it helped me focus with my ADHD, but it requires you to keep going back to your phone to set new timers, which feels against the purpose of the app. There is a 3 hour time limit, which is TOO SHORT. I can focus and work on something for 4-6 hours easily, especially at my job. It would be great if it encouraged you to just leave your phone alone entirely instead of forcing you to come back once every 1, 2, or 3 hours. 
Furthermore, the Apple Watch app is basically a nothingburger. All you can do is watch your forest grow, NOT set timers from the watch! I would FAR prefer being able to set the timers from my watch so I don't have to go to my phone,  but nope... can't do that. 

I feel, from a developer's POV, that this app is trying to balance people relying on it and using it constantly so they make money with also trying to be a focus app, and frankly, those two things can't easily co-exist. 

To fix this app from a user-experience POV, having an option for up to 5 hours would be great, and having a functional Watch app would be great. I'd be far more likely to want to buy exclusive trees if I had a more positive experience, because frankly, I stopped using the app after 2 weeks out of frustration, which was worsened when I found out I couldn't set timers from my watch.

title: Beautiful app that should be free given it’s model
body:
First off…. Please stop giving me popups with a “free” offer to “buy” one of your other paid apps.  It is annoying and is turning me off to your brand.  I would expect for a paid app I wouldn’t be bombarded with the same annoying messages as free apps.

There is not a good variety of trees unlocked to me at the get go.  Further, when I filter by “unlocked” trees, most of the trees cost coins and are not unlocked.  What gives?  The trees are also pretty pricey - understanding the motivation is for you to focus to get more coins to get those pricey trees.   But, you can “cheat” the system and buy coins with actual money.  If an app is going to be so micro transaction focused, the app should be free from the get go.

Honestly, I’m going to request as refund from Apple.  This app should be free or modeled differently.

title: Annoying Micro Transactions
body:
This app has the audacity to ask you to pay for little virtual tree skins. It’s about time we start punishing companies that fill their (paid) app with micro transaction extortions.

Review update: see the developer’s response to my rating. They act like we are fools that don’t understand the concept of micro transactions. Yes, you can “earn” the trees by spending hundreds of hours to do so. That’s fine. Unlocking the trees should be a goal of the gamified system. A micro transaction is where developers offer a short cut that capitalizes on customer’s frustration or impatience. It should have no place in a paid app.

title: Awesome app, few improvements needed
body:
This is exactly what I was looking for, it helps so I don’t get distracted when I’m reading articles or watching movies. Also the fact that it’s a one time payment is what I like, I absolutely hate subscriptions. The in app purchases are completely for extra stuff and doesn’t hinder the functionality. Kudos to the developers for that. There are 2 things that I would like to suggest however. -I use this as a timer since I take alloted breaks at work, and it doesn’t really act as an alarm if I doze off. I think that should be an option for the few of us that don’t want to set the phone timer on top of it -Using with the Dynamic Island is cool, but the constant countdown can be a distraction when you’re reading an article. I would suggest doing something like the native iOS countdown with the Dynamic Island or at least just doing the minutes instead of seconds.

**for some reason it won’t block Reddit. I’ve double checked all my allowances on the app and iOS.

title: Great Discipline
body:
I looooove this app! I paid for premium, which was a ONE TIME purchase, and I think it is so worth it. (And I’m a person who doesn’t do in-app purchases) I am able to gain control back over my studies and gain the discipline I need to do my work with minimal distractions. Plus the trees are very cute!

I also love being able to choose which apps I can still access, because there are times I do need to access either my calendar, or another app I use for school. Plus I can keep my Spotify or Youtube ambience going while I study!

I don’t write reviews, like ever, but I am serious when I say this app has worked for me, especially with things like my phone being my biggest distraction. This is truly one of the few apps I recommend people get, and I’m constantly telling friends or classmates about it, basically advertising for them for free 🤣

title: Would love to see a redesign!
body:
I have recently come back to this app after a few years away. I appreciate being able to gameify the simple goal of NOT picking up my phone, so I‘m not really a full featured user or terribly interested in the tracking of my different habits over time. But I like plants.

As an artist and designer, I see missed opportunities for the visual layout of the app. The appeal to me is in seeing my forest grow and more lush… but I have to tap in and out of forest view to appreciate that reward, which feels clunky and unintuitive. The designs of the plants, as well as the way they look in aggregate could use some love from an illustrator. There are so many people making incredible botanical art, and this app feels stuck in a more blatantly techy past.

title: Started out good, seems to get slower
body:
Hello, I’ve used Forest for many years at this point. I remember when I initially joined, bushes were still for just small increments of time. I like a lot of the features that have come around, stopwatch mode, toggling deep focus, integration with screentime, etc. But it feels like the app has just slowed down. It takes so long to react to touch input, particularly when selecting a tree species. I just want the time to be faster to create a smoother experience. And I do actually miss the smaller bushes being for smaller increments of time only. It provided some variation and when looking at a forest, told me if I had done a lot of small focus sessions or fewer and longer ones. It was rewarding for 2 different skills. A feature I would love to see is a return of the short timed bushes, and the addition of some species for longer times only - sequoias come to mind. Thanks for all the work you’ve put into this app.

2024 updates:
Hello! I still like this app. Still seeing some slow reactions when tapping buttons or loading information like the forest timeline and today’s forest, but still fast enough to be acceptable. 

Feature I would love to see: being able to adjust the app allow list from the planting settings - I have a few that I use throughout the day and it would be wonderful to just save a favorite tree with the app allow list, instead of switching them in the settings.

title: Loving it so far!
body: This is the first “gamified” focus/timer app I’ve tried and I have to say, I’m loving it! I’ve been using it for 2 days, and the interest in growing my little forest is giving me enough motivation to open it each time I sit down to work. It keeps me from mindlessly scrolling on my phone as a work avoidance strategy (work avoidance is a skill I’ve become quite adept at lol). I’ve used the countdown timer to pay better attention to how long certain tasks take me (like showering, getting ready, etc), and I love that it tracks the times so you can refer back to them and improve your time awareness when planning out how long something will take in the future. I’ve used it to keep me from being distracted by my phone during workouts, even play time with my kids! I’m excited to collect enough leaves to buy a new tree species. Definitely a fun tool to keep in your adhd toolbox!

author: BigForestFan

title: Best decision of my senior year
body:
Forest has been an absolute game-changer for me during my senior year. As someone easily distracted, this app has revolutionized the way I approach my studies. With its ingenious focus mechanism, I've experienced a significant reduction in my screen time, allowing me to channel my energy towards tasks that truly matter.

The delightful aspect of this app is the visual representation of my focus time through the growth of a virtual tree, providing a tangible sense of accomplishment as I witness my progress. Not only has this helped me stay focused, but it has also instilled a sense of responsibility and commitment to my academic goals.

I highly recommend Forest to anyone looking to enhance their focus, reduce screen time, and ultimately achieve their academic goals. It's a must-have for students striving for excellence and seeking to make the most out of their educational journey. Five stars without a doubt!

title: Editing the allowed app list is PAIN
body: They break down the apps into so many categories with no search feature, and the way they categorize the apps is arbitrary, so if you’re a normal human being with a lot of apps installed, you’ll have to go through each category to locate the specific apps that you want it to be allowed during the use of Forest. More than that, Forest will crash and become unresponsive when I try to expand the category that has many apps in it. To be clear, I made sure Forest is up-to-date and it’s running on my iPhone 12 pro, so I don’t see the reason of any app being unresponsive except the optimization of the app itself is bad. I have to go back and forth and expand one category at a time to just finish editing one list. It ended up wasting me more time rather than doing the actual work that I should be focusing on. Even now I haven’t finished editing the list because the category “Other” couldn’t be expanded. I guess they just stuffed all the apps they don’t know how to categorize into that one category. I would much prefer they just don’t categorize the apps and simply add a search bar.

title: Simple, effective, impactful
body:
I’ve been using Forest since 2018. I first got it to help me stay off my phone in my daily life. 

Then, it became absolutely essential when I went back to school. I went through undergrad using Forest almost daily to help me focus on reading and doing homework. Now, I’m pursuing a PhD and I use it for several hours a day, every day. I credit it with increasing my stamina for reading difficult texts by breaking them down into small, manageable units of time. 

The most valuable aspect of Forest is seeing my time add up in the form of cute plants in my “forest.” It’s easy to get to the end of a day & wonder “Did I even accomplish anything today?” With Forest, I can look at my app and track the time I’ve spent in deep focus. It’s motivating and rewarding. 

The app is simple, works great, and has made a huge impact on the way I read and study. I recommend it constantly!

title: Best Autism/ADHD Focus Environmentally Conscious App
body: I cannot rate and recommend this app enough! I’m a psychology student who recently got diagnosed with ADHD and Autism. This diagnosis, plus the Forest app has given me my first set of straight A’s. I’m now actually believing I can get into grad school, move to Scotland, have a family, and live my dreams more than ever. This app has encouraged me so much. Plus it has my favorite tree ever (which I happily tested as) Wisteria 💜🍃🌳. I never write reviews but this app is amazing. It also functions like apps used to. Just buying up front instead of a tedious subscription. Please don’t change anything in that regard. The app does have options to pay to get “grow points”, but it’s not popping up in everyone’s face. It’s an app that just helps you focus and gives you motivation. Plus you get to actually plant real trees and feel more motivated to make an impact environmentally. Thank you so much Forest!

title: Missing key features that would make a 5-Star app!
body: I’m an ADHDer and daily Forest user - the App has helped me to stay on track and check things off my to-do list (or as us ADHDers call our “wall of awful”). However, there are times I need to focus more than three hours and that three-hour limit is extremely annoying!!! I have unhealthy addictive habits that I’m trying to break - I started by restricting these activities to once very two hours and each week I increased the interval by 15 min; now I’m doing good at once every three hours but I can’t make progress without being able to set a longer interval. I’d also love to have more control over the visual design of my Forest. Specifically, I want to move things around and enter new lands that represent my progress with longer intervals. Because these features are missing, I’m now looking for a new app that offers more customization. I’d absolutely return to Forest if the developers offered a meaningful update - I’d even pay good money for the elements I’ve described here!

I am still a huge fan of this app and continue using it, but I used to use it far more often before the Screen Time/allow list update. title: I love the Forest app!

I love that I can pick a beautiful plant to watch grow while I am working that I can redeem coins to plant a real tree. One my favorite features of the app are the personality tests that are sometimes posted in the news section. They are so sweet and high-quality, such a welcome break from the scholarly work. I am so happy I purchased the Forest app and am proud to recommend it to everyone! I never write reviews, but Forest is so deserving of one. THANK YOU Forest team for this wonderful and beautiful app and for staying by my side while I get my PhD!

title: The whole point of the app is lost due to...
body:
The whole point of the app is lost due to two things. First is the top score rank and the second is the ability to purchase new trees by coins. 

So users are just planting 24/7, usefull app (to improve productivity) becomes a silly game, to gain coins and buy trees, sound libraries and become top-xx in global rank or whatever. 

 The main and the best point of the app is totally lost. People getting even more out of focus, by playing it, instead of using it properly as a solution to become more effecient, more productivity, focus, etc... 

Imho developers need to find a solution for it. To continue monetize it, but in proper way. You can provide coins, for daily usage. Like daily claiming you coin bonus. Not for count of trees you plant. And just remove this totally disappointing top-xx ranks. 

 Of course people can't be focused on important tasks 24/7 and be in top-10/50/100. Cmon guys. Where is the logic? Think about the proper ways to monetize the app, don't turn it to silly game.

title: Could be more engaging, needs interface work.
body:
The app is functional and pleasant to look at, but a frustrating interface and focus on in-app purchases will draw you to look at other options.

Pros: 
Visually nice to look at
Menus navigate quickly
Music white noise is pleasant

Cons:
New “trees” cost far too much (or the rewards are too low).
For a paid app focuses too much on ads and selling premium “trees”
Frustrating interface to plant new trees.
White noise does not start by default as also ends with the timer.
Keeps draining battery in the background if not force quit.

I have had this app for two months now and still only have the default trees plus a couple free ones that were seasonal. Currency needs to be tripled for sessions or the cost of new trees brought way down to increase engagement. Alternately give out the “triple-reward” boost potions for reaching certain productivity milestones. Planting always the same trees on a grid is not engaging because of this, and makes me want to see what other apps can improve my productivity by keeping me interested. I also shouldn’t have to look at an ad for other products on my main interface at all times, looking at you “TinyTan.”

After a tree is planted the app will continue to reward currency, but it shuts off the white noise which then Distracts me from my work if I’m in a good flow. I understand the 25/5 minute nature and I should take breaks, but give me the option to switch automatic shut off.

After my tree is grown I should be able to directly plant my next tree. Instead what happens is clicking on the tree icon takes me to a menu. I have to navigate back to the previous screen each time using the upper left arrow icon then press plant for the next round of productivity. This is not intuitive and disrupts workflow.

Allow for white noise to start with a new tree being planted as an option in the menu, I shouldn’t have to do three clicks for each tree session (navigate back to plant menu, click plant, click headphone icon for white noise). This should all be seamless with one click.

Finally when I installed on my new iPhone 14 pro, Forest accounted for 30% of my battery drain in the background while not even playing music or growing a tree. This seems to be a common problem from looking online. I changed the settings on my phone and force quit the app when not directly using it, which has made the app drain less.

title: Encouraging app block
body:
Nothing much happens when you fail to stay off your device. A tree dies, you lose what you’ve worked for up until now, but nothing else. 

Yet it’s still so elegantly effective at keeping me on task when I needed it the most, while not being too restrictive in case of an emergency. 

Especially as forest has created an allow list, it has really helped me to stay on task. The trees are really cute. Watching them grow is very rewarding. 

The only complaint I have is it being incompatible with pomodoro 25work/5min breaks and forces you to focus for 2 hours at a time should you want late-stage trees, which doesn’t work for me sometimes. 

But overall it’s a very nicely made app. I love it.

title: Pay to focus
body:
My experience of this app is that the limited variety of plants available at the start is unappealing and the cost of coins for purchasing new trees is too high. Having to begin with Christmas trees, coral, bushes,  and seals is very confusing to me, and I would much rather preferred aspens, white pines, maples, etc. This poor variety makes you want to buy more plants right way but to do so you need coins of course. This results in my having to constantly pick up my phone and reset the focus for every activity during my day in order to accumulate enough coins to actually purchase the trees to plant a forest with and variety or just trees. This is both tedious and distracting in and of itself which is ironic given the apps purpose. This process can be sped it up by purchasing elixirs from the store of course. maybe I’m too frugal, but I have an adverse reaction to paying for an app, and then being nickel and dimed to make the app more functional and appealing and the lack of variety to promote pay to focus is off turning. 
Lastly, the daily tiles don’t give one a sense of a Forest, more a wooded lot. I suggest having a visual of the daily tiles connected to one another to show an larger dicpiction of one’s Forest that has grown over time, which would be satisfying.

title: Wish it was compatible with pomodoro!
body: This is a great app, and I’ve been using it for years now, but I’m really disappointed that it isn’t compatible with the pomodoro technique! Per that technique, I only study for 25min at a time but of course do multiple 25min sessions in a day. Unfortunately, this app doesn’t have a mode that works with the pomodoro method; I can’t plant one tree and have it grow due to cumulative time for one day, I can only plant multiple sprouts of trees that never grow. It’s disheartening to not be able to grow big, final form trees just because I use a more paced studying technique when the whole point of the app is to stay focused so you have the reward of looking at your beautiful forest. If they were to add a pomodoro mode that either lets you plant final form trees for every 25min OR lets you plant one tree and have your cumulative time for the day grow it, then I’d give this app 5 stars!

It’s spamming the customer to spend more money, which is annoying and distracting, and I’d say antithetical to an app whose sole purpose is to help increase focus.

title: The app everyone needs
body: Let me start this off with a statement everyone can agree with — I never want to spend money on apps. But Forest is the best app I’ve ever used and I’ve never regretted spending that $2 for a second. I am a student with horrible attention problems and struggles with staying motivated, and this app manages to solve it all. I’ve been using it since 2018 and I’m only reviewing it now to say that the newest update brings this app to a whole new level. With the app allow list using apple’s screen time feature it solves every single little problem I had with the app (except for the plant together feature, it lags a bit when planting with users across platforms, if a developer is reading this please fix it!). I’ve referred so many friends to forest and it’s helped them so much as well, it gives us an incentive to study, to be productive, get off our phone, and then makes it so easy to do so. If you need help staying focused, this app is the app for you. And you can help plant real physical trees!! No other app gives you the chance to save your brain and the planet. I really do love this app & I can’t recommend it enough.

title: ADHD user loves it
body:
Wow, I actually love this app. I rarely write reviews but this is important info to get out. I’ve noticed with my ADHD I get very bored very easily and if I don’t have something that keeps me accountable, I will simply forget what I was just doing and start playing on my phone. With this app, I leave the screen open with the timer counting down and my task of “work” or “homework” facing me so when I get the urge, it’s a reminder of what I SHOULD be doing. I love how the app isn’t busy so when you take your 5 min break it’s super easy to just set up another timer and not get lost in something else. 
This app rocks, I recommend it to anyone and everyone especially those of us that suffer from constant distraction that inevitably lead us to picking up our devices to “cure” boredom. 
Thanks Forest team, I told my therapist all about you!!!

title: Tangible for ADHD
body:
I am someone who struggles tremendously with studying due to my ADHD. Part of this is because setting restrictions on time and trying to force an intangible structure on myself doesn’t work. I can “say” I’ll follow a schedule to do my homework, but there’s nothing stopping me from straying from that schedule only I have a stake in, so I don’t maintain it. 
This app gives me a time limit that has a tangible consequence for breaking, because the flower or shrub (or TinyTan BTS member) I’m growing will die if I break the rules of the app, and will remain on my forest record forever. I don’t want that to happen, so I follow the rules and do what I set out to do originally. 
However, as is the case for many people who are neurodivergent, setting habits is almost impossible, because one missed step or one missed day ruins the entire process. So opening this app and turning it on to study is a choice you have to actively make every day, and that’s difficult. I choose to because I like the act of having a little forest I don’t have to maintain in real life, but also because I know I feel worse if I don’t study or don’t get everything done when I could have, but it took me 2 years to get to this point of knowing the choice to open this app and use it is worth it. 
It’s so hard to do things of my own volition, but this app helps. It’s not perfect, but it’s better than nothing at all, so I think it’s worth the download.

title: User of 4 years. Used to be solid, now super buggy.
body:
Don’t get me wrong. I love this app and consistently use it. But I’m embarrassed to love it, because it’s slowly getting worse. 

This app crashes all the time. In some ways the crashes are very predictable. For instance, anytime I’m done with growing a plant and try to return to the Home Screen, it crashes. Or anytime I’m viewing my plot for the year and try to view a plot for a year from before I had the account, it crashes. 

The developers for this app don’t seem to really handle errors. I don’t ever receive errors in the app - it just full on crashes. Which is super off-putting. 

To make matters worse, the built in support is garbage. The people I’ve chatted with on the app have absolutely nothing helpful to offer. Mostly they tell you to do screen captures of the behavior you’re reporting and tell you to make sure you have settings for auto reporting on. If it’s inconsistent behavior, how are you supposed to screen capture anything? 

The bug that irritates me more than anything is the fact that simply unlocking your phone with FaceID when you have notifications will kill your tree behind the scenes. And I mean this happens even when you are on the Lock Screen, and have not even opened your phone or interacted with the notifications in any way. I have to make sure to explicitly dismiss the Lock Screen when this happens and go into Forest to ensure it understands I haven’t left the app.

This is one of the bugs I contacted support about. The way they responded indicated they are aware of this bug, and just tell users to work around it. 

Aside from the highly irritating bugs I’ve encountered and the increasing faith I have that this app will only get buggier, it’s nice. The concept is great, the plant designs are cute, and I like that you can truly plant trees IRL through the app. It’s helpful to use this during work, when I need to get off my phone and sleep, or when I’m struggling to stop mindlessly scrolling on social media. The ability to tag the reason you are planting something and filtering your plot down by tags is great. It helps me see how often I’m exercising self control by using this app, and how often I’m doing so.

title: Forest is Fun
body:
As a neurodivergent ADHD type person I really like this app. I never write reviews but feel like this deserved one!

This app is really simple - it doesn’t try and do anything except create a timer for your work (ideally pomodoro style chunks of time but whatever floats your boat). You can set the app to not complete your study time (poms are 25 mins) if you leave the app! You can also turn that feature off easily. 

Other than the option to require you to stay in the Forest app and the time you study, it’s really simple. For each study session you complete you grow a little tree and get reward coins. 

The different things you can grow as you keep using it are actually really motivating but not interesting enough to be distracting. I have had a lot of pom timers but this is always the one I use.

title: Great Concept & Motivation for Studying
body:
It’s a huge plus that there’s a humanitarian and ecologically motivating factor for diving into productivity. I’ve perpetually avoided school work (among many other less than desirable responsibilities) for years and I’ve tried countless things to help keep me on track and focused. Along with other self-care tips like creating a relaxing setting for studying, proper breathing, getting up and moving, meditation, vitamins and eating/sleeping right This app is the icing on the cake. I can bring a more creative/optimistic outlook on studying. 

Also, for student that don’t know what the Pomodoro technique is - it really works!! If you’re a student and haven’t tried to, give it a shot. The technique is setting a timer for 25 minuets studying/reading/working & 5 minuets off. Personally I found that taking two 5 minuet breaks every two sessions and then one 15 minuet break after the third round is my sweet spot. There’s plenty of research to back up the technique if you’re interested in it :)

For App Developers: 

Please bring this app to full timer control/functionality on the Apple Watch!! A lot of students are looking to completely get away from their phones while studying (at least I am). Other than that amazing job on the app, will be by go-to every time I need to crack down on some productivity :)
