title: Honest Review of Forest
body:
This app is very useful and has helped me complete many assignments distraction free. I would definitely recommend it to students that feel they are constantly distracted by their phone. It is very satisfying to unlock new tree types and watch your forest become larger and more unique. However, I do have two complaints about this app. My first complaint is that this app $3.99. I think that it is worth the price if you continuously use the app, but nobody wants to spend $3.99 on the App Store. Many people probably scroll past this app after seeing the price alone because most apps that are popular are free, such as Tiktok, Instagram, Twitter, Youtube, etc. My only other gripe with this app is the ability to turn off the feature called deep focus. Deep focus is the feature that causes your tree to wither when you leave the app. If you disable deep focus, you are still able to do all of the distracting things that a phone has to offer while still growing your tree. In my opinion, I believe that you should not be allowed to disable the deep focus feature and that your tree should always wither when you exit the app. I find it contradictory that the ability to disable deep focus even exists since in the description of your app it states, “A interesting way to help you beat phone addiction and overcome distraction” (SEEKRTECH CO., LTD). If you can just disable the setting that punishes you for using your phone while growing the tree, then how is it helping you focus?

Overall, if you use this app correctly and have enough self-discipline as to not turn off the deep focus setting, then it is extremely useful for reducing the amount of time spent consuming media.

title: Saves Time & Energy
body: Forest is the BEST productivity/focus timer app out of the dozens that I’ve tried. Forest is truly so helpful and they partner with Trees for the Future to convert focus time into real trees being planted. 🤩You’re allowed to customize the intervals for task time/break time and even lock access your phone (or not) to enhance concentration. Your garden gains new flora with every successfully completed focus round. This is a beautiful representation of sowing a seed and watching it grow with time. Forest also have a handy web browser extension making it accessible for most phones, laptops, and tablets. LASTLY, we can’t forget that you can actually use focus coins to plant real-life trees and to support Trees of the Future! Forest has planted nearly 1.5 million trees. If you’re looking for a quality productivity app, look no further my friends. Forest app is the crème de la crème.

title: Two stars
body: While I love the idea behind this app, I cannot believe that there is no pomodoro timer! While yes, you could theoretically make one by having 2 separate timers, one set for working and the other set for a break but it doesn’t work seamlessly that way and feels like more of a hassle. There IS an option to use a “take a break” after your session but it should be automatic and you should be able to set sessions with a custom amount of breaks! Minus 2 stars for that, any time management app should have it. Another gripe is that you can’t have a timer set for less than 10 minutes, which makes trying to do a work around for the pomodoro timer even harder!!! You can’t even set a custom amount of time, it’s ONLY in increments of 5! Minus 2 stars for that, it’s utterly ridiculous.

author: HamzaHTX

title: Consistent user since 2016, love it!
body:
Hey forest team. I rarely ever post reviews, but I feel after this many years this app deserves my effort. I’ve been using this to help me focus since 2016 and have literally logged hundreds and hundreds of hours using this. It’s helped me with highschool, college, technical programs, and other courses. I’ve even used it to track my meditation and personal reading. I just want to say thank you. I have a ridiculously difficult time focusing thanks to a myriad of mental health issues that are quite literally out of my control. This app has been a game changer for me and I hope other people can have the same experience.

I also just wanted to voice some issues that I’ve had with the app (not very many at al but I know your development team is strong and actually takes reviews seriously). One issue is with the friends feature. I’ve tried to get many people to join the app and plant trees with me but I feel like each time it’s pretty difficult. That process could maybe be a bit more streamlined? One more thing is I think that I’ve noticed the app slow down as I’ve been using it. Maybe it’s because how much data I have logged in it? Not sure. It doesn’t affect the functionality too much but just something I’ve noticed.

All in all, hands down the best app I’ve had the pleasure of using. Again, thank you. If I could give more the 5 stars I would.

title: Incredible for people with ADHD
body:
As someone with ADHD who struggles infinitely with focus and maintaining my attention on one thing, especially with a phone within my grasp, this app has been an absolute life-saver. Before I started using this I would zone out, mindlessly pick up my phone, get lost on social media or some app, and completely forget I had been working or doing school work to begin with. As soon as I unlock my phone and see the Forest app open, I’m reminded of the task I was originally trying to focus on and it prevents those rabbit holes I would get lost in. 

Getting to see the physical manifestation of your focus and hard work is priceless. Not only do you get to see your forest and know that each individual tree represents 2 hours of focus, but you can look at each day, week, month, year to see the exact amount of hours you spent. I was really down on myself and felt like I wasn’t spending enough time studying. This app made me realize I’m actually spending a full 40 hour work week on homework, studying, tests, etc. It was a confidence boost that I am actually putting in the work.

title: Version for Tablets in Horizontal View
body:
I have always been (and sometimes still) a MAJOR procrastinator, and even with timers and using pomodoro technique, I still struggled with keeping myself from picking up my phone.
I’m a sophomore in college, and this app has been very helpful in making sure I keep myself accountable as far as studying and completing school work. 
Though this app is amazing already, I do have a few suggestions for future updates:
1) Be able to modify how many minutes = 1 plant for timer and stopwatch mode. I think this would be really helpful so that people can look at the trees and know that each tree represents a certain amount of time, especially if they use stopwatch mode.
2) Be able to use the app comfortably in horizontal mode. I think this would make the app experience better overall
3) Be able to use in split-screen mode on the IOS IPads. I think this would be good so users who already enjoy keeping timers through split screen can do so with the app.

title: 一些可以改进的地方
body:
我用这个app也有些年头了。一开始真的很爱，现在也还算喜欢。可是用得时间越长，越希望app能在一些方面改进。
比如：
1. forest在手机上启动起来有点慢，不能立刻进到界面，选想种树种得延迟至少3-5秒，选标签也是，很让人沮丧。本来高高兴兴打开app是要工作的，划来划去就是不动也是很让人丧失动力。原来以为是手机太烂换了个最新的iPhone,还是一样。
2. 树种不喜欢的可不可以退？用来用去喜欢的都只有几个。客服看到这个可能会建议我加最爱组合，可是有些树种我不喜欢，我就不想留。本来app就有点慢，还划来划去在庞大的树种中找自己喜欢的。
3. 更新树种的速度也要快起来。世界上那么多树种，可以帮助我们认识真的植物科类嘛！用来用去就那几个，实在是有点需要新东西了。
4. 标签可不可以纵向划？不要横向？标签一多，本来就卡，还要横向，屏幕总共就那么大。而且可不可以稍微给标签宽泛点的空间，一小条条，划来划去，本来就有延迟，真的很影响工作flow。真的。
5. 种了真树不显示？我种了真树，种到了哪里，长什么样子？我的小树长多大了？我都看不到，只知道我种了三棵树，我朋友种了8棵，世界种了几十万棵。请求不要告诉我你可以去哪里哪里看，我在用你的app，我就要在你app上看到。希望改进。
6. 为何在美国store上两美元，在中国store却要贵一点？

app本意就是记录productivity，如果因为app的设计而prevent productivity, 那就不用了吧。请求不要fix the user, please fix the design. 

我打三颗星。一年前的话四颗，两年前五颗。

The other issue is the few options. Being able to select the trees you want is nice, but you only start with about five and there aren’t many in total. Besides, with the charity option staring me down, I feel guilty buying any trees that aren’t gonna convince me to keep the app longer. There could be more events or a further-expanded second currency to get most trees, but instead I’m stuck with the five trees I have now.

title: Very Good App but with a very annoying flaw
body:
The app is great for what it does. It’s not too complex, but just has enough fun functionality to keep you motivated and involved. You might not like these kinds of gamified time trackers if the game part isn’t attractive to you (aka you don’t like growing trees or raising an RPG character), but for everyone else they should like this. 

There is only one very very annoying flaw. There is no landscape mode, at least not on tablets. People have been asking for this for a while now and it still hasn’t happened. I understand why they’d hold off on making it initially but with the release of the Magic Keyboard (which is now gen 2) that puts iPads in landscape, they should have developed this by now. Essentially it’s their way of saying only use this app on your phone.  Also it’s not a bad web plugin but I don’t really find it that useful. Maybe if your workflow lived entirely in a browser, it’d be more helpful.

This isn’t to be a downer though. It’s a very good app, it just has some flaws that are puzzling at best and keep it from being really great

title: Great for Developing Study Habits
body:
Overall, this application is 5/5. The visuals and theme are beautifully done and cohesive throughout all aspects of the application. It is perfect for users seeking to break unhealthy habits so common with cell phone usage. It could be particularly useful to adolescents as their limbic system and prefrontal cortex develop at separate times creating the need to practice and develop executive functioning skills explicitly (Laser, J.A. & Nicotera, N, 2021). Using a rewards system, this application effectively promotes self-discipline and self-regulation. The positive reward of growing a successful tree or forest capitalizes on adolescents heightened sensitivity and desire for reward (Steinberg 2014). Instead of creating a punishment or negative consequence for the inability to stay focused and off other apps, Forest rewards time well spent. Users can choose what type of trees they want to plan and work towards earning coins to buy a bigger selection of trees and plants. This allows the user to really make their forest their own and become invested in it, therefore helping positive brain development.  

A huge benefit is the ability to train the user’s brain to focus for extended periods of time. By starting at ten minutes and with the ability to go to 120 minutes, the user can increase at their own pace the amount of time they can enter focus mode. Through varied rewards, the application encourages the practice and growth of self-discipline. The achievement badges for users who plant trees multiple days in a row and establish practice patterns really emphasize the importance of practice and repetition for positive brain development and self-regulation. The more the user practices self-regulation and self-control through the app, the easier it will become.

title: Great, but could use some more features
body:
I absolutely love this app. I’ve gotten into the habit of using it so much that it’s part of my studying routine. There are some things I wish it had. 
1. It would be really nice to be able to pause a tree. For example, if you were planting a tree at work, but then needed to step away from your desk for a few minutes to help a coworker or something, it would be really nice to be able to pause the tree and then come back and restart it. Otherwise, you either have to kill it, or just let it grow - but letting it grow isn’t a truthful measure of your focus time. 

2. I think the “Plant Together” feature could be updated. It would be nice if friends could plant a forest in a room together, but not be constrained by the planting time of the other person. For instance, if my friend and I started a forest for the day, it would be nice to independently add to it at the same time with different trees and different lengths of study times. Right now, you need to be planting the same tree and the same time and for the same length of time as your friend. 

Overall, I really do love the app. I just think a few updates could make it even better ☺️

title: Improved my career/grad school habits…and
body: The 1st and only app that has effectively changed my life for the better. The support/accountability of being in the Discord/Facebook communities is great for planting trees that I don’t have (but that the room owner has), so I can focus on saving for planting Real Trees. But this review wouldn’t be helpful to the developers if I didn’t mention some possible improvements that would make it 5 stars: #1. The daily ranking for “Deep Focus” time has been counting the time when I disable “Deep Focus” mode too. Either the rankings should just say “Focus Mode Rankings”, or the rankings should only include time when “Deep Focus” is enabled. I recommend the latter option because I planted with “Deep Focus” disabled, then I closed the app, and scrolled through Instagram for over an hour, and still got coins/trees. I tested it again to make sure: I planted a tree, then I exited the forest app (closed it completely), opened up Instagram, waited for a minute, and when I reopened the forest app, the tree was still growing and the remaining time hadn’t even stopped counting down while the app was closed. It defeats the entire purpose of the app/rankings. #2. Add room invitations to the timeline. This would be so valuable. I’ve accidentally dismissed room invitations, and I know people sometimes wait 10+ minutes before starting to grow the plant so that people can find the link and join the room, but I can’t view my “recent invitations” or anything to join the room if I accidentally dismissed it. When that happens, it feels like I’ve really missed out, and I get discouraged. But if the invitation were in the timeline or even in a “Recent Invitations” section for 30 minutes, and it included a link to the room, I would almost definitely be able to join more foresters for growing sessions. #3. Add an optional “status” field to my profile for friends (or specific friends) to see. Also, the option to make the “tag” visible to friends would be great too. That way, my real life friends can check why I’m not responding to texts by checking my Forest status and would see that my planting status is “active” and the tag says “meditation”, so they know that I’m not just ignoring them. The option to make these things visible to friends would be a nice addition. #4 I would love it if my screen could rotate while the plant is growing. You allow the screen to stay on so I can see the plant grow periodically, but I like to lean my phone up against something so I can glance at it now and then…If my phone is charging, then it must be sideways for it to be leaned up against something (or else it will need to balance on the charger cable and that causes it to fall and become a distraction). If it rotated, then I could have it on it’s side, but still see the plant grow in the right direction because the screen orientation would have adapted to landscape. I’m only speaking from my experience, so I understand if these ideas don’t make it to production, but I think there are good reasons for them. Thanks for reading !

title: i like it a lot
body: To be honest, I really like this app. I think it’s super helpful, and super beautiful. I really like the grid layout and all of that. My only complaint is that I think that although the developers know this already, it is silly that there’s a limit on how many real tress you can plant through the app. my biggest complaint however is not necessarily with just this app but also similar apps that reward you for focusing which is that they don’t really get of a full Pomodoro experience, i.e. letting you set up multiple cycles of 25 minutes of focus and 5 minutes of break. Instead, you have to open up the app every time you finish your focus session and click to set a timer for the break and go back to the app after the break to start the focus timer again. Of course, this isn’t a dealbreaker on the app for me, it just means after that five minute break I will often get distracted and forget to come back to the app. Other than that I think it’s a great app and adding the classic Pomodoro experience would push this app to five stars for me.

title: Good! But I’d like an Autoversion
body:
The app is good at helping me keep track of the number of hours I work on art and teaches me to take periodic breaks for my own health. In that respect it’s successful. And it even has a pledge to plant trees. That’s always fun. You can look back on your productivity and keep track of how "good" you were that week.

I’d be interested in a version of this app that works automatically, though. Like you set up a date and times when you intend to be productive the following day, and if you don’t make it to those things you promised yourself, it keeps a record by showing you how many trees you "could have planted" if you had been on time. Like maybe some transparent trees in your forest. Just a thought!

title: Helps with my ADHD!
body: I have ADHD so I tend to getting easily distracted by my brain. I’ve been using the free chrome extension which helped, but then I would just go on my phone instead. I was hesitant to buy the app but it was really worth it. You feel kinda guilty if you end up going off task and kill a tree, which sounds bad but it really helps keep you on track. Once your in the groove of whatever you’re doing you don’t even notice that the time you set aside has been up already! If you’re a student that procrastinates, this is great for you! You can set the time and use it for more than just studying: breaks, cleaning, drawing, writing. Some of my only complaints are the price. Even though is pretty cheap, there is a desktop Chrome extension of this that’s 100% free. You’re only limited to only one tree and a bush which gets boring after continuous use; and if you want a different tree it’s only in the mobile, which is rather annoying. Other than that, it’s very versatile and user-friendly no matter the age. Very well done. 👍🏼

title: BEST INVESTMENT EVER OMG
body:
I hardly ever write reviews for apps, but I seriously LOVE forest! The whole app is very intuitive and they seem to be very invested in making sure the customer actually enjoys the product. They’re also always releasing new features so if you’re super ambitious and have bought all the trees, there will always be new options for you. 

I have two absolute favorite features. One is the break timer—you set it for a few minutes, and then it sends you a notification reminder when it’s time to start working again. It’s like a customizable form of the pomodoro method because unlike other apps you can choose exactly how long you want different intervals to be. 

The other feature which was just introduced recently is the stopwatch feature! My issue with selecting a time beforehand was that I didn’t know how long a particular task was going to take, and I prefer to do large chunks all at once. This way, I can do the hard part of starting a task and putting down my phone without having to fit my tasks into pre determined increments. 

Some people might just pick up their phone again right after the initial required 10 minutes have passed, but i feel like this feature allows me to work more because I don’t feel like I’m making a huge commitment to not touch my phone for 45 minutes. 

Overall, fantastic app and 100% recommend!

title: 100% RECOMMEND!!!
body: If you are on the fence about buying this app, take this as a sign to purchase and download it. This app is so fun and motivating. I have tried other methods like the Pomodoro technique, but it doesn’t seem to work. However, as someone who sometimes has trouble staying focused and getting things done, this app is helpful than one may realize. I love plants so this app is definitely for me. I get excited once I have planted things in my forest and sometimes don’t even feel like I am working because I am motivated to make my plants and forest grow. And I am disappointed when one of my plants die. Maybe it is just me but I also love how I am encouraged by receiving coins, which I can use to buy different types of other beautiful plants of my choice (which just motivates me even more). I love the aesthetic of the app and don’t know where I would be without this app. I spend A LOT of time on my phone, so the Deep Focus setting that kills my plant if I exit the Forest app is amazing. Because I hate seeing my plants die. I hold my forest in my heart and love watching it get bigger and bigger. The app is the best. It helps me get my work done while keep it stress free, light and fun.

title: Please, be aware…this app collects LOTS of personal data!
body:
I used to use this app and loved it. I had earned just about all the trees and many badges. The app isn’t glitchy and it’s just plain cute. (I didn’t like the update that changed how to select trees with the scrolling time ticker, etc.) Overall it’s a fun and useful app. 

HOWEVER, in all reality it’s a timer/time-tracker. There are many others out there that are equally functional yet DO NOT collect personal data. Maybe this isn’t important to you? If not, I would suggest you read about data collection to see if its something you ought to consider. Apple makes it easy to check what each app tracks and this one is a greedy little thing. 

For me, it’s a deal breaker. I had to remove it from my devices. There are other plant growing timers in the app store along with many Pomodoro type apps. I’m a student and teacher and this app has been a part of my life for years. I was disappointed to let it go. If they ever stop tracking personal data I’d be glad to return. 

If you really want to see a greedy data app, check out the App Privacy for that one major social media app that begins with F. Eeesh. (Don’t forget to click on the “see details” under the App Privacy section in the app store.

title: Very helpful app!
body: I have an anxiety disorder and one of my coping skills is to scroll through Facebook or play a game on my phone.  Mentally it can be very hard to break that habit, and sometimes I’m not even anxious, I just get distracted.  This app plays so well on how humans bond to things.  If you’re anything like me, the adorable plants you grow will quickly become your little buddies and you’ll want to avoid killing them, which makes it so much easier for me to just leave the app open as the timer counts down.  If you find yourself bonding with small things like stuffed animals or a rock that looks interesting, I highly recommend this app for when you need to stop playing on your phone for a little while!

body:

It helps time things during finals and makes sure I’m not on my phone too much when I need to get things done! I’m also very competitive...so I make it a game for myself to see if I can achieve a certain amount of coins within a certain time period 

I look forward to the new plants that come out and I WISH they would do like a “Turtle Plant” for reptile lovers (don’t have a cat or dog). In case anyone is wondering: National Turtle Day is May 23 and are in dire need of conservation help. 

Or perhaps a horoscope line that would target a large majority of their demographic.

Overall: 10/10 would recommend for anyone who needs help staying on track and focusing.

title: Seriously, find a way to incorporate regular breaks like pomodoro.
body: It’s a shock to me that the most recent largest revamping of the app is just installing a count-up feature. I mean is that seriously the most demanded feature? I’ve been trying to incorporate regular breaks into my continuous work sessions by running a pomodoro app together with the Forest app for ages, which has been super inefficient, and I’m sure I’m not alone. Maybe you can set an allowance of max of 5-minute break every 30min. You can choose how often you break with total amount of break time as constraint. Say you are planting for 2h, giving you a max break allowance of 20min. You can choose the traditional pomodoro method of breaking for 5 every 25min, or you can choose to work 1h and 40min and take 20. But seriously regular breaks are so essential for concentration and I just think missing that feature is a big flaw in an app that aims to improve concentration and productivity.

title: Engaging and Efficient
body:
For those who don’t want to read my “life story”, this app is awesome and yes, you should invest in it.

The first day I looked at this app, I thought it was a flunk, thinking I could time manage and be focused on my own. I slowly figured out that wasn’t the case, and I was more distracted than I said I was. Being on my phone was a huge factor to it as well.

So after two years, I come back and invest in this app. Sure, the ole’ planner and “hide your phone” prioritizing strategies were something. But I always knew where the phone was and my planner wasn’t getting filled consistently. When I tell you this app saved my work life.

The first day I used it, I played around with the settings and tried it without the Deep Focus. Once that seemed to do something, I grew my determination to turn it on. It was a challenge at first, but as I continued to use it, I realized my screen time went down, and I was getting workload after workload done. That’s when I knew I made the right choice. This app is everything and I plan on judging this more. Thank you for making this awesome time manager.

title: Longtime user as focus aid for ADHD
body: I’ve been using Forest on and off across Samsung, Microsoft, Apple, and Google devices for years and am very happy with it. It’s gotten better and better and the format is so pleasing to the eye. I am working on adapting to my ADHD and the motivation of keeping my little tree alive is fantastic. I especially like the deep focus mode that kills my tree if I exit the app. The app allows for use of Spotify or other listening apps while also blocking off other apps so you can continue to listen and adjust what you’re listening to while still locking the phone down. I honestly love it and am so glad I’ve stuck with it all these years.

title: Needed features
body:
I thought when I downloaded this app that I could name trees and dedicate my time to them like watering. Every day come back to my little “chores” bonsai and watch it grow a little more until I have a beautiful little tree on my phone after months of dedicating time. Same for studying and meditation. I thought this app would be a visual representation of time invested but it seems to be a token unlocking game where you choose the price and that seems so dull to me.

What I propose is: you set goals [7 hours a week] and depending on how much time you leave the app open on that plant it feeds off that time relative to your goal.

title: Totally Worth the Money
body: This is the app that’s got me through middle school and two years of high school. I don’t have a diagnosed focusing disorder, but I get writing blocks and procrastinate a lot. Like, a LOT. This app has helped me so, so much. It’s really got everything you could ask for. An amazing user interface, currency that you get  from focusing, fake (and real) trees that you can plant to make a beautiful forest out of focusing, tags so you know where you’re spending time focusing, and really cool analysis tools that show you what days and what times you focus the most. This is the one of the only apps that I would say is completely worth your money. The tech team is really amazing, I reached out to them about an issue I had and within a day they responded and within a week had fixed the issue. I’ve also for years been pushing for a stopwatch feature in their feedback survey(as a student I don’t always know how long homework will take) and they listened! The only things I guess I would say could be better would be the leaderboard, since it’s worldwide and there are some people who use the app to just get away from their phone, so they can have seriously high hours and it’s really impossible to beat if you use Forest for studying. Overall, amazing app that has literally changed my life in a positive way.

title: Simple and Effective
body:
I love this app so very much! It’s quick and simple to use (without unnecessary complications like to-do lists, etc) and so effective at getting me to put my phone down and just stay focused. And I love being able to look at my growing forest to see a visual representation of how productive I’ve been!

Two suggestions:
• I would love to be able to create an exception for a single app to use during my focus session, if the work I’m focusing on requires that app. 
• I love that Forest also credits for extra time when my focus session goes long... and I think that means I deserve to get birds in my trees! Maybe one bird for every ten minutes over? It would be such a fun bonus to work for.

title: Fun way to track daily activity!
body:
This is a great tool for those of you that build motivational momentum throughout the day by seeing your progress accumulate.  Once you’re familiar with the interface, it’s a quick tap to start tracking.

A few requests to improve the app:

   Allow users to modify the alerts when the timer ends.  Currently, when a timer ends the notifications are a little too subtle so it’s easy to go over your time.  If users can modify the alert notifications with a different tone or vibration sequence, that would make it much easier to allow yourself to focus on your work without having to worry about missing your intervals.

   Add apple watch complications showing time left and letting you start timers.

title: Please add scheduling!
body:
I love this app so much - I have a horrible phone addiction and have tried a ton of other apps but nothing is quite as motivating as knowing I’m going to kill my little tree if I don’t get off my phone. I’ve set up those Apple Screen time limits and every time the limit comes up, I just say “15 more minutes” with absolutely no shame. But I NEVER kill a Forest tree.

The only thing that would make this better (and for which I’d love the developers forever) is if you guys made it possible to schedule trees in advance! I often wake up and start the day on my phone and half my work day will go by before I *realize* and actually plant a Forest tree. If I could preschedule a tree for the morning, that would allow me to start off the day on the right foot. Super hope you guys implement this - and thank you so much for the wonderful app!

title: Motivation
body: It honestly makes me study more and to more work. I’m a lazy person. I would open up my laptop to do work but I would just sit there on my phone wasting a couple hours. So having to grow the tree while staying on the app the whole 10-120 minutes helps me do my work. I High key hate it when I have to hit the “give up” button to use my phone for something important or with unexpected events. But seeing the words “give up” makes me have self-motivation and higher self-development once I overlook that and continue to work/study. I love how I can add in my own tags, I have one for “Eat” and that’s my cooking time to prepare and eat time with my roommates so that I can be social and not want to check every little thing on my phone. So it really helps with distractions if you struggle with that. Plus, you can have your own custom motivational quotes. So I worry about my social media a lot and games that I play, so I would have quotes that say “Facebook and Instagram is fine, no one needs you”, “Chloe didn’t put up a new selfie beach picture”, “stop eating those m&m’s”.

title: Great, with Some Opportunities for Improvement
body:
I love using Forest as a way to feel like I am doing something positive (planting imaginary, even actual trees) while focusing on various activities.

My one suggestion would be to offer an option where a timer for focusing can be started and run for as long as focusing lasts, rather than requiring the user to specify a time period. Sometimes I’m not sure how long I’m going to be able to focus before I’m interrupted (e.g. my son running into the room needing something, a call coming in that I can’t dismiss), and it sometimes discourages me from planting if I’m worried I can’t determine how long I’ll be able to stay focused and don’t want a dead tree on my hands. Sometimes the break in focus is outside of your control, and I think this would be a good feature along with the timer option currently available to ensure that users can track how long they’re able to focus without interruptions.

title: Excellent app
body:
This app is really good. I’m a student who uses my phone way too much and this app has both made me aware of that and helped me spend less time on my phone. It takes a while to get new trees but I don’t even care because you start out with 2 or 3 anyway. I like to use different types of trees for different activities. 
As someone who enjoys nature but doesn’t have much opportunity to be in it, I’m very drawn to the forest aspect. I also like how you can see your forest for the day, week, month, or year. 
My ONE suggestion so far would be to have a feature that counts up instead of down; either that or a way to continue the same tree immediately after the timer goes off assuming you’re still focusing. If I’m focusing on reading I don’t always know how long it will take so if I set it for 25min and read for 45, I’d rather just extend the tree than have multiple smaller ones.
Other than that this app is fantastic and I highly recommend. I’ll keep using it for sure.

title: Great for studying
body: Honestly, I’m the type of person who just suddenly goes on my phone or laptop in the middle of doing homework, projects, etc. It’s especially been a problem since this new school year started. This app has helped me quite a lot, though sometimes I forget to plant a tree before I begin completing assignments. It’s helped with decreasing the amount of time I spend on schoolwork, and makes me feel like I’m doing so much more. Whenever I do reach over to my phone and am about to do something besides studying, like scrolling through Instagram, I’d open it and see the tree on my screen. Then, I’d ask myself, “Do I really want the tree to die?” I’d say no. In the beginning of using this app, I was always close to using my phone while the tree is growing. I began to develop a mentality after a few days that I should finish my homework before going on my phone and do other things. Of course, I sometimes still do it when I don’t use Forest, but I feel as if I’ve lessened the amount. This is the first productivity app I’ve used, and I’ve always seen people recommend it. It’s definitely an app worth the money. You can use it on your laptop or computer as well, as a Chrome extension (which is what I started out with). It’s simple to use, and has a minimalistic aesthetic that I really enjoy. Overall, it’s a great app.

title: DONT BE HARD ON YOURSELF
body:
This is a WARNING: you do not do as much work as you think. LOL. 
Before I first started using a timer I was, in comparison to my teammates and age group (‘97 baby woot), what I thought, very productive. I don’t even remember the last time I was “late” for a deliverable or anything... I just wanted to organize my brain with a timer. 
OMG. The first day or two... phew. I felt DUMB. My total work time was maybe 2 hours. (Then I started wondering what the heck my teammates we doing all day, if they don’t even work that long, but whatever.)
Breaking everything down into tiny steps? Used to that. That’s business, baby. 
Breaking everything into 15-45 min tasks?Mind-altering. 
I usually stick to 20 or 25 with 5 min break after. That sounded counterproductive to me at first, but HA. I can genuinely say after using this app that I did not truly know what it was like to focus on one task for even 10 minutes. 

Tip: Start on and ALWAYS stick to deep work mode. This will give you the discipline you are most likely looking for. Trust me, it makes you very sad to see that dead tree.

title: Not Awesome on iPad
body:
As a time-tracking/management app, Forest is both easy to use and fun to engage with. That said, it’s clearly optimized for the iPhone. The iPad version doesn’t support landscape mode, which makes it rather awkward to use while working on an iPad. It’s a shame, since the increased real estate on a tablet offers a wealth of opportunity for, say, streamlining the information gathered by the app.

I also wish there were a pomodoro mode. Yes, I could try to kluge together a series of trees to approximate the pomodoro timer, but it’s a pain to figure out if it’s time for a long break and it’s too easy to remember not to start a break timer.

title: So close to perfect!
body:
I’ve used Forest for about a year now, and I love it on my IPhone! Before using Forest, I would find myself using my phone while studying, which would lead me to losing focus and having to reread sections of text because of that lack of focus. When I got this app, however, I started studying much more effectively because the urge to use my phone was no longer there. I would highly recommend this app to anyone who is having difficulty with staying focused!

Now as to ways that Forest can improve the app: I recently bought the Apple Watch SE, and when I saw that forest was available for my watch, I knew I had to download it! When I opened it up, however, I was greatly disappointed. You can’t start a study session on your Watch, and the majority (if not all) of the features that make Forest for the IPhone great aren’t present. To me, it would make sense to add the ability to set a study session on your watch and have the countdown on it. After all, isn’t Forest meant to keep you off your phone? I could over look this, if it weren’t for the fact that you pay for this app. Other apps similar to Forest have the same features on the Watch app and their IPhone app. On top of the superior functionality, some of those apps also have the benefit of being free. 

So to sum up: this app is amazing if you’re using it on your IPhone, but where it can truly shine (in my opinion) is the Apple Watch. Forest is an amazing app, and I truly hope that the developers find a way to add more features to their Apple Watch app.

title: Amazing.
body:
I only have two suggestions that could make this better aside from prettier trees.
1) the option to arrange the week’s forest like a garden. More than the week would obviously cause one to spend too much time on their phone.
2) THE IMPORTANT ONE: I wish I could automatically plant a tree at certain times of the day. I would love to get an alarm warning that I am planting a tree so I would have to open the app. I believe I would use it 6xs a day. I would have it set to plant a tree an hour before bed, for an hour shortly after my sleeptown alarm goes off, when it is time to make food, and for a meditation/prayer/edification break. Sometimes I forget to even use forest if I get really locked in or obsessive about something. I need the help.

I am a writer and I prefer working on a computer or device. I also have Hashimoto’s which causes a number of mental illnesses when mu hormones get messed up, like OCD, ADHD and anxiety. Obviously I know how to spend lots of time on something fairly simple. I have a couple friends I text too much too. Point being, it’s really easy for me to spend my entire day looking at my phone and it doesn’t leave me feeling good and I tend to neglect my body. 

This app has been pretty great. I didn’t like the tree I started with, though the final incarnation is okay lol. I do wish they all looked a little prettier. I like things less cartoony, and I don’t actually like evidence of people in it lol. But it’s fun to build a forest and it helps when I am conscious enough to think, “I need to pay attention to my kid right now.” Often I end up not even picking up my phone again for a long time after I put it down.

Lastly, it does allow for a couple seconds away which is good because I do like to listen to music or podcasts while I do stuff sometimes.

title: 简单·有用
body:
Forest优点非常明显：
a.自动化程度高。所有番茄开始和结束的时间都自动记录，便于回顾时观察自己休息时间长短，以及高效工作时长与时间段。
b.color code和标签是很好的任务记录符号。
c.番茄结束后，可以写下工作记录。
d.无需纸笔，节省空间。

有朋友提到为了减少手机使用，他避免用Forest。这个问题完全可以得到改进。我有一个退休的iPhone SE，上面只安装了Forest。这样就算用手机，也不用担心短信和电话的干扰。现在便宜手机很多，完全可以用起来。

I should be able to switch between my note taking app and still be in landscape mode after going to forest. title: College Procrastination
body:
Thanks to COVID, all my freshman college courses are online, and procrastination has been the devil on my shoulder. 

This app has helped me eliminate my procrastination, and I didn’t realize how much my cellphone was distracting me. The feature of “deep study mode” kills the tree you’re attempting to grow if you leave the app, and the stress of accidentally leaving the app is surprisingly immaculate. I spend less time thinking about going on social media, and more time focusing on growing my tree. 

It’s also allowed me to grow the tree, and reward myself further with a timed break the app suggests. 

This is the first review I’ve ever typed, I get a sea coral tree from typing a review, I’m pumped.

title: Not worth it.
body:
I usually never pay for apps but I thought this one would be helpful. I was wrong. I love how it plants trees in real life but it doesn’t help much with productivity. It’s mostly just a way of setting time and measuring progress. 

This app does not let me know when to stop. It is not ideal for studying. It would have been great if this app was more of a timer so I would know when to stop instead of checking my phone to know if the time is up. It can send alerts for when the tree is planted or when the time is done but so can my other apps, which is distracting. If I let this app notify me with sounds, I would also be letting other apps do the same. It would be inconvenient if I turned off notifications for other apps. 

The app has an option that prevents me from checking other apps while the time is running but the system is not ideal. I would still need to do the work; control myself. I could still open other apps but my tree would die. It would have been great if I couldn’t access non essential apps while trying to focus. 

Basically, I don’t need this app.

Does my payment for the app help plant trees? If it does, I’d feel less bad.

title: Practical. Some limitations due to iOS.
body:
This app is a godsend. Well... not really, but it feels better to say that than to admit “I have no discipline” or “I’m addicted to my phone.”

It is super helpful in establishing some self-parenting/boundaries with my stuff. Hopefully this has a spillover effect on my social media use.

The only complaint I have is that I can’t give certain apps permission to not interfere with the growth of my trees. That’s due to iOS and it seems like the developers are aware of the situation. I make up that the response is “that’s just the way it is, nobody likes it, but we all have to deal with it.”

The way it’s currently set up is: I either pick the Deep-Focus mode that harms my growth if I exit the app or cancel the D-F mode, which means I can go in and out of the app. Basically all-or-nothing, which blows for my particular setup because I do use some apps for legitimate work reasons. I’ll have to find a way around that for now.

4/5 would recommend. If this Deep-Focus thing ever gets resolved, I’ll change it to 5/5.

body:

1) Please add landscape mode - if it’s available, I haven’t found it.  This is my biggest grip by far.  

2) The unlocking and gamification could definitely use a lot of love.  I know this isn’t the crux of what the app does but penalizing me for canceling a session by charging 60 coins seems too penalizing.  Earning coins takes too long.  The ‘reward’ of seeing the variety of the forest is meh...  

This could really be a killer app if these two things were added... I better get back to work :-)

title: Such a good app for productive sessions.
body:
I’ve been using the app since around 2018 I think? 

It has been a go-to for when I need to sanction time out of my day to do work, be productive, so on. 

The concept is fun and the app has a nice UI. It has looked great for a long time. I love the new widget options and versatility of all 6 types - honestly one of the best new widgets out there, I’d say. 

Every thing about it is clean and simple, while promoting productivity.

My only suggestion would be the ability to start planting from the Apple Watch app (synced to the iOS app). To me, being able to only see my forest on the watch app is kind of useless.

Great app all around. Would recommend it to anyone!

title: Love my forest!
body:
I know. The app seems silly. My friends laugh at me. I understand. But for those that are serious about limiting screen time, it is a HUGE HELP. For some perspective, I averaged 7.5 HOURS A DAY on my phone! That’s insane. I work in the media, so I’m naturally on my phone a lot but I need to be more in the present moment and unplug. 

This app does exactly that with a fun little game/challenge included when it comes to building your forest. The more lush the better!

Give it a try but only if you’re actually serious about changing your bad screen time habit. I did, and now I’ve cut off 3 hours! Within a single week!

title: Challenging App to Inspire a New Level if Focus
body: Planting trees requires REAL work. 1 simple timer won’t cut it and that’s where your role begins. You have the chance to push yourself to new levels of concentration to save as many coins as you can to plant a real tree at 2,500 coins. 2,500 coins is a daunting challenge that isn’t cut out for everyone. Be the exception. Be better than yourself. The more you study, the closer you get to adding real trees to the world. I thought I’d genuinely be planting at least 1 tree a day. Although I originally thought this was too good to be true, it is very clear the challenge you are presented with to create a better environment. Join the wave and enjoy the benefits of the new you. See ya there.

title: best app for students
body:
Gonna state the obvious. Of course there’s no ACTUAL enforcement from the app. It’s just perfect for keeping you off your phone. Smooth, runs nicely, has lots of cute plants that evolve as you study longer. For someone like me, who’s weak to cute things, the various plants are the perfect incentive. I also really like the feature that enables you to study with your friends! When you’re studying with them at the library it’s nice to “plant” together. 

If you’re hesitant because of the price—come on, it’s still not that much. It’s worth it in the end, and your higher grades will thank you.

title: Such a useful app
body:
My first app review...here we go!
This has to be one of my favorite apps. I take some pretty advanced classes and it’s important that I get the focus time I need. This app does an amazing job at encouraging me to not only stay off of social media apps, but to actually want to use this app to rack up coins and study time. You get coins for using the timer, and once you finish, you can spend them in the virtual store. It’s so satisfying to be able to earn new study sounds and/or trees to plant. Ah- forgot about that. While you focus, a virtual tree is planted and grows until you finish. It’s then added to your personal virtual garden- and I make a daily goal to make it as pretty as possible! Also you can use the coins you earn to have a real life tree planted somewhere In the world! Imagine getting work done AND saving the environment? Killing two birds with one productive app!

title: Definitely worth it!
body: This app has helped me greatly, no matter what I’m doing wether it’s cleaning, doing school work, or trying to go to sleep I’m always picking up my phone for no reason. I wouldn’t say I’m addicted it’s just when I’m  trying to get things done I always try to find something else to do. forest has helped me so much in staying focused, and it’s simply because I have a reason not to use my phone. Not only that though Forest provides labels when you plant your trees so you know what you were doing for that amount of time and then gives you a pie chart showing how much time you spend doing each thing like work or exercise.It also gives you sounds like rainforest sounds and things like that to listen to. Then you get to unlock different cute trees and build your forest. On top of all that once you get enough coins they plant a real tree in the world. Overall this game provides great statistics and motivation for me and was completely worth the two dollars.

title: Fun and works, but needs more features
body: So far I’m actively using it and having fun with it. I do feel more rewarded and accomplished when I finish a task which makes studying more fun and working from home less of a chore. It was definitely worth the $2! I think a reading feature would help though, especially for studying. It operates strictly on a timer, but say you need to read two chapters before tomorrow. It’s really hard to tell how long that will take. If you take to the material easily, it won’t take nearly as long as you expected to finish but if you stop the timer early you don’t get rewarded. So a checklist or task feature that maybe worked it conjunction with the timer would be better, something where you could mark a task as completed without being pinged because you got it done quicker than you thought. This could also work well if you’re trying to get chores done without getting distracted. Right now, this is better for work or sleep when you know you’re only going to be doing it for a set amount of time.

title: i enjoy it, but i’m missing some things
body:
i really like using this app to track how much time i spend on my work and it helps to take breaks with timed sessions so you avoid burning out. i like the tagging system so you can see specially how much time you spend on a certain task, such as certain classes or chores. i like that it shows which days you’re most productive and other interesting stats, and you can plant actual trees after awhile. 

some features i wish were included would be the ability to add a tree/chunk of time for the times i do work and forget to set the timer. id also like to be able to set a stopwatch without an ending because sometimes i want to keep working past the original time set. it’s annoying to have to pick it up and set an extra 10-15 minutes. at the same time, sometimes i’ll finish my work sooner than when the timer goes off, and then i need to kill the tree i’m currently growing or just let the timer finish, but then my times are slightly inaccurate. i know this is nitpicky, but it’s just some features i’ve used with other apps that i really enjoyed. i will continue to use this app regardless because i like their commitment to helping the environment and i think the forests are cute ways of tracking time spent.

title: Faulty Chrome extension
body:
This app used to be great, and its strongest point is the syncing between web browser and mobile app. While the mobile app still gets regular updates, the Chrome extension is no longer maintained. It stopped working in 2019 and was never updated. Trees planted in Chrome sessions are not synced, and the extension is really glitchy. Most of the distractions in WFH comes from web browsing. Developers, please fix the Chrome extension.

EDIT: Devs got in touch to say the Chrome extension was updated. Well, it was not. Everything is still buggy. The screen is not responsive unless you close it and open again. Can't change tree species. Won't sync. Doesn't work at all.

At the start of the summer, I wanted to stay productive (because even though I rushed through my work, I’m a huge nerd that likes school), so I decided to learn Spanish. I didn’t use Forest while I was learning Spanish because I completely forgot about the app. Eventually, I got tired of Spanish (and of course duolingo shamed me for it), and so I’m trying to learn Japanese. Japanese is a big struggle, and that’s when I remembered I had this app. This app is very helpful, because I can stay on track instead of getting bored and picking up my phone. My grades in school last year were terrible and I was on the verge of being dropped from advanced classes, but my grades improved when I started studying, despite rushing through my studies. This upcoming year, I hope that I’ll be able to use this app more. Also, because I’m doing virtual learning, I’ll get more chances to use this app! 🤗 さよなら!

title: Helps me be more productive
body:
This has been a great find for me. I set it like a pomodoro timer, 25 minutes at a time. I’ve been getting a lot of writing down, as well as getting work done on some other goals. Now, you can definitely “cheat”, so to speak, but like my teachers back in grade school would say, “you’re only cheating yourself”. 
Thing is, you might want to use your phone for the task you are working on. I like writing on my phone over paper and pen and even my laptop. So you can set the app to allow you to grow your tree even when you’re not in the app itself. And that’s how one could “cheat”. 
But I highly recommend the app. It’s been a fantastic help in me being more productive lately.

title: Useful, helpful, needs some improvements...
body:
Thank you for Forest. I appreciate the motivation the app creates to stay focused.

Several things are bothersome. I’m a tablet user, and I have an attached keyboard. It is not helpful to be limited to portrait view only. That’s kind of primitive, like early 2000s. Please add landscape view.

Second, it seems counterintuitive to have a support page that requires you to scan the page you are looking at to get to FAQs. Scan with what? Another device? Why would you assume I would have two devices? I suppose I can figure out a way to screenshot and then use it to get to support, but that’s not the solution I would expect from a Stanford guy.

Also, the Contact Us link do not create an email or go to a support fill-in form. It does nothing. So, you get to read my support request here. Please fix that.

I also found the app a little hard to work with at the start. The flow from operation to setup to reports to settings were not very easy to navigate. I still have some difficulty with this, and I think this can be improved.

Thank you for the productivity improvement that Forest brings. Keep upping the good work.

title: Excellent App
body:
I love this app, it is very motivational and user-friendly.  Some things which I think  could make it better are:

#1: Some sort of an alarm/“ding” sound at the end of the work sessions.

#2: A feature which allows you to see the average focus time spent per-plant.  For example, if you have planted two trees total, one after 50 mins and the other after 30 mins, the “average time spent” per tree could be 40 mins.  This could be extended into average focus time spent per-plant in the last day/week/year/etc, and could also be something you could turn on and off.  

Otherwise, very well done.

body: Forest provides a fun way to stay motivated while staying on task - an important strategy in a distracted world. I read the Forest dev team’s rationale behind not supporting starting planting from the Apple Watch, however this functionality is critical for people who are trying to fully reduce the need to pick up their phone in the first place. title: Eric
body: I usually don’t write reviews, but I knew I had to write one for this app. At first, I had doubt. I’m they guy who constantly checks his phone for no reason and gets distracted. I planted the first tree, and magically, it just worked. I did longer trees and it helped me get off my phone for the whole night! The app makes you plant a tree, and you can’t exit the app for however long you set it. If you finish planting the tree, it goes in your forest. However, if you leave the app, the tree withers and shows up on your forest as well. You can use this with friends, coop, and gain coins for ever tree planted and achievement completed. Not only that, it is a relaxing app that has a selection of calming music(beach sounds, forest, etc). I believe the reason that this work is psychology. It makes you want to finish the tree and get coins, any brag you your friends about how many trees you planted. It puts pressure on you to not give up which I think is genius. Overall, this is probably one of my best purchases ever.

title: Need to have the ability to re-adjust time
body:
This app is very, very great. Definitely 5/5 stars to the majority of people. But, 3/5 stars for me.

I want the ability to re-adjust each time spent on focusing. 

For example: I enabled “count exceeded time” in the app setting and used 30 mins timer for studying. Then after studying for only 30 minutes, I forgot to stop the timer and, instead, went 50+ minutes rather than 30 mins. This ruins the accuracy of my tracked time. 

Perhaps take back my 1 coin for every 6 min re-adjustment.

body: I got this app after seeing a really cool quiz on Twitter that was about what kind of tree/flora you are/like/etc. I had downloaded it a while back, and didn’t pay much attention to it until now. I have made in-app purchases, (which I usually forbid myself from doing for apps,) because the variety of trees you can plant while focusing and the amount of different relaxing sounds has made me fall in love with Forest! I feel a pang of guilt when I pick up my phone and deviate from the forest telling me that my tree/s will die if I quit focusing LOL it’s actually been extremely helpful for me to keep track of my study time, I never realized how often I am distracted by notifications, text messages, etc, and Forest has helped me stay on track in the most interesting and beautiful way. title: One of the best apps I’ve ever purchased
body:
Here’s the truth: I’m only in middle school but this app has been a LIFESAVER. I’m a straight A student but still find myself procrastinating and not putting all my attention toward my schoolwork. Especially when I have an exam, I always wait till the last minute to study. Ever since getting this app though, I have found myself being more productive. This app allows me to set a goal for myself for when I would like to get something done in a period of time but still allows be to do it correctly. It makes you want to get your work done because you are building a forest while spending time towards your responsibilities. I have stopped looking at my phone every five seconds and have learned to detach from social media. This app has helped me pick up a good work ethic which is very much needed right now as I am having to start to prepare for high school.

If your anything like me, you have to have some sort of sound going on in the background. One specific thing I absolutely love about this app is it’s option to put on a sound while the timer is going. These sounds are soothing and don’t distract you. One sound for example, is just the background noise of a rainforest. I use this option all the time when doing homework or even just preparing for an exam. One thing I will have to say about this app is that your forest doesn’t grow very quickly. You have to be constantly using this app to fill up your forest and don’t get many plant options at first. But every time you grow a tree it’s very rewarding to see how your forest grows. Overall, I am so glad I stumbled upon this app and know I will continue to use this in the future. ( If your deciding whether or not to buy this app, I suggest you do. It’s well worth the two dollars. )

title: Great app! Broke me of my constant phone-checking habit!
body: Great app! I have to admit that I thought, “How can a simple little game like this actually make people more productive?” Then I tried it.... No one was more shocked than me as I found myself going to my phone only to plant my next tree and check on my forest! Rather than constantly checking email, texts, Facebook, news alerts, etc., I’m actually living life the way I used to - which I’ve missed (family conversations, getting work done, exercising, preparing meals, etc.) It’s surprisingly fun, and it works! If you want to get your time back, just plant your first tree!

title: Cheated
body:
I downloaded this app after its recent hype on Twitter. Basically they falsely advertised it as this sweet concept where you are able to grow a tree which reflects you- I assumed this app would give me great strides in self discovery. In reality: it is an app designed to have your phone on but also off limits. 
Overall, helpful and a nice way to redefine productivity- you can even spend the "money" you earn through staying off your phone on planting real trees! I would recommend this app to anyone I know with phone addiction problems.

title: 100% Worthy Investment
body: I do not buy apps. Ever. It is against my religion. However, there was a quiz made by this app going around Twitter that told people what kind of plant they were. It was Pure™, so I looked into the app itself. When you need to get something done, you just set the timer and start planting a tree. I am an AWFUL procrastinator. I am procrastinating right now by writing this review. I can rarely be successfully guilted into not procrastinating. But when you leave this app, the tree you planted starts to die. Nothing has ever motivated me to stay off my phone more than a pixelated tree’s life in my hands. The app will even play soothing music while your tree grows. Everything about the aesthetic of this app is amazing and it actually works, if you find yourself saying “I’ll just text this person back really quick” then end up scrolling Twitter 30 minutes later. PLUS you can help plant real trees. 10/10 a great app, definitely worth the $1.99.

title: It's a neat app
body:
I have a hard time doing work because I easily get distracted but this app is certainly helping. I don't know how but I guess it's just how the app makes me consider that giving up on my task kills tree motivates me to keep going. The app also has features like being able to adjust the timer from 10 minutes to 2 hours of studying, get different kinds of trees, use gained coins to plant actual trees, has different kinds of study sounds, and my favorite is the deep focus mode where you can't leave the app at all. 

While I can force myself to focus on my own, this app makes it way easier to focus and makes it fun in an endearing way. And while they have lots of types of trees, I wish they had more kinds of study sounds and trees though.

I wanted to get back into reading, doing chores on a far more regular basis, you name it. While using this app, it has taught me to turn up my Spotify playlist with whatever mood music I’m interested in and focus my time and energies toward the tasks ahead of me. Time flies so fast but at the end of all of it, you get to see what all you’ve spent your time accomplishing and soon you are a part of a book club (or two), you are learning to code, and your house has never looked so good in over a year.

title: Decrease in Quality Recently & Counterproductive Chrome-to-iOS Sync Issues
body:
PROBLEM: You must improve Chrome-to-app syncing so that we can use and reap the gold rewards for using the chrome extension on multiple devices AND this app on multiple devices. Currently, users are punished (by losing gold) when they run the extension and app simultaneously. For an app rated at #2 in productivity, this seems counterproductive.

TIMELINE: This has been an issue for over a year now (there is a Chrome extension complaint about this from Feb 2019). We paid for this app. That means you have the funds to dedicate resources to improving the Forest application. 

SOLUTION: If you’re worried about players getting gold too quickly by using multiple devices, then input an algorithm that first recognizes when multiple decides are running a session simultaneously. If a user has only one device, then they earn gold normally, with no change to the rate. The gold earned from any simultaneously-running extra devices (eg extensions or app) should be at a lesser rate.

I’ve used this app for over a year now, and it’s been good for the most part. However, the Forest app developers need to get it together. For a paid app, I expect better.

PROBLEM: App developers have ceased giving users motivators for lengthier sessions. All the new trees have just one stage for all session lengths. That’s laziness. 

SOLUTION: Make multiple stages for new trees.

Low rating to get app dev attention.

title: Best productivity booster for me
body:
Love this app! It’s very motivating to see your forest grow, work toward unlocking new trees, and be able to look back at your stats to see how much you’ve done, what you plant most, and what you spend the most time doing. I also like that you can toggle deep focus depending on the task at hand and tag your trees. I appreciate that the developers are consistently updating to fix bugs and add things like new trees.

A couple ideas for features that would be nice to see added:
-I would appreciate a feature, especially as more trees are added and the store continues to grow, that allows us to favorite trees in the store so it’s easy to find what we want to buy again when we have enough coins.
-It would be nice to be able to earn time crystals or have an option to convert from coins to time crystals. I understand that there are costs associated with developing an app and keeping it up to date, and consistent income including revenue from in-app purchases is helpful/necessary to do that for an ad-free app, but it would be nice if that feature wasn’t completely inaccessible to those of us who don’t have much money to spare after the initial app purchase but missed the trees when they first came out. (I would still expect time crystals to take more work to earn, but it would be nice if it was a possibility.)

This is one of the few productivity apps that’s actually worked for me, and I have no qualms about recommending it to anyone who’s easily distracted by their phone and looking for a productivity boost. Coming from someone who doesn’t have tons of money, I don’t regret paying for Forest at all. It’s simple but effective, customizable in the ways it needs to be, collaborative when you want to work as a team, and ad-free. Great app!

title: i love it!
body: Not gonna lie, I NEVER buy apps. I always go for the free version. I actually first discovered Forest through the free Chrome extension and fell in love with it! I had planted so many trees that it was to the point where I was like, okay, time to get the app. I haven't regretted it! I even just got the 21 day coin booster, which is also well worth the extra $2. Instead of getting 43 coins for my regular 2-hour sessions, I get triple that amount for a great price! I wouldn't even mind paying a few extra dollars to make the booster permanent, if that was an option. I also love that it syncs to my laptop. In the chrome version I can block off certain websites while my tree is growing so I can stay on task, which I definitely need. I'm a full-time homeschool student and it is SO easy to get distracted, but with this app I just can't risk letting my little tree die! Overall it's a great app and I HIGHLY recommend!

There are a couple of things I don't understand, though: when you successfully grow a tree for 30 minutes, you get 10 seeds, but when you successfully grow a tree for 2 hours, you get 31 seeds. Shouldn't it be 40 or more to reward the person for staying focused for a longer period of time? It would also be nice to see a full weeks’ forest and a couple of other features, maybe like blocking certain apps while working with your phone or something?

Forest is a great idea, and it works well, but all you get from your productivity w default setting is a shrub and a pine tree. So you just fill your garden with that for a while. You need A LOT of coins to buy other stuff or have to pay $. The only thing I like better about it than flora (another productivity app) is that you can plant an actual tree without paying money, but you obviously still need a lot of coins. I prefer Flora because you just have to be productive for so long to unlock a new tree. It takes less time. The garden isn’t on a square though - which I think I’d prefer. title: Read the privacy policy!!!
body:
I was using this app for a while and decided to let my son (under 13) use it.  When I created his account, it triggered the “age mechanism“ and I was supposed to click “contact us” to obtain a code (which crashed the app.  I mentioned this bug twice and support failed to acknowledge it both times).  So I emailed support directly for the code and they said “please provide copies of two government-issued photo IDs (e.g. Social security number, driver’s license or passport) for review” and they would delete it after.  I hope I don’t need to explain why this would be a major red flag from a security perspective.  If I do, you will probably not be concerned about this review.    

Upon reading the privacy policy shared by the support team, I noticed they are collecting “geographic position; Camera permission; Storage permission; Photo Library permission;”. (and plenty more which I won’t get into).   Maybe there’s functionality in this app that I’m not using and there is actually good reason for this app to be collecting this kind of data, but, on the surface, this app seems like a pretty simple timer and I was using it for that purpose.  From reading other reviews, I believe that is what others are using it for as well.  Why on earth do you need my geographical location to set a 25 minute timer?!  

I was going to just forget about creating an account for my son and continue using the app, but, after reading the privacy policy, I decided I really have no reason to be sharing all of this data to do something that any basic timer can accomplish.  I would encourage everyone to question whether or not the risk of exposing all of this information is worth the reward of using this app.

title: Helps me Improve my Relationship with Technology
body:
Studies show that wasting time by distracting yourself with distractions from doing productive work leads to less having no motivation to complete your work for the day. 

There’s so many applications out there today on the internet to try their application for productivity using the Pomodoro technique, and implementing features to prevent getting yourself distracted all the time by sending a notification that your tree, or plant will wither if you don’t get back to work. This is an amazing feature because this shows you need to focus so you can continue working until you’ve finished or done some progress. Since progress is everything than striving for perfection which are what I’m most insecure about actually. 

However, as I realize while looking at this time management app by Freedom because they have MacOS version of Freedom.  I want a MacOS version of Forest, so I can keep Forest on my laptop too than having the chrome extension, and app from the App Store alone. If you could possibly make a Forest available for MacOS especially for Windows this can tremendously get people to improve their relationships with technology even more. 

Freedom is expensive because of their pricing options, but a Forest is better for the rational reason I got this app for $1.99 or someone wants a free app for productivity uses. 

As form of closure, this app is created for everyone who uses technology in unhealthy ways like staying up late and sleeping late at night, overworking which leads to serious health risks such as emotional exhaustion, stress, depression, and physical health issues. I would highly recommend this to anyone who are often distracted from being able to be focused.

title: Love it, but a COUPLE SUGGESTIONS
body:
The app reeeeally helps me stay focused so I really love it. But I truly feel like we should be able to 
1. Earn more coins if you focus with a friend! It incentivizes others to plant trees together, which might be a way to attract new users!
2. Earn more coins for each tree that we unlock. It’s kind of annoying that the price of trees goes up after each purchase, but you don’t even get anything extra out of planting them besides seeing the tree in the forest (which I don’t really care about). If the price is going up for each tree purchased, so should the amount of coins we can earn.

title: Title (Haha, review is more serious than my title)
body:
I absolutely love this app. I fee really motivated to work when I use it. Even if I’m not being productive, I’m still working on something when I use it. I love how you can cancel a tree without killing it for the first 10 seconds after planting one, but I really wish that time was longer for bigger trees. It would be pretty helpful.
      The biggest moment for me was when it came time for me to kill my first tree. I really didn’t want to kill it, but I hadn’t been working. If I hadn’t chopped it down, it would’ve opened the floodgates for me. The main difficulty for me is starting to grow my tree. If I don’t start it, I don’t have to be productive.
      I’ve had this app for under a month and I’ve already recommended it to a few people, who have all said it was really helpful.
      I definitely think this app is worth a try, and I love the little changes that come out every one in a while.
      Gotta go, my math homework is waiting!

author: cyndy_ella

title: Forest: A cute little productivity app
body:
Yes, it is a timer app that can easily be substituted for your stock timer app on your phone or device but Forest is so much more than that. 

Every time you use the timer, you get the opportunity to plant virtual trees. The more you use the app and stay focused, the more coins you receive that you can use to unlock different kinds of species to plant into your virtual forest. 

Additionally, you can save up your coins and make an even bigger purchase (no real money need to be spent besides the initial fair price of download) and plant a real tree! 

Tags are useful to categorize how much time is dedicated to a specific task you have or will complete. Interface is simple, nice and clean. Definitely a useful app that will be in my devices for a long time.

title: Positive Inspiration is Working Bettering
body: You name it, I’ve tried it when it comes to productivity/focus aids. I was not expecting this...but somehow this tree-planting thing is strangely motivating me. I feel protective of the tree while it’s “growing”. I feel like it’s not too hard to resist my impulses until the tree is finished uling software “growing”.  With the ability to tag trees gwith various categories, my mind is exploding with the possibility of where I could be after “100 trees of #websitedesign” or a forest of #meditation or how my relationship with my kids would improve after “50 trees of #qualitytimewithkids”.   It is bite-sized so it isn’t daunting. I don’t have any guilt associated with not-planting-another-tree-right-then and it is SO fast to get started that I don’t dread it like I dread loading my scheduling software each morning.  I’m pretty safe to be productive as long as I keep planting trees and GO!  Thank you! Thank you! Thank you!

title: Helps Me Read More
body:
I learned early on that ebooks were not for me because of my tendency to get distracted by the other features of the device. Even dedicated e-readers failed to keep me focused on the page because of their tempting note-taking and highlighting features.

So I stuck with time-tested paper books. But even then the nearness of my phone made reading more challenging.

Forest helps me ignore my phone. It’s such a seemingly simple psychological trick, but it works: pick up my phone, kill a tree. It doesn’t matter that it’s not a real tree. The app successfully games my mind into behaving as if it were.

I highly recommend Forest if you, like me, feel your phone takes up too much of your attention.

title: Love my trees but is it useful?
body:
There’s definitely a productive benefit to watching a tree grow and focusing on a specific task. That’s what this app does. So, for anyone who creates content, freelances, or is looking to build a skill, this is a SIMPLE way to monitor time and focus. 

But this is not a time management app. 

It’s barely a time tracker and more of a in-app store to buy digital trees. Maybe that’s all the app wants to be. And as someone who has a deep love for tamagotchis, Im into caring for a focus Forrest with different unlock-able trees. That’s totally my bag.  

My issue is that there’s no real analytics behind how you’re spending your time. I’d love to be able to see how my time is being used. That stats they do show you are pretty shallow. 

I know the app doesn’t promise to be a habit tracker, I just see the potential of it being one. I want similar stats to programs like Mint or Instagram analytics. I also wish the animation and actual Forrest function was more dynamic. 

In all it’s an okay app but I think it could become awesome. 

P.s 
I wrote this review for a free tree.

title: Unlike All Others
body:
I personally use these types of apps to motivate me to achieve certain tasks... and many of those tasks are work-related, and thus on my phone. It helps to set a timer, with a motivation like a tree attached, for me to focus on whatever task it is. Whether it be finishing an art project, responding to messages, or clearing out my inbox. 

So many other apps don’t allow me to exit the app. This one does. A+. No glitches. Variety of trees. Fair rewards. 

I only wish I could set it for 5 minutes, or at least have the option for it to send an alert at the half-point mark.

title: Lovely App
body:
Helps me focus to study; as someone with major ADHD, it’s useful to provide motivation for short periods of time! Love the aspect of unlocking trees, just worried about whenever I unlock them all; if the app creators can make some sort of consistent and ever-expanding progression system where you always have motivations to keep gathering the coins it’d be 5 starts for me! Given that they occasionally add trees, I think they’re getting there — could definitely improve the sounds/atmosphere music offered for purchase and maybe more purchases or aspects could be added later? This is all just nitpicking though, currently I’m quite happy and highly recommend the app!

Edit: A simple addition would be a way to batch edit tags; it’s a simple fix, but would improve user interface as I create tags for classes and different aspects of projects; once a project or semester is done though, it’s tedious to individually delete — and I’m sure other people rotate through different tags as well :)

Earning seeds/coins takes a lot of time, I just wish you got more seeds per studying session — but I get it, it’s a way for you to earn your new plants instead of getting them all quickly.
