title: Makes me want to be productive!
body:
I really enjoy using this app! I recently got it and I used it on the first day I got it. 
I think the features it has is cool, too. There are different settings for the background noise and they start you out with rainfall outside a window. (You have to “earn” the others with the coins you make). Another feature I thought is helpful is the ‘deep focus’ setting that you can put the app on and if you leave the app, then your tree or bush withers and dies. It kind of forces you to put down your phone or else the thing that shows that you’ve done your work is gone.
I like being able to label the trees or bushes with the task I completed as well. My forest is growing!
The only thing I don’t like as much is how you have to wait for a long time to unlock a different type of bush or tree. It’ll probably take a week to two weeks of like, an hour in order to unlock a new tree. :/
Overall, I really enjoy this app! (Please let me have a new tree).

title: One of my go-to productivity apps
body:
It’s funny; I’ve downloaded so very many productivity and timing apps which are, admittedly, more sophisticated. However, time and again, I turn to this app to stay focused. I really enjoy it, seeing my cool trees grow.
My one complaint is how sparse the interface and “forest-view” are. . . This is the only reason I’ve taken off a star. It’s a free app; I get that. However, there are optional in-app purchases—-it seems to me that it would be worth it to the developers to put a “prettier” pic in background while growing my tree and a MUCH nicer view of my forest. I’d pay a little for this if they did it (for sure) and/or perhaps they could implement better/different in-app purchases to support such an overhaul. Anyway, would be truly my fav productivity app, and never would I stray, would they work on these aesthetics!! In the meantime, though, I’m sure I’ll continue to use this pleasing little app :)

title: Different Timing Options
body:

I would suggest having a mode that lets you just turn off your phone in the app for as long or as short of a time as you want without setting a goal.  And if we leave the app, it doesn’t kill the tree.  Just the amount of time we stay in the app without leaving it results in different colored plants and trees.  Like maybe 1-5 minutes could be a flower and maybe like 60 minutes could be a willow tree and so forth.

title: Best Productivity App Ever!
body:
I very rarely spend money on virtual things, but this app is definitely worth the $2. I have never been this productive in my life. The sheer quality of this app is amazing. Forest has a beautiful Graphical User Interface. I end up spending the most time on my phone using this app, if you don’t count Safari and Messages. Forest has a feature that displays a graph that implicates your productivity throughout the day. The feature that breaks down how much time you spend on individual activities is also quite useful and interesting. It’s genuinely a great app.

My only complaint is that you cannot rearrange the order of your tags, or the order that they show up in the pie graph. Also the Time Line tab is a bit useless. Other then that, this app is perfect.

title: Awesome App!!
body: I have been using the Forest app for almost 2 months now and this app has been amazing!!! It has helped me be way more productive and create so many good habits!! I'm a mom with kids and it's often hard to get motivated to do housework, pay bills, etc., when the same chores stare me in the face day after day. Growing trees gives me just enough incentive to not only get things done but also I can then look back and realize at the end of the day I have actually accomplished something! Also, I have always struggled to maintain good habits such as exercise daily, eat a certain amount of fruits & veggies, get to bed on time, etc., but with this app I grow specific trees/bushes for each habit I maintain each day. I then have a record to not only help me remember to do each habit but to see how long I've maintained it. I know some reviewers mention it's "just a timer" but for me, it's the extra bit I need to motivate me especially as there is a record of my accomplishments. Also, I like that each tree/bush costs an additional 100 coins up to 1000 per tree/bush as early on that motivated me to add more things/habits I grew trees for, which then made it easier/quicker to earn enough coins for the next tree. Just be creative how you use the app!! Finally, and very importantly, I wanted to mention that I had no issues with the app until just the other day when an issue came up with trying to label the trees. I contacted the app makers through feedback under settings and they not only responded but had the bug fixed within 24 hours. For a couple dollars this app is so incredibly worth it!! Thank you!

title: I LOVE THIS!
body:
I LOVE THIS! It definitely helps me get started when I feel disoriented and am having trouble focusing. I just set it for 20 minutes, study, and then bam that’s all I need for my head to get back in the game. Just a nice little motivator to get started on the tasks at hand. 

I give it 4 stars and not 5 because unless you’ve been using it for a really long time it can get kind of boring. Just because you keep planting the same tree and or bush over and over again. It takes a long time or $$$ to get something different. 

And this can make it less motivating sometimes. It would be nice to have more variety of trees and bushes available from the get go soon as you get started. 

And maybe we could add some other things too like little houses or swings and stuff and maybe people.

It would also be nice if I didn’t have to start a new forest everyday but could also have the option to just add to a world or map that stays as is. 

Other than that I love this app.

author: JoyceHere

title: Not for me
body: I feel like this is a concentration tracking app more than a productivity app. You plant a tree for every task you wish to concentrate on and if you break your focus (leave the app) the tree will wither. The problem here is that I need to concentrate on work, to work I need to use my phone. This app allows you to create a white list of apps that are required for your task, however this feature is not available in IOS devices. This renders the app to be nothing more than a tea timer and a graph depicting how many times you set the tea timer. You are allowed to create your own tags, but you can’t assign a task to your session until after the session is over, this means that if you read a book 7 days in a row you plant 7 trees instead of continue to water the same tree to keep it alive. I only bought this to be a visualization of my consistency with the various aspects of my life, but the app doesn’t work this way. I don’t see why this app isn’t free with ads considering that one of its most important features does not work on iPhones.

author: Shovel boy 2000

title: Really makes a difference!
body:
I just wrote a review for SleepyTown so I thought I’d come back to update my Forest review to reflect my current opinions. This app basically got me through nursing school and boards. I recommend it 100% to anyone, whether you’re a student or just use your phone too much, and I have gifted it to college friends before to help with study focus and/or phone addiction. I used to get very distracted from my studying and needed this kind of subtle motivator to stay away from my phone for specified periods of time. I’ve heard friends recommend such free apps as tomato clock, but Forest (I always accidentally call it “Trees”) is better because you have some proof of your efforts and can gain some satisfaction from actually seeing your success and trends over time as your forest grows, and it’s gratifying. If you’re a completionist like me, it would also bring you great displeasure to have to kill a tree that you’ve invested any amount of time in, so it’s like there are stakes and consequences for cheating yourself. It’s just an extra push to go all the way and keep focusing when you feel like it would be harmless to break focus and sneak a peek at Twitter.

There are also so many beautiful tree and bush designs to encourage you to grow a gorgeous forest. If my forest is looking a little barren, I get the urge to grow some more trees, and can’t have too many of the same kind of tree, so let’s switch it up and plant some sakuras today! It’s like addictive art. I also like that, if you choose to leave your phone open while you work, at any given time you can glance at your phone and see a little motivational message to stop stalling and get back to it! You also have the option to input custom messages, but I haven’t taken advantage of that.

Another well-used feature of mine is that you can customize tags for each tree to indicate how you spent your time focusing, whether it be studying, reading, exercising, or just relaxing. You can also see those analytics in your Forest overview. Now that I am a college graduate with a big girl job, I don’t need to study as much anymore, so it is nice that I can still continue to use this app for leisure activities such as reading. I occasionally use it to get some uninterrupted sleep, as well, since I work third shift, nap a lot, and sleep at odd hours. This is okay for me since I was interested in SleepyTown but can’t get use out of it as it is not really designed for people with schedules like mine. There are even the cute Starry Tree and Moon Tree designs that I will save up for to perhaps use exclusively as sleep trees!

My request: More visual growth “stages” of a tree. After all, the longer you focus, a more interesting-looking tree is yielded. I like this feature a lot! Feel like focusing for only twenty minutes? Nah, maybe I’ll go 25 just so I can have that more interesting-looking tree instead of that boring bush. It encourages you to go to the next level and increase your ambitions if you were feeling a little lazy. That being said, I would love a couple smaller benchmarks, like maybe one at 40 minutes, as going from 20 minutes to an hour is quite a big difference when intensely studying, and a lot of the time I only want to focus for 30 or 40 minutes at a time. I rarely ever have an occasion where I need to focus for two hours at a time or where it is practical to not use my phone for two hours (unless I’m asleep, because I’m an adult, and sometimes people just need to reach me) so I never get the fanciest trees. However, one of the features they have added since I started using this app allows you to turn off Deep Focus mode so you can exit the app without killing your tree. I still have yet to try this feature as it feels a bit like breaking the spirit of the rule, but I will be experimenting with it in the future.

I hope this app continues to come out with more features, designs, and achievements as it’s been quite useful and very fun to use! Thanks for a great app.

I set a timer for how long I want to be productive, and for that whole time, I can’t use my phone without making my tree wither. title: I.LOVE.THIS.APP.
body: I've used a lot of "focus" timers before, but this is the best. You put the timer on, and depending on how long you work, you plant a tree or bush or other things you can unlock (not by purchasing, but by more deep work). After accumulating 500 coins, a REAL TREE is planted by Trees for the Future. It is moderately challenging to accumulate this number. Trees for the Future has a 90% overall score from Charity Navigator. If you leave the app to do  some internet browsing etc., you kill a tree in your own digital forest. Instead of an "exit" button, you click "give up"...which I found to be rather reinforcing. Finally, if you get texts, they come up on the screen briefly but you only officially "give up" if you exit the app and respond.

title: Great productivity app!
body:
Used this all the time to get me through studying and am still applying it in my engineering career.

Set for initial 25 mins to get yourself to focus. Keep going past your final timer for an intense work block. I have 2 different “work intensities”. The second type of work block, after the 35 mins I break for 5 mins. This is for the more boring work that doesn’t required that much focus but “needs to be done”.

I like the game aspect. Getting different trees and forcing you not to click away from the app are very helpful in making you want to do your work and keep you off your phone. 

Highly recommended

title: Focus for a good cause
body:
This app has been a helpful asset to building better habits in my life. Sometimes I use it as a timer/ dare to get stuff done , e.g. “I have two tasks to do, I’m going to see if I can get them done in 30 minutes.” It takes personal work to build habits and work ethic, and this app acts as a good support of that. When I first bought the app I was studying for the GRE, by the time I collected enough seeds to plant a real tree outside of the app, I was one year into graduate school and that was a pretty cool moment. (I definitely would have accumulated enough hours work before that if I used the app EVERY time I did work or studied)
I recommend this to my friends and family! We need more trees in the world, more time applying ourselves to meaningful work, (and less time on our cellphones.)

title: Perfect for students who just can’t focus!
body:
I’m a high school student, and I use this app when I have to study or take notes. For those of you who aren’t interested in reading a really long review, here’s my summary: 

This app wards off distractions and is a perfect way to keep yourself focused! 
The in-app purchases are not at all necessary (I haven’t felt even the slightest bit tempted to spend money), so you should definitely give this app a try! 

Here’s the longer explanation:

I originally heard about Forest from a friend after I told her how I was struggling to avoid getting distracted. It seemed like every time I tried to sit down and start working, a new notification popped up on my screen- whether it was a text message, an email, or a game alert- and I couldn’t stay focused.

I love this app because it helps me stay on track and get work done. With the adorable game design aside, using this app is just super gratifying! Of course, the tiny trees are cute and it’s fun to grow your own forest, but this app isn’t just aesthetically pleasing: it’s extremely functional. It allows me to focus, avoid distractions, and succeed in school. 

There’s nothing you need to buy in order to use the app, so just download it and give it a try! If it doesn’t work for you, then you can just delete it, but it might end up being super useful for you, just as it was for me!

title: $2 for this type of productivity is worth it
body:
Love the app. 

The Home Forest screen is good. Only thing I would change is I’d like the ability to edit my own forest/garden. Almost like a game appeal so that it’s a bit more fun. You can still do everything you’re doing (because I like seeing my productivity) and add this feature as another tab after “year” if you catch what I’m putting down

The timeline is super cute and I like the fact that I can see a detailed view because I’ve tagged my tree to what I’m doing. 

I love that I can see my friends but I hate that I can only see what they’ve been doing on that day only. Again I’d love for everyone to be able to edit their forests and for their friends to view it too. 

Achievements are cool, I haven’t unlocked any yet. It’s only my 2nd day out here 

The inventory in the store is selective and I love the choice of trees. I’d add more sound choices and I think bushes should be worth less than trees lol

It’s so cool you can actually help plant real trees with the coins you built up in the game! 

The news tab is well organized and appealing to look at. Everything about this app has a very “fun” appeal, it’s easy to use and it all ties together ☺️

title: Wish I knew this existed when I was in school!
body: Throughout my entire academic career, I’ve never been the type of student who could study for 6-8 hours a day. I got really anxious and resorted to checking my phone to avoid studying. I’m currently preparing for my licensing exams and desperately needed something to help me focus on studying and more importantly off my phone! I saw someone on Reddit recommend this app and figured that it’s $2, it wouldn’t hurt. To my surprise, this app has kept me accountable with studying! I follow the pomodoro method (4 25-min sessions with 5 min breaks in between). With each 25 min session, I plant a little cedar tree and my goal is to have 4 trees in 1 study session. Definitely wish I knew about this app sooner!

title: Great app, currency problem
body: I really like this app. It has a clean, easy to understand design, and the look of the trees you "plant" go well with it. I also like how the app shows your app use sessions in a virtual forest which is fun to look at. However, I feel like it takes too much currency to plant one real tree. You need 2500 in-app coins for a real tree to be planted. I tend to use the app for shorter sessions (15-30 minutes), but you get few coins per session (I get 4 coins for 10 minutes and around 20 for 30 minutes. Though this won't stop me from using the app, maybe there could be free "powerups" you can get for free, possibly by watching ads, that will allow you to receive more coins per session. Still, the app is great.

title: The best pomodoro timer
body: I have ADHD & the pomodoro technique is a god sent for me but it’s hard to find a timer or a system that will really help keep me focused. THIS is the app! I’ve used Forest in the past & then drifted and used a dozen other timers for the pomodoro technique but I always come back to forest. And now I’m here to stay! This app has everything you need to use the pomodoro technique in a way that works for you. You can set timers for 10 minutes, 20 minutes, to 60 minutes and everything in between! You can schedule your breaks and use labels and make notes on your tasks as you do them! It’s so flexible and perfect and I love the Google Chrome extension as well so I can use it on my Mac & my iPhone with no added cost! I love seeing my forest grow and the options to buy different trees and things as well! Work hard enough and Forest will plant a real tree for you! 10/10 everyone should use this app!

author: lulumewmew

title: Very Useful!
body:
Incredibly useful app, helps me stay on task! I’ve recommended it to friends, and they’ve told me they like it too. The different types of plants are not only really cute, they provide a nice incentive to keep you going. The option to plant real trees with the coins you’ve earned is also really great. It’s really easy to look back on all your different forests, and you can even connect with friends to compare, if you’re the competitive type ;^) Granted, you still need the self control to open the app and stick to it in the first place, but that’s not the app’s responsibility, haha.

Smooth design, some customizability (phrases to motivate or keep you in check while you work), reminders, and even ambience. Forest is my go-to whenever I’m studying!

If you go the whole time without using your phone the tree will grow to full size. However, if you use your phone then your tree will die. You get coins for every full grown tree you have that can be used for planting a tree in real life! What is better than being productive while helping the environment at the same time?! You can also collect different types of trees and build a colorful forest all your own.🖤👍🏼🌎

title: My productivity has grown
body:
I usually don’t buy apps, but this one is worth it! I am a very task driven person, and being able to see a concrete thing being accomplished by setting time aside to be productive helps me not give in to picking up my phone. I love the little trees you can see that you’ve built over time, and that eventually you can build a real life tree!

The only criticism I have is that I think it takes way too many coins to buy new digital trees or a real one. I understand it’s expensive to plant a new tree and they make money by people buying things to make them get more digital currency, but it seems hard to set your goals to plant a real life when the goals seem unattainable. 

Regardless, this is definitely the best productivity app I’ve used! Worth the $2!

title: Keeps You Accountable
body:
This app simultaneously irritates me and doesn’t, because it does its job so well! You set the timer as to how long you want to focus on something and a tree starts growing. If you close the app your tree will die. The only downside to it is now I can’t use my phone to procrastinate work. Oh, and, you can’t really change your music while growing a tree because leaving the app kills it. I like the in app sounds, too, they’re peaceful. You can mute them if you like, but I find myself listening to the bird chirping anyways.

Long story short, I love it because it keeps me from getting distracted! 
(And you grow a cute tree)

Sometimes, when I’m doing homework and I need a break, I can’t stop the timer and the break time is counted as my studying time. I would love a break time function! I also think you should make this app more like a game. I love games and it’s the reason why I downloaded this app. You should add levels, character shops, more rewards, maybe competition to motivate people, motivation quotes, more items in shops, studying tips, functions that help concentration like to do lists, and make sure the features or functions that are new are not distractions and helpful to make the app fun and motivating. body:
I learned about this app through numerous study blogs on Tumblr and Instagram. I noticed a lot of students who run those blogs use Forest to help them focus when working on assignments and studying.

Out of curiosity, I downloaded this app and tried it myself. As a graduate student, I love this app. It allows me to set a specific time which correlates to a different tree that you plant. The cute graphics makes me motivated not to use my phone while on this app because it will kill my tree if I exit out of it. I’ve noticed I have been less distracted during those chunks of time I set on Forest. To all students who have trouble staying motivated and focused, try Forest out! :)

title: Love this app, but here’s my only complaint
body:
So experience wise, i think it’s great. The only thing i would change is how the tiles form with more trees you plant. Because the tiles keep growing at a rate higher than the amount of trees you plant, your forest is always looking emptier than it should, leaving you feeling unsatisfied.

You could make the argument that the empty tiles incentivizes the users to plant more trees, but I’d wager that users will most likely use the app longer if they’re able to consistently feel that their forest is jampacked with trees, and not sparsely potted. If you’re a designer for the app reading this, hope this influences your decision to update the algorithm for the tiles. :)

title: Thanks
body: I get distracted very easily (I have ADHD and chronically poor time management skills), and this app has been so helpful for me. Sometimes, you just need that little push to get yourself started on a task, and when you know that it’s not going to be endless, and that in 25 minutes or so you can take a break, it makes it seem much more doable. That’s the best way to get anything done—break it into bite-sized pieces. Sometimes, just starting a timer on Forest is enough to get me started on a task that I would not have started otherwise. Also, I like the calm ambience of the app, and the cute trees and other plants that you can earn. I also like that I can use the app on my computer as well (on Chrome). Thank you!

title: Review as requested by app.
body:
TOP LINE: Meh, so far. It looks pretty. It’s stable. It’s cheap. Poor user support and tutorial. Limited use compared to other “Pomodoro” type apps.  Buy if curious. Skip if you’re happy with your system.

PRO: the app (1) looks pretty and (2) is stable within the current version of iOS (12.x.x). (3) Reasonable one-time price for most features.

CON: (1) very weak tutorial. Much seems to be figure out as you go. (2) Poor user accessible support. Ex: App Settings -> FAQs -> blank page with spinning circle. Waited for a full minute. Still spinning. (3.) Arbitrary request for review instead of, “How are we doing?”  I’ve seen other apps, in their tutorial, mention they’d really appreciate a review but they don’t interrupt your workflow.

NEUTRAL: I wish Apple didn’t restrict putting specific apps on the Whitelist. That would have been a great boon if possible. That said, I’d imagine the developers are more frustrated about that than I am.

So that’s my review as requested.

Hopefully, I’ll learn how to get more out of this app and will update my review at that point.

title: Truly and brilliantly unique, Forest is a must
body:
It brings together two vastly different ideas that are perfectly suited to empower the other.

Forest helps you spend less time on your phone unlike anything out there. Everyone suffers from a varying degree of cell phone addiction and we all know we need to cut back. 

With Forest, it’s simple. You plant a virtual tree on your phone for a set amount of time, if you use your phone before the time is up, you kill your tree 😳. Or you can wait another 15 minutes and the tree thrives. Still, so what? The trees aren’t real... right? Wrong! The less time you waste on your phone, the more your trees grow, the more REAL TREES ARE PLANTED. 

That’s right, save up enough of your in game currency and Forest’s partner organization Trees for the Future will plant a real living tree. So we all spend less time on social media, YouTube, and Candy Crush... more with the people in our lives who matter, and hundreds of thousands of trees are being planted as a result.

What are you waiting for?

title: Excellent way to gamify productivity
body:
The reward system in Forest really helps to motivate me to remain focused during work sessions. 

I’m giving only four stars because I dislike most of the tree illustrations—apart from the default tree and bush, all other tree illustrations appear childish and have toys or other debris hanging from the branches like Christmas decorations.  

I would love to see a less light-hearted approach taken with some of the unlockable tree types that caters more to mature audiences or those who enjoy realism in gaming.

As a home gardener, I would also enjoy reading interesting facts about the chosen specie of tree if they to appear on the “success” popup that appears if a tree is successfully grown.

This app is cheap and useful! I recommend it.

body: this app isn’t going to solve absolutely all of your problems if you’re a procrastinator like me- but it definitely helps! forest is a fun, cute, and encouraging way to get you off of your phone for certain periods of time (all of which you can customize). it’s worth the money honestly- and another cool feature that i loved was- you cant buy your way through it. after you purchase the app- there’s only two “in-app purchases” but both of which have very little effect on your tree growing and just give you little boosts of coin for new trees (i really love this feature as i didn’t want to feel as if the company wanted my money more than actually being a productivity app💕). i do wish that there were different kinds of bushes (10-15 -maybe 20- minute reward)- but that’s just a tiny detail ☺️ otherwise!! i really love the app and the concept it’s pushing💗

title: Great way to focus and get stuff done
body:
Its a great app if you need to get anything done, work, sleep, or just can’t put down your phone, it works very well. Seeing the amount of trees you’ve grown over the month is very satisfying and actually quite difficult/heartbreaking to kill trees, I haven’t killed one yet. A few notes though: there isn’t a way to end a timer if you got all your work done, meaning even if you have everything done, you still have to either wait for the tree, or kill the tree. I wish there was a good way to get the work done, maybe change it for a different tree, but something so you don’t have to kill the tree but don’t have to wait 20 minutes.

A few quick things about the app;

Parents:
This is not a good way to make your child get work done as they still have the choice to get out and will get out if this is against their will. I am not a condoner of things like OurPact, there are better ways to control your child and let them get their work done

Students/anyone else:
This app is a great way to stay encouraged and not have the distraction of your own phone, I count computer games as killing the tree though, so you set your own rules and get down to getting your work done!

I wish you the best of luck!

title: So helpful!
body:
This app has provided me all the incentive I need to stay focused. In this world of nearly constant connectivity, having the app encourage me to ignore my phone has also helped me put aside emails, other side tasks, and in-office distractions in favor of writing. I first used this app during a writing workshop and got so much done that I decided to incorporate it into my daily writing practice, and I have not been disappointed with the results! Thank you! 

I do wish that the app played a sound when a tree has grown. I also wish that there was a way to allow the app to turn off notifications, because if I leave my phone screen up so I can see when the tree is done, I also see my text messages, emails, etc. come in. title: Dramatic increase in productivity!
body: In my case, the phone has always been a huge distraction of mine. Forest, utilizes evidence based methods of productivity, known as the Pomodoro technique, that many successful people have utilized to accomplish their goals. This technique provides a strict study schedule to follow (25 work, 5 min break, repeat), which not only helps you stay focused for greater lengths of time but the app itself also applies its own twist on this technique by one, making it harder to get distracted by using your phone, and two: allowing you to see the fruits of your labor in an aesthetic and rewarding manner. The one dollar it costs is more than worth it. P. S. I’m also studying for the MCAT.

title: Effective but can be improved
body:
I’ve been using the app for a few years and love how it motivates me to stay on task. That said, I think it’s time for this app to do far more to really facilitate better focus.

The Pomodoro Technique is effective for a lot of people because you can move between productive time and small breaks. The way this app works, however, is that if you want to plant a tree to its full size you need to focus for two hours straight otherwise it dies or you get a small, not as cute looking tree stub. Frankly, I don’t know anyone nowadays who does that. That’s 1/12 of the whole day already. As a student, I need breaks like most people do. Other productivity apps have this option and I think the devs should consider incorporating a Pomodoro Technique option when you decide to focus for longer than 25 minutes.

This is frustrating because I slaved away to earn 1000 coins on buying a cute tree that I can’t focus long enough for. To contextualize, you get 5-6 coins per 20min study and the number of coins earned increases the longer you study in one session. You can imagine how many hours I spent with this app to buy a few trees. These days though, the shrubs are clearly more valuable because the focus-time for those is 20 min at most. 

Please consider incorporating a Pomodoro Technique mechanic. 

Just to note, I suggested this in-app but received no response which is why I’m finally posting a review.

title: Forest is my new favorite app
body: I’ll be honest: I’m a student, and I spend WAY TOO MUCH time on my phone. It is a major distraction and I can feel myself getting sucked in but was having trouble ever convincing myself to just put it down and get stuff done. I never buy apps (I only go for the free versions of everything) — I literally just paid actual money for my first app ever earlier this year, after owning a smart phone for the past 6 years. This app is well worth the $2. It helps motivate me to stay off my phone when I’m practicing (music student) or trying to get work done. My boyfriend also has the app and we’ve made rooms to help us both focus simultaneously a few times but I’m hoping to get more friends to buy it so I can do this more. It is the perfect combination of motivating and making you feel disappointed in yourself if you slip up 😂 Seriously, it’s so satisfying to watch your forest grow and it’s very easy to use. You can also create new “tags” for why the trees were planted, which I love (I made one specific for practicing which is also a good way to help me keep track of how much practice I do). I had tried setting time limits for screen time/social media through iPhone settings but I’ve already started ignoring that....but Forest is so much more convincing and I just can’t let my sweet little trees die lol. Overall I love love this app and wish I’d heard of it sooner! It’s a relief to have something really hold me accountable for my screen time!

title: Good enough but could be much better
body:
Effective for keeping your phone away from distractions. With the chrome extension, this app is good for fighting distractions. 
Good for tracking “focus time”. However, the tree reward is not really much of a reward. Not sure if it’s worth the 1.99 price tag especially because the app can’t sync automatically with the chrome extension so if you’re using both at the same time it doubles the amount of time recorded scaling back the feature that made it useful in the first place.

+5 stars for effectiveness — gives you a goal for focusing and tracking/visualizing focus times
-1 Star for not syncing 
-2 Stars for 1.99 price tag and stingy coin rewards: need 500 to buy a tree but focusing for 30-40 minute intervals (optimal focus times) got you only 10-20 coins encouraging users to do in app purchases. For a paid app, this seems greedy.

title: Got it for the cute interface, stayed for the productivity increase
body:
I’ve only been using this app for around a week, but it’s already cut down on the amount of time I absent-mindedly use my phone.  Initially I got it mostly for how cute the little forests look, I’ll admit, and for the fact that earning enough in-game currency lets you plant a REAL tree!  Now, it even helps me keep my phone away when going to bed (a big hurdle for me), since I set it to the longest break setting (2 hr) as I’m laying down.

Obviously, how people use their phone-free time will vary.  For me, it’s allowed (forced?) me to eat my meals uninterrupted by scrolling, and I’ve begun creating art more frequently again (as I would always get stuck in the loop of “looking for inspiration” on my phone and then never actually getting to the art).

Honestly this is the best app I’ve ever paid money for (and one of the very few I shelled out cash for period), and it’s been completely worth it.  If you spend upwards of 4 hours a day on your phone (like I was doing), I highly recommend taking this app into consideration!

title: Good app, helps me focus
body: This is a good app. I have been using it since 2015 and I am pretty satisfied with it. The new tree/bush species are beautiful and having different species really does motivate me to keep planting my garden and to earn more coins so I can unlock a new species. I have huge issues with wasting time on my phone and time management due to executive function issues and mental illness and this app has helped me a lot as a college student. The app can’t force you to do your work, but it CAN force you to take a break from your phone, and that ten minute break can be really, really useful when you are stuck. I also love that you can input custom tags to  track and categorize different categories of planting time (sleeping, class time, homework time, etc) and that you can see your progress on the graph. The options to keep the screen on, track exceeded time, and ding or send a notification when the tree is done are also really helpful for me. My only suggestion would be to show us a better preview of what a tree will look like when planted for a shorter time before we pay coins to unlock it. For example, the preview image for the apple tree shows a big apple tree with apples and a picnic basket, but once you buy the tree you realize that you can’t get it to look that pretty unless you are able to plant it for a longer time, like 40 minutes+. If you are only planting trees for less time, like 30 minutes or less, then a lot of the trees look kind of the same and they are not as colorful or as big as pictured in the store, because they don’t “grow” to look like the picture. Overall I love your app and would absolutely recommend it to anyone who is struggling to break away from their phone. Thank you, Forest app developers! ❤️🌳

title: Cheating and no breaks
body:
I like the app and use it often but I find there are two major problems: first, the leaderboards and earning points for doing so. I use this app honestly when I’m really focusing, but people who choose to can log onto Facebook or whatever on a computer or another phone and rack up points, climbing the leaderboards for nothing.
Secondly, I wish there was a “break” option during focus sessions. I find I do well with intervals of focus and break like 20/5 minutes or 30/10. The app rewards long uninterrupted focus times and sometimes that’s just more tiring than efficient. Would be nice to get the same amount of points for a two hour max session with a couple 5-10 minute breaks in between.

title: Fun Incentive to Stay Focused
body: LOVE this app! I have ADD and tend to procrastinate the important things I need to do at work and social media is the perfect tool to do so- however this app has been super helpful with staying off of it. The premise of it may sound cheesy or like it wouldn’t be that motivating but it’s become a game for me to see how long I can stay off of it. And the fact that you get to plant real trees once you’ve earned enough coins to do so is 1. personally a good enough reason to pay for the app and 2. an even bigger motivation to stay off my phone while it’s turned on or else it’ll “kill the tree” (just on the app) that I’m in the middle of “growing.” Definitely recommend to anyone who needs help with self-discipline!

title: Keeps me from falling in YouTube hole
body: I recently bought this app and am not disappointed. I grow trees at work, which helps keep me from using my phone to procrastinate. I also LOVE the rain sounds, because I work in an open concept space. Even though they pump white noise through speakers on our floor, I can still hear people nearby clacking away on their keyboards with their fake nails, coughing incessantly, or complaining. With this app, I focus on my work, and listen to soothing rain sounds to drown out the rest of that noise. At home, I plant my forest instead of falling into a YouTube vid watching, hours long session spiral. It stops me from wasting hours and keeps me thinking about what I really want to do. I do waste a little time picking which tree I’m going to plant next though...love this app. My only gripe is I haven’t quite figured out how to use the tag feature. Doesn’t really matter too much to me though. Suggestions to add in might be more achievements or “easter egg” type items for staying focused for a certain amount of time or for planting a certain tree so many time etc. Items could be treasure chests , bonus point elixirs, or just an extra fun item to put in the forest for free (like an animal or statue or something. Just some thoughts...Anyway, I highly recommend!

title: Have used app for 2.5 years, and I love it
body: I’ve been using the Forest app for the past 2.5 years, and it’s survived the chopping block this whole time. Being a college student with ADHD, this app has helped me so much because there are times where I can get distracted by Instagram or FB for hours. I love the concept of planting trees and being able to see how much you’ve stayed focus for a day, week, month, or year. I also love that you have the ability to help plant a real tree. That being said, I do wish I was able to see the timer on my lock screen, so that by just turning on my phone I would be able to see the time left. I usually leave my phone on silent or do not disturb while studying, so I don’t get the notification that my tree has been planted.

body: It’s $2, and I’m usually not a person to pay for an app. After all, I like to not be distracted by my phone. Why would I pay to be distracted? I have trouble getting motivated to get out of bed sometimes, but because I want the cutest forest of the day, I find a reason to stay focus, like getting ready, and it feels like a major accomplishment. title: Helps you stay on task!
body: This app is good for those who unconsciously move their hand to their phone and then get distracted for 4 hours! In other words, someone like me... If you have a heart and do not have the audacity to kill a pure, growing, virtual plant, then give this app a shot. It helps me stay away from mindlessly going on social media just to check “something”. I get sidetracked very easily and I’ve been wanting to improve that habit because I end up being less productive. Unlocking my phone and witnessing my little seedling growing seems so pure that I allow it to grow. (Most of the time. There had been some incidents.) If you’re like me and are easily distracted and you lose focus often on what needs to be done, by all means try this app out if you lack the mental stability of ignoring your apps.

title: Hands down one of the BEST productivity app!!! OMG!!
body: I friggin LOVVVVVEEEEEE THIS APP!!! I used to use a regular pomodoro app that just automatically do 25 mins with 5 mins breaks. I’ve used it for a long time until I got introduced to the forest app. I didn’t even bother with the free version, I just bought this app and it was the best $0.99 I’ve ever spent!! It’s literally the best way to gamify your life in a smart way! I absolutely love this new updates with the new graphs and pie charts, like I can’t stop gushing about this app. I’ve been consistently using this app for a good month now and it is going to be in my collection for life. My only tiny itty bitty wish is that I could have the option to use the 12 hour timeline clock rather than the 24 hour military time clock. Other than that, this app is perfection and I 10/10 recommend this to everyone. If I could give this app a 100/100 stars I would!!! Keep it up Forest App crew!!

title: Love This App, Would Recommend
body: Well-balanced mix of gamification, environmentalism, and social aspects. The art is also really wonderful and cute! Makes my pomodoros feel effortless, and gives me motivation to do work with friends. I like that it takes a significant amount of time for me to gain enough coins to get more trees, it makes the purchases feel important. I also like getting friends trees when they host the session. I do think the social connection could use a little work — I have never gotten a pop up when my friends send group requests, and have always needed to fill out the code, which really increases the effort as you need to connect for each tree. Regardless, I think the positives of this app highly outweigh that shortcoming, and would recommend this app to anyone wanting to try and keep a healthy work-break balance.

title: Essential for modern life
body:
This app allows users to redefine the way they use their phone: make your phone use intentional and your relationship with your phone will change. 

I am always looking to plant trees—which means I’m thinking ahead about how much I actually need to use my phone. Then, if I find that I do need to use my phone, but I’d still rather grow the tree, I hold on to that objective until the tree has grown. I’m using my phone because I want to, not because it’s there or because I can.

author: Hdaks w

title: Satisfying and Full of Potential
body:
I don’t write nearly as many reviews for apps that I enjoy as I should. I had to for this one. While I’d enjoy a few added things, they’d be additional sources of happiness that are not necessary to love this app. I’d enjoy different themes (seasonal would be apropos as well as dark for those of us with migraines and eye strain) and an ability to temporarily increase our yield of points (I’d be good with watching a few ads in exchange for that). Maybe the option to have a quote when you finish a tree would be a cool way to end your session; you could even choose to get an expanded quote pack on success or wisdom or happiness or pop culture for coins or as an in-app purchase. 

Having a place to look over quotes you enjoyed would be nice. Being able to post a picture to show what you did while you were focused would be cool. While I often write on my computer while I have the timer up, sometimes I spend the time with my family or I do some art. It would be cool to show the fruits of my labors instead of just having a tag in those instances. If having a “photo view” of your forest would be an added purchase option, that would be fine too.

I’d like a few more sounds added, but I have faith they’ll be added to like the trees are. I really like that the devs are adding new trees and bushes, and it makes me kind of push myself to keep going. But it’s also very frustrating; I feel the price increase per new plant or sound purchase is too steep. I’m not a huge fan of that. I mean, at some point it’ll cost more to get access to a kind of tree or bush or sound than it would to actually plant a tree IRL. That’s... super frustrating.

I love the idea of rooms. I think it would be cool if there was some sort of boost, or reward for working together. It can be a bit of a hassle to arrange it but if you could plant a certain kind of tree (and after doing
it as a group a certain amount of times, you can plant that kind solo), or if you get more coins per minute, or maybe if you get a wildcard tree, that would be great. 

I also like the idea of rewarding app fidelity. That maybe if you plant every day for a week, you get to plant one tree of any variety regardless of it it’s unlocked or not. Or you get half an hour of listening to a sound you haven’t fully unlocked. Or if you check in every day to “water” your investment with your forest, you get some kind of reward. I am motivated to a ridiculous extent by achievements and streaks (I have a 550 day Duolingo streak as I type) and the better the reward system is implemented, the more likely I am to feel invested in the app and loyal, to an extent. Once I kind of work through the existing rewards and I’ve already reached the cap of having five trees planted IRL I may well get bored with this app and move on to something else, despite really enjoying the layout and idea, because if progress is so slow it’s barely noticeable at all, and I’ve already achieved most of what I can, I’m going to see if other apps have popped up that can offer me something more engaging that has new and more extensive rewards and achievements to go through, to challenge myself.

The more this also functions also as a memory holder (with photos and memories and quotes) the less likely I am to eventually drop it. If it needs to stay very streamlined as it is, then broader achievements or a less steep curve in terms of adding trees to the collection would be great.

I really like being able to add tags with the upgrade; I can look back and see if I was reading or writing and what genre it was, see at a glance what kind of month I was having. 

A note would be that I wish the reward system worked a bit differently. You’re not incentivized to spend more time being productive. While I love that it doesn’t make it not worth your time to use the app for short periods of time, it also would be better for me if I had three sets of 20min sessions instead of one 60min one. I think having a few idealized time slots around half an hour apart is a good idea, and it would be a nice little perk for the nerds in the room who took the time to do the math and figure out just how many coins you’re getting per minute after each 5min increase is accounted for. But it feels sort of random and haphazardly done right now, no rhyme or reason to it, there’s no pattern to it. Does the app want me to log more time? Which, is what most apps what? If so, then why don’t I get more coins per minute if I commit to a long session instead of a shorter one? It doesn’t really make sense to me, and I’m sure there are other people who were trying to work out how to maximize their system that became puzzled and perplexed about it.

I like that there is added detail the longer you stick with the app. You have a smaller and less detailed tree at half an hour than you do at an hour, etc. I think that is really snazzy.

I feel like just... a little more customization would be cool. Being able to pick having leaves instead of grass under your trees, or pine needles, or moss, or even have like a cotton candy dreamscape backdrop or theme for it if you want. There may be people who would love the first week of April to have a cotton candy grass theme and only plant cotton candy trees that week. Or if you’re happy it’s officially autumn you can do an autumn leaf theme.

Having a little bird or squirrel or something be able to perch in a branch now and then would be cool. Like, if you plant 50 bushes in a week, you get a lady bug, you can choose to place it somewhere on a bush in the forest for the week.

Also something I’d like would be a remembrance tree. My Mom has cancer so when she has bad days, I plant her favorite kind of tree, because I’m thinking of her. But, if she died, I’d want to memorialize that in some way other than just tagging one tree. Having a Memory Tree would be nice.

I really like the app. I hope it grows. It has a lot of potential; I’m excited to see where it goes. There’s a lot that could be done here.

title: love it
body:
honestly, i love this app so much. it helps me stay focused and forces me to stay off my phone. With my struggles with ADHD, I just need some motivation and discipline to help me get started and this is the perfect program to help me through that. there are other apps very similar to this one that are free, but I would recommend spending the .99 to buy this one because the money actually goes to contributing to a good cause - by planting actual trees. 

there are only a few parts that make it difficult at times. sometimes i need to do a homework assignment but i need a photo of a sheet of paper or take notes from my browser online, and i cannot do that while running the app without killing the tree. it would be really helpful to have a white list to allow certain apps or websites. or maybe you could just implement a feature to allow for an upload of a picture or screenshot so you can use it as a reference while using the app. While there is the option to work with the phone, it is easy to become distracted if I am able to access everything.

Another possible feature that would be helpful / beneficial could be to set some sort of goal for the day/ week? A lot of times I forget about the app and struggle until I force myself to go back to it; I tend to use it in bursts (many hours in the span of 3 days but nothing for two weeks). If it could send a notification like “hey, do you want to do xyz so that you can meet your goal?” and then you can get extra coins or something if you meet the goal. 

However, overall this app is wonderful, works great, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone that needs to focus and is motivated by collecting cute things haha

title: A modest, but wonderful app.
body:
I’ve owned this app for about a year and a half. I’m trying to write a book and Forest has helped me immensely in this regard. Previous attempts have always ended fizzled out, either because of lack of time or inspiration. Since February 2018 I’ve been using Forest as a means to take time and focus on my writing. I use the Pomodoro technique of 25 minutes of pure focused work and use Forest to track this.

I now have over 90,000 words and while I still have a ways to go, for the first time ever I feel that I am reaching my potential as a writer. I don’t normally write app reviews, but Forest has been such a great part of my writing process that I felt it deserved five minutes of my time to praise it.

title: Put your phone down!
body: I love this app. It’s super fun to pick a tree each time so it doesn’t feel like I’m being deprived of phone time or getting tsk-tsked about my usage. It’s very customizable and flexible so I can tweak everything to help me get the most out of it. The timer lets you set your time anywhere from 15-120 minutes, which is a very useful range. Ambient sound is an available option during each planting and you can even change sounds mid-tree without harming your growth. For each successful tree you receive coins to buy new trees, contribute to a real-life forest, or unlock new ambient sounds. I use the app for myself, to keep me off my phone during work time, dinner, or family time, but my kids also like to use it. I set a timer and turn on ambient sound for my little one’s nap time or we set a timer so they grow a tree during chore time. It’s been incredibly useful to my whole family.

title: Increases productivity
body:
Forest has helped me stay present over dinner, at work and in my leisure time. I didn't realize how much I actually look at my phone until I started setting time frames to leave it alone and allow trees to grow. I've even scored one real tree planted so far, which is cool. My friends who are with me in body appreciate it. My friends and family in mind who text me do not. I'm okay with that. I've read four books this month and been more efficient at life.

I would like to see some upgrades such as an option to save different tree types as labeled for different activities (cherry blossom for studying, birdhouse for cleaning...etc.) and seeing a large grid of all trees ever with a zoom function. Graphics could be better. However, it serves the purpose for which it was created. Recommended!

Update: I’d also like the option to grow trees for up to 8 hours at a time. Why the limit to 2 hours?

title: Guilt Motivation Works!
body:
I absolutely love this app. In fact, it’s so effective that it almost has the opposite effect – it’s addicting! That being said, it is extremely effective In that it does really make you think whenever you mindlessly pick up your phone of what you’re doing. The immediate guilt trip of having a tree that might die if you don’t immediately stop using your phone is perfect and usually all the reminder you need.

What I will say is that you can circumvent the app if you’re really dedicated. It lets you navigate away for a few seconds at a time, so if you just want to send a quick text response, you can usually get in a word or two and send it and then get back to the app before the tree dies. However, the alternative is to kill the tree every time you accidentally open your phone and navigate away from the app, Which is a little much, so I think it’s just up to us to be responsible adults and use the app the way it’s meant to be used.

The positive reinforcement of being able to buy new trees and shrubs, and see all the variety the more time you spend focused, is Probably the thing that gives it return value. If you were just punished for not focusing, it would be easy to stop using the app. However, the creative and fun new options keep me interested, and I even find myself starting themes for the week or the month with different types of trees!

The only wish I have for this app is that you were able to grow trees in specific places on your grid. It would be so cool to be able to start a row or pattern of different types of trees or shrubs, and honestly give even more motivation to spend more time focused. However, that may just be me being a little bit OCD. It’s still cool when they pop up in random places.

Certainly worth $2 to gain hours of motivated focus!

title: As Effective as You Are Honest With It
body:
Forest has been a good tool for preserving both my productivity and phone battery. The pie chart it provides (after you tag each session with a category) also helps break down where your time on Forest is going. 

As a more competitive person, having a ranking system between my friends and I is helpful. Having more trees and bushes is something I enjoy looking forward to; the last update was a fun experience. While I understand the idea of an increasing 100 coin cost with each tree bought, I found myself taking a mental L after prices started going beyond 1000.

Otherwise animated trees. That’d be amazing, and I wouldn’t mind earning a ton for coins for those.

Something that might be fun to see in the future are personal challenges. I enjoy the achievements and their rewards offered by the app (i.e. X consecutive days rewards and X many days’ worth of focus time for coins), and it would be nice to see more of them. Reward variety in the form of exclusive trees/bushes or planting actual trees is also something that’d be cool to have.

TL;DR: effective app. More trees (animated trees? ✨) and bushes to purchase/earn and more achievements with rewards would be cool.

title: Excellent app with one minor exception
body: Forest is an excellent Pomodoro-style app for blocking out time for tasks. The only thing I would change about the app is to allow for time blocks below 10 minutes. Sometimes I have tasks I do not even want to spend 10 minutes on, and I think a five minute or even a one minute timer would motivate me to get those tiny tasks done. These are the kinds of tasks that do not benefit from overlearning, so setting a ten minute time on them doesn’t make sense. You might ask why set a timer for them anyway—but sometimes it’s about tricking the mind to just get started. That’s what this app is great for: tricking your mind to get stuff done.

author: Aaaaaahhhhhhhhhh!!!!!!!!!!

title: Great app!
body:
I have ADHD and this app has been incredibly helpful! It’s greatly improved my ability to stay on task and off my phone.

My biggest problem when working is I don’t realize I’ve gotten distracted. Before it was easy to just pick up my phone and spend hours not doing anything.

Now when I pick up my phone I see the forest app I realize I’m distracted. It’s an amazing mental stop and is usually enough to get me to go back on task. 

If not the little trees are cute and I know it sounds silly but I don’t want to kill a tree to check reddit. If you do kill a tree it also will put a dead tree in your forest. 

You can also unlock new trees with coins. You get coins by putting more trees in your forest so it’s kinda a motivational thing to focus more to unlock more trees. (You can also unlock sounds to listen to while you focus.) 

The app is a great tool for anyone who gets mindlessly distracted and doesn’t realize. It’ll keep your phone from being a distraction point at a minimum. (It’s not magic unfortunately and won’t stop other distractions).

If you’re the kinda person who deliberately procrastinates or realizes that you are distracted it may or may not help. It depends how much you can bring yourself to care about the app. 

It’s helped me an incredible amount and I am thankful for the app.

title: so good for focusing!
body:
let me just say that this is hands down the BEST app i have ever paid money for.  at first when i bought this app, last year, i wasn’t really in the right mindset to make the most of it.  i didn’t really use it and felt no motivation to use it.  but this year i decided i wanted to be more productive, and not waste time on my phone.  when the new school year started, i had a system: get home from school. eat a snack.  browse social media for 10-15 minutes MAX.  then i’d go to my room and open the forest app, and set it to 25 minutes.  for 25 minutes i do nothing but the task i have in front of me, no distractions, ringer off.  when the 25 minutes are up, i set the break timer to 2-5 minutes, depending on how hard the task was.  during this time i get some water or a snack, stretch, do a mini workout (pull-ups are a quick one), answer any texts, or go outside for some fresh air.  then when my timer is up, i get back to work and do another 25 minutes.  and i keep doing this until i’m about halfway through with all of my work for the day, and i take a 10 minute break to really process the information i took notes on or just take a break.  then i get back to work and repeat the 25 minutes of work, 2-5 minute break cycle.  this system has COMPLETELY changed how i get my work done.  instead of procrastinating and doing it all last minute, or doing 2-3 hours with no breaks, i do a decent amount of work with enough break time in between that i don’t get too exhausted.  one thing if you try to use this method or something similar—while you’re on the break in between work sessions, i recommend NOT going through social media.  answering texts is fine, but i find that for me if i look at social media it’s very hard to go back to work, and i ignore the “get back to work!” notifications.  even if you don’t use this exact system, or something similar, i recommend taking a few breaks because it really does help you understand what you are actually doing.  my grades have gone up a lot after i started using the app for homework, and i have much more free time to do fun things once i’m done with all my homework.  i highly recommend this app to anyone who has work or homework they have to do, and anyone who has a phone and struggles with putting it down and not getting distracted.  i’m sorry this is such a long review, it’s the only review i’ve ever written for anything.  i just felt that people should know how amazing this app is and how it can completely change your life!  also as a bonus when you complete your 25 minutes or whatever time you set, you get credits which you can use to get new types of trees, or if you want you can use them to plant real trees in real life!  

in conclusion. BUY THIS APP :)

title: Honestly a game-changer
body:
Don’t get me wrong, my phone is a useful tool, and I wouldn’t necessarily say I’m addicted to it. However, it’s also a super easy way to waste time you don’t even realize you could be using on other things. I use Forest mostly in small increments, and it keeps me from picking up my phone whenever I have a few free minutes and get bored. Since I don’t actually need or want to be on my phone, the small motivation of growing little bushes and trees is enough for me to direct my attention elsewhere- and it turns out that those few free minutes throughout the day can translate into a lot of extra productivity!

Otherwise: initial download price might seem a bit high, but considering that they plant real trees if you make enough coins to buy the option, the $2 is warranted. Coin prices in the app are average, but payment per tree during the week is okay and you can make enough yourself with a little effort (I personally think you should make a little more per tree than they offer, but it’s not a bad amount either). The interface is simple and intuitive, the art is charming and stylistically uniform, and my favorite part- the white noise options- are incredibly helpful for studying and neither overly expensive or so complicated that they become distracting.

All in all, great app that I use frequently. $2 has never bought me so much extra productivity.

title: This app is a GODSEND
body:

I needed something to take my Sleaze level way down from Super Saiyan Sleaze God to, like, just a regular Super Saiyan Sleaze. 

One day, during my procrastination addiction, I was looking though some apps and I saw it: Forest-Stay Focused. I immediately felt drawn. “I’ll just keep procrastinating and sleazing it up while I check out this app,” I thought. Unbeknownst to my Sleazy Habits, this app would soon become the death them. I use it all the time and have gone from not studying or doing homework at all, to working on homework and studying for over 3 solid hours a day (and growing! As is my forest!). This app is awesome, and I can actually feel my Super Saiyan Sleaze Power leave me. Best $2 I ever spent. 

If you think about it, I’m only giving up like, a snickers bar and like, one or two 4-packs of Wrigley’s gum. Also, I can’t wait to unlock mushrooms and start sleazing it up with them.

title: Incredible and Effective

I was horribly addicted to Reddit. I was spending 5-6 hours scrolling my life away reading one forgettable post after another. I tried content blockers but addiction just made me delete them when I needed to mindlessly scroll. 

This app is different. The fact that it’s like a game where you can watch beautiful things grow and even make a real difference by planting a tree in the real forest is so motivating. Now when I start scrolling I plant a two hour tree so I can read, practice music, do yoga, or a multitude of other productive things. 

Thank you so much for creating a wonderful app! Looking forward to more trees and more updates in the future :) 

One suggestion. I think it’d be really cool if you could have a custom forest where you could pick and choose trees and bushes to decorate your own plot of land!

title: Incredible! I’m amazed.
body:
In the first stage, you ignore the app. You continue procrastinating and slacking, the app serving only as a reminder of your ideal, more focused self.

In the second stage, you open the app. You fail numerous times and your efforts come to little fruition, until finally one day, after a week of focus, you reach stage three. In this stage, you rely on the app to guide your focus. Things are actually getting done and you’re amazed at how such a simple thing has reigned in your potential for productivity. And the one day...

One day, you reach the fourth and penultimate stage. You no longer need the app. Simply having the icon on your phone is enough to deter you from using your precious time doing anything extracurricular... including even using the app. All focus had finally become internalized, and the app, being a mere external vehicle, also seems to waste your potential for focus.

In the final stage, your phone vanishes, app and all. I’ve obviously not reached this stage as I’m reviewing from my phone, but you get the point.

App really does work, if you’re willing to put in the work yourself. Otherwise, it’s useless.

title: Love it!! Please add forest animals
body:

Here’s my problem - I’ve unlocked almost everything except for a couple trees I really don’t like.  While I could just keep growing different combinations of trees and bushes, what I really wish I could do is to add forest animals. 

I’d like to be able to earn various forest animals to my existing forests, or maybe start with the animals some times and then add the trees, or add a couple trees and sprinkle animals in. For the shorter time frames smaller animals like birds, butterflies, bunnies, lizards, squirrels, bats, etc. and for the longer time animals like deer, elk, wild pigs, and other regular animals found in the forest. I think the animal options here are endless and also would really make the forests look cool.  The animals would just “grow” exactly like the trees and bushes do.  The animals should match the various kinds of trees that are available. Some regular, some tropical (for palm tree), etc. 

Any chance of animals coming soon?

Also the smaller animals should cost less coins and the bigger ones more coins. I find it annoying that currently the bushes cost the same as the trees. They are smaller and therefore shouldn’t cost the same as the larger trees.

title: Really helpful, would like more customization
body:
This really does keep me from getting distracted by my phone. I want the tree to grow and I am motivated not to hurt it. 

It also works as a timer. You can set it up beside your computer and see the tree grow until it's time for a break. This is a nicely visual method for those of us with terrible time sense, more useful than a numerical countdown.

The tree doesn't die instantly if you leave the app. You can switch away for about 3 seconds, which is important for me because I use my phone for music or audio books all day, and a few seconds is just long enough to switch radio stations or whatever. You can also use the lock screen and the camera safely, talk to Siri, and answer phone calls. So all the really important functionality is still available to me. 

I think the app would be a lot stickier if there were more options for customizing the forest besides unlocking tree types. I would like to arrange my trees and choose background colors and grass colors. I'd also like to be able to zoom in more to see my trees bigger. The Christmas trees were soooo cute and I wish I could keep them!

One interesting thing about the app is you can't just buy trees. You can only buy powerups that increase your rewards for using the app. In a way, that's frustrating, because I am impatient haha! But it genuinely motivates me more to use the app. I admire the creator for refusing to take the easy money and ensuring their app is as effective as possible.

title: Great app and idea, but could you consider adding this feature?
body:
Hello,

First off, I love this idea and the app is well designed and visually appealing, great job on that! If you could add the option to have an unlimited timer, and the ability to pause that timer, this app would be exceptional. I guess not so much a timer, and more of a stopwatch since it would be counting time forward. It would be really cool to have multiple trees grow in a day, maybe one tree every two hours or something. I like keeping track of how much time I spend studying, but I can't pause the app's timer if, for example, I want to grab a quick bite or use the bathroom. Maybe an option to not kill the tree if you exit the app would be nice, too. I understand that the point of the app is to get people to not use their phone and be productive, but some of us have note card apps on our phones (ex. Anki) that we use, and so I would want the time spent doing note cards on my phone to also count towards growing trees! 

So basically I'm asking for a stopwatch feature to the app, that would be amazing!

I highly recommend this app!

title: Engaging, creative and fun time mgmt tool
body:
I usually use an online Pomodoro timer to help me focus and stay on task. However on my new IPad I was unable to get their notifications plus I was still playing on my phone. As a first year medical student my new lifestyle is mainly studying. I needed a time management and focus tool that would help make studying less painful. 😩 I heard about Forest and was skeptical at first. I did not want to pay for the app since I am cheap and thought I could do it on my own using alternative ways. However I was not successful and decided to buy this app. Since purchasing Forest I have no regrets! 😊 I enjoy the ability to track and visually see my progress. I am a visual learner and am positively reinforced by the forest I am growing and enjoy earning money to unlock more features of the app. What sold me was the social impact of the app where you can plant a tree. Love it! 

Highly recommend and so worth the money spent. Would definitely buy it again.

I do wish there was an ‘allowed app’ feature or something, because I love to use this at work, but in my work team it’s pretty common to use texts to communicate, so I usually end up setting it for short 30 minute bursts, and then checking for team member texts. I get it would somewhat defeat the purpose of the app, but it really would make it more work friendly.

body:

I really wanted to give this app a 5 but I get the impression that the developer hasn’t fully considered Apple Watch use cases. The watch’s timer app is more practical to use than this for the time being.

title: Most adorable and fun way to beat procrastination
body: I use the Pomodoro technique (25 min focus, 5 min break, repeat) because I know myself and I will be paralyzed with procrastination anxiety if I remind myself “I need to study for 7 hrs today. That is 420 minutes.” Cutting the studying up into manageable chunks of time worked for me after I overcame the hardest part: starting. I needed the Forest app to incentivize me. The Forest app keeps track of the number of minutes I stayed focused for that day (reminds me that I am accomplishing more than I give myself credit for and 420 minutes of focusing is conquerable) along with keeping me accountable for my lovely garden filled with various whimsical trees. I cannot bear to see a dead tree caused by my utter lack of focus (exiting out of the app) in my lovely garden. Who would have known the guilt brought upon by killing a tree would be powerful enough to beat my years of procrastination? 5/5 great productivity app!

title: Growing with Forest: Technology and Procrastination
body: In a residential university setting, there are already so many distractions that I face. Most of my friends live just down the hall, social events occur every night, and activities in my dorm and clubs have become a part of my daily life. When I am finally able to escape this frenzy of socialization and sit down in the library, I confront the most tempting distraction of them all: my smartphone. I grew up in a generation of social media and personal technology, and in result, I have become somewhat dependent on the constant stream of information and entertainment available to me on my mobile device. From Twitter to Snapchat to Instagram, there are endless feeds to go through, videos to watch, and people to talk to. In the past, I have taken extreme measures in attempt to squelch my temptations toward the infinite scroll. I have turned off my phone, deleted applications, and logged out of accounts. Despite my efforts, I have always failed to honor my own restrictions, regardless of the fact that it is in my best interests. Because I had not found a solution to my tendency towards distraction, I decided to try ‘Forest,’ a focus-motivating iOS application for smartphones. Forest uses the symbol of a tree in order to motivate users to stop their phone use. When one uses Forest, one sets a timer on the app, and throughout the duration of the set time, a virtual tree grows. If one uses one’s phone as a timer is ongoing, the tree dies. In using Forest as a part of my student workflow, I found that its usability, aesthetic design, and conceptual design work well into my practice of study. Although I observed that the app helps me focus in times of high-intensity study, I will probably not use it in the future for relatively low-urgency schoolwork.

body: The cute little trees are just so adorable that I start wanting to put down my phone so I can unlock new ones! I am eagerly awaiting new trees to be added. The user interface is very simple and aesthetic. All in all it’s a great app; the only problem is that sometimes I run into situations where I plant a tree but then end up needing to use my phone for something (like if my mom calls or I have to look up something for homework) and can’t wait for the tree to finish. There is a feature where you can have the app continue counting time after the tree finshes growing, so you can work around the problem by planting a short-time tree and then just continuing to not disturb it. But it would be really great if there was some sort of pause feature, maybe with some limitation like not earning coins if you pause it so that people don’t take advantage of it to ‘cheat’ on their time. Or maybe something where you can erase or reset the time, so you don’t have to feel bad about killing a cute little tree when you actually legitimately needed to use your phone for a minute.

body:

What is clever with this app is that you can set a pomodoro timer and simultaneously “grow” a tree to create a forest. When that timer is up, take a break; a tree is grown after the timer and you receive coins. You can use these coins to plant real trees. So, this app is designed to increase your productivity and contribute to the environment. I hope this provides whomever is reading this review. 

This app is awesome. Go and download it!

title: Incredibly Useful Time-Management App
body:
I normally don’t write reviews, but this application deserves an exception. At first I thought it might be somewhat useful; I’ve not found that Forest is an integral and important part of my life. The minimal reward sequencing of Forest, planting a virtual “tree” when you’ve completed an adjustable time commitment to stay away from your phone is a friendly and positive reminder to avoid distraction. The fact that the Forest application actually plants trees when you’ve accrued enough focus currency makes this a wholly incredible idea. 

I would recommend it to anyone who finds themselves scrolling away valuable minutes and hours of their lives.

title: Really keeps me off of my phone
body:
A few years ago I downloaded this app on my tablet and loved it. So as soon as I got a device capable of installing the app again, I did! There is just something so rewarding about growing a tree while doing something I actually need to do. I have been known to turn it on in serious study mode or when out with friends so I can really be in the moment.

Since the last time I used this, they have added some new capabilities. You can tag trees to say what you were doing while growing your tree. You can use the app with your friends to really make your group focus or actually spend time with each other. And, one of my favorites, you can use the virtual coins you earn from growing trees to plant a tree in real life.

If I have one criticism, it is that they set point values for new trees and real trees entirely too high. It is very hard to raise enough coins to unlock even one new tree type let alone get the funds to plant a tree in real life!

title: Easy, motivating, effective
body:
I downloaded the app for work productivity, but it’s made me hyper-aware of how often I actually pick up my phone. For any task, just having the reminder that my phone is not currently available to me is extremely helpful. I’m realizing that I waste a ton of time that stems from, say, just looking at a text that could wait until later. Moral: don’t think this app isn’t useful because you’re not at a desk all day. It has countless uses. 

I agree with what other users have said about gamification being a good motivator, and the user interface is very appealing. Creating and naming tags produces helpful data. For instance, if you’re concerned about work-life balance, you can see a colorful pie chart with a few simple clicks. 

One thing: I’m fine with how the trees become more “expensive” as time passes. However, it can take a long, long time to gain sufficient coins after awhile. I’m not asking for instant and easy gratification, because that’s contrary to the spirit of the app. I think adding more achievement bonuses (that don’t depend on having friends that use the app or on leaderboard performance) would be great. Unlocking achievements is also rewarding and something to strive for, so I’d love to see more!
