title: Excellent for resisting distractions
body: This app really works for me. I’m not sure I really care about growing a forest, to be honest, and there are plenty of distractions out there that do not use my phone, so it would be easy to cheat. But the point of this app is to set a 25 minute timer to stay focused, and then to “nudge” you mentally back on task when your mind starts to wander, or if you think of other things to do—check email, get up and get a glass of water, whatever. This app is a reminder that whatever you think you need to do immediately, it can wait and it’s not that hard to stay focused for the time remaining in your 25 minute work session—and if you succeed you will be rewarded with a new “tree” for your forest (if that is important to you).  It’s also good to see your progress day by day and week by week.

body:

It MOTIVATES me to study because the ability to view how many minutes of work I did in a day/week makes me feel so happy and proud of myself, and it encourages me to plant more and more trees. It also encourages me to continue studying even when the timer is done since you can get more coins. Being able to study with friends is really fun, too! The different trees/bushes you can buy with coins you earn from focusing are all super cute as well. Lastly, I LOVE the idea of being able to plant a REAL tree! (It takes a TON of coins, though, so it takes a while to save up for.) 

Overall, I love this app so much, and every penny was worth it!

title: This app is charging my life
body:
First, I would like to say thank you to the creators of Forest. I am a highly distractible person, and my life has been a battle for focus (often a losing one). I honestly didn’t think this app was going to work so well. I’ve tried many techniques to attempt to focus, including the Pomodoro technique that this app employs, but have never been successful. Forest is the perfect blend of Pomodoro timer + game.

The reason it works so well for me is that I love trees and flowers. Thus, it provides me a reward that I actually want, that convinces me to not just give up and let the tree die in order to indulge my Pinterest addiction. I have a feeling that if wanting to “grow a forest” isn’t something that interests you, this may not work as well. It does help that you have the opportunity to grow real trees, thus adding an altruistic reason to succeed in focusing.

Forest is also simple to use, has adorable art, and sports a decent selection of trees and bushes to work toward for continued motivation to use the app. I hope they continue to add new types of flora as once I “complete” the game aspect of this app I may not feel as compelled to use it. 

All in all, an elegant solution to phone obsession.

title: This is the only app I’ve ever truly loved
body: I’ve never reviewed an app before, but I love this app so much. I downloaded it after my previous pomodoro timer app, tide, stopped timing correctly, which was literally all it had to do. Also, the ability to tag how I spend my time (ex: work vs all other things) is an easy way to stay balanced. For instance, I can see if I’m falling behind on daily meditating even if it’s something I’m not conscious of. I can also see someone using this app not necessarily to boost concentration but as a way to literally bar yourself from using your phone for periods of time when you need to be present (ex: during a meeting or with a friend). One more thing I love: I just finished a project that took two months, and I went back and looked at my little forests for that time. Each lil tree helped me get that project done. It’s such a beautiful reminder that everything big happens with many tiny steps!

title: Amazing!
body:
Update:

After the developer responded to my review not more than 1 day after I left it, I wanted to update my review. Just as I state below, the app is wonderful. I forgot to mention they also offer a program where you can spend your earned coins to have an organization plant a REAL tree. It’s a really great app. I totally recommend!!

I absolutely love this app. I’ve tried every other anti-procrastination app out there, and none have worked for until I found Forest. The fact that it still plants your dead tree makes you feel guilty because you’ll be able to see it. I feel like that’s the key right there. The saying “out of sight out of mind” really applies here. It’s NOT out of sight so it’s NOT out of mind. I really like this app, it is definitely worth the price

Also, there’s a chrome extension. You manually put in which websites you are NOT allowed to go to, so you can still use your computer for work (blacklist), or you put in the specific websites you ARE allowed to visit, and anything else will kill your tree (whitelist). 

All in all, this is a great app and totally worth the money if you really need help with procrastination.

title: Idea
body: This app is great. What would be really awesome too is if it could have a feature that allows users to track what they spend their time on —it would be a great thing for freelance billing and for getting an overview in general of how much time certain tasks are costing people. For instance, it would be so useful if I could set the timer for say, 25 minutes, and before hitting “Plant,” if I also had an option to name that 25-minute planting session “Storyboard illustration project 01,” or something. And then also to be able to save these task names on a list if such a storyboarding project is going to take me numerous planting sessions, so that I can just select it from a list instead of typing it ever time. With such a feature, I’d be able to look back and see how much time I tracked —good to know for my own productivity, and also to be able to track my work hours all in the same app. Either way, the app is amazing and I’ve already been able to have a real tree planted :)

title: Good App, Could Be Improved
body:
This is a pretty good app for helping people get off their phone during work, class, studying, etc.

Some things that could be improved:
1. If “taking a break” didn’t end the extra minutes you can get. As it is, the feature is useless because you may as well have just quit out of the app anyway.

2. If you could take one break during the original time you had allotted. This would be useful for long work periods and/or if you just needed to make a quick phone call or text.

3. Giving up should give you a dead tree and the alive trees you already earned. If you spend 60 minutes working, then have to end 5 minutes early for something, all your time working shouldn’t go to waste just because of that five minutes!

3b. Dead trees also have “stages” based on how much time you gave up on, where giving up on less time gives you a smaller dead tree.

title: Worth
body:
Does this app improve my productivity and therefore happiness? Yes. Is it perfect? No. Some minor bugs and annoyances. Lacks some features I would like. However, best app like it that I know, and I don’t think a further investment of research/experimentation is likely to be worth it.
 I do recommend it.

Edit: 
Example of minor bug/annoyance: menu animates and collapses into a single position.

Example of “missing” feature: a friend of mine tracks a set of activities that only partly intersects with mine. I would like to be able to either: have shared tags, which is what is tracked in the social competition, or be able to see what her activities are for that day- which incidentally brings up: why can’t I see a friend’s activity for the past week?

There’s a lot more, naturally, but those are the first two gripes that came to mind.

Anyway, solid app regardless.

title: Changed The Way I Spend My Day!
body:
I’m very easily distracted, a habitual phone checker and struggle with my ability to focus. I used to pick my phone up every 2 minutes, even less, just clicking the phone screen to see if anything new had happened or just to check the time (even if I jut checked 45 seconds ago). 

When I downloaded Forest, it took some time for me to actually get the ball rolling and utilising it as much as I can. 

I love knowing how I spend the minutes in my day. I love the productivity I feel when I’m in a flow state and am not distracted by a cellphone going off, I love how much work I get done when I’m not spending one minute refreshing all my apps for every five minutes I’m working on something. 

I use it to time things I hate doing, like the dishes or studying or mopping. I use it for things I love, like yoga, running and reading. 

Plus, every few minutes I spend allows me to receive a coin, which will eventually build up until I’m able to plant a REAL tree. This inspires and drives me to spend mindful minutes in order to have the reward of doing something good. 

All in all, I LOVE Forest. 

I do wish we could customise our dashboard, though. 

10/10

title: Put Down the Darned iPad!!
body:
I am an adult woman with ADHD. I am addicted to iPad games, Facebook games, you name it! I also have responsibilities. “Forest” helps with the latter. Once I plant my trees, I am far less likely to pick up the iPad until the requisite time has passed. Yes, I know they’re not real trees, but still, it works. 

I do not use the app in a competitive fashion, but to help me put down the iPad and get on with my life. Once I plant my tree, I often don’t pick up the iPad until well after the tree has grown, but the mere action of planting a cartoon tree in a cartoon forest helps me to put down the darned iPad!

I highly recommend this app!

title: Actually helpful!!
body:
I’m your typical college student/office worker; I’m on my desk at work, home, or school and my phone often keeps me busy doing ANYTHING but my actual work I’m supposed to be focusing on... this app was worth the every penny.

I actually have fun growing as many trees as I can during a work shift, school day, or study sesh in my room. I like that they also have “timed breaks” after you’ve grown a tree. What i do is the Pomodoro Technique: I grow a tree for 25-30mins then take a timed 5min break where I get up and do something else then repeat it!

The visuals of how many trees you’ve done gives this a healthy desire to fill up your little forest each day.

title: I LOVE this app! A couple of requests...
body:
This app is the best for those who need a little visual stimulation and extra incentive to stay productive. I truly hate exiting the app during a work session (thus killing my little sapling), and I get a lot of satisfaction from seeing my daily forest grow. The app has kept me from getting distracted by calls, texts, and web-browsing on many occasions. 

A couple of requests: I would love more kinds of ambient sounds to be added to the "store." Also, please create a version for Mac desktop to keep us chronic procrastinators from using distracting apps and websites there! I know that a basic version of Forest exists as a Chrome extension, but it lacks a lot of my favorite features from the app, and doesn't currently block distracting desktop apps. I'm not such a fan of Chrome, anyway (I prefer Safari). In any case, keep up the fantastic work! Oh! And go check out the SleepTown  app by the same developer. It uses the same concept to help people develop better sleep habits, and I can verify that it helps with getting a good night's sleep!

title: The updates and tree variety keep me hooked
body:
I have a newborn son, and we have a routine. He wakes me up about an hour to two hours before I’d normally be up for work. I plant a two-hour tree with Forest and I play with my boy. It was hard at first, because babies don’t appear terribly interesting at times, and I’ve had such a long-time habit of checking the morning news on my phone. But when I plant a tree in the morning, I am so focused on my boy and no longer tempted to read or check my phone. He has my complete attention. 

My wife and I also plant trees right before we sit down to dinner with our kids or watch a movie with them. Forest really helps us to be and stay present with our family. 

I’ve tried other apps that had similar concepts of growing plants and trees, and when they stopped updating I got bored.  Forest has a wonderful variety and updates that have kept me hooked and interested.

And seeing them die saddens me, which more or less reminds me that I need to protect them by focusing on my tasks. Fundamentally, the visualisation of how I spent my time leaves no chance for me to find an excuse for not getting work done; now I am confident to say “hey, I have actually focused on my work a lot.”

title: Secret weapon in war against ADD
body: Forest is a vital tool for me in school. I have been using the app for about 11 months now, and I can say it is completely worth the cost. As a college student who has had to work her way back from a 2.0 GPA to a Masters student, I can say that this app has contributed to my growing success academically. I used to get easily side-tracked by notifications on my phone or even just by scrolling through my camera roll to procrastinate. Now, I like logging hours and knowing exactly how much time per day and week I spend preparing for classes. Knowing I can't take a break until my tree is grown keeps my self control strong. Logging study hours gives me confidence before each lecture or test because I can operationally define how much studying is "a lot of studying." Additionally, I use this app as one of several weapons against symptoms of ADD. I used to justify distractions on my phone, telling myself I couldn't miss out when I got a snap chat or Instagram notification. This app has shown me that those social distractions snowballed into hour-long escapades online and kept me from completing basic academic tasks. I tell everyone who asks about this app that it is fantastic. I love that there are new changes, such as the background sounds and 10 second grace periods. Additionally, the opportunities for awards keep me coming back; since the start of fall term I've made it my goal to plant healthy trees thirty days in a row. My suggestion for this app would be to keep it simple no matter how many updates it goes through. Other apps such as Instagram and Snapchat (though they serve entirely different purposes) are receiving poor reviews because they added too many unnecessary features. As someone who gets distracted easily, I fully appreciate the simplicity of this app and its basic reward system. Please keep the app clean and simple! Thank you for this app!

author: Just A Tree

title: Amazing app!
body:
There are a few things I adore about this app.

The Trees Themselves

The trees are a physical manifestation of all of the time you’ve spent doing things that are important to you. There are many activities where the time spent is more important than the important than the ultimate product of the activity. The trees place a tangible value on that time and that is a wonderful gift. 

The Rewards

This app turns working into a game.
Like any good phone game, you get gold coins and rewards and there are things you can buy with them. For each tree you plant, you earn gold coins that can either be spent on fancy virtual trees or real trees planted through a charity.

You get extra gold coins for hitting various checkpoints (working for a total number of hours, planting trees a certain number of days in a row, etc.)

These are great additional sources of motivation for when you really want to spend the day binging that new Netflix show, but you’re so close to being able to afford that cat-shaped tree, you might as well get an hour of work in.

However, I will say that I REALLY wish there were more checkpoints and achievements available, because working towards those is something I love doing. 

Limited Distractions

A lot of the time when I write, I open apps reflexively. My mind is straining to figure out a plot hole and suddenly I’m scrolling through Twitter, without any conscious intent.

With this app, that reflex is blocked. Every time you reflexively pick up your phone to check twitter/facebook/whatsapp/whatever, you’re reminded that you have **:** minutes left in this session.

Task Tags

The ability to tag how I'm spending my time with various tasks is great. The app lets you view your 'stats’ to see how much time you spend on your respective tasks so you can better visualise how you spend your 'focused’ hours. It's beyond useful if you really want to work on time management. 

Customisable Inspiration

I love adding my favorite inspirational quotes to the home screen.

title: Make it a habit and it's golden.
body:
I've been using this app for years now, forgetting about it here and there. This last year, though, I made it a habit and remember to open it when I have a task that needs my undivided attention. The ease of use is welcomed, in addition to the overall presentation. 

The trees and bush types one can acquire are adorable and thought out, with variations based on the time one sets for the goal. The unlock-able sounds are basically the only ones I don't unlock, but maybe others have uses for it. I also look forward to spending my earned coins on a real tree in the future, now that I use this app often enough to make it a reality. The app does a very good job of explaining the process. 

If I'd ask for any improvement, it would probably be in the layout of the forest. Once a person has a number of trees for the month, the placement feels a little repetitive or uniform. Mirroring a few of the trees might help alleviate this, and possibly grouping related trees/bushes in rounded patterns, instead of rows. 

Otherwise, it is very awesome to see my efforts visualized. Worth the dough in my opinion, if one makes it a habit.

body:

I am aware that there seems to be a Whitelist on the android version of this app, and am curious to know if it would be possible for this version. Ultimately, though, one really ought to stay away from their phone in general when Foresting.

I've managed to convince one of my friends to buy this app, and we spend time reading together and staying focused. Even during the semester, we Forest together for hours on end and are thrilled to know that our distraction-free efforts certainly do pay off.

If you are a firm believer in the Pomodoro technique, you can set a 20/25 minute timer, and then set a break timer when you finish, and then repeat.

Forest has served myself and my friends well. It can serve you, too.

title: Great!
body:
Wonderful app overall, helps me stay focused with work (important for a Masters student approaching finals!), and finally leave my phone alone. The guilt mechanism, to be honest, works wonders for me, especially with being able to plant trees through an NGO after winning a certain number of coins. I've planted two so far and while the going isn't fast -- I only set Forest for specific study tasks (and to help me track how much I've worked) instead of other points in time, it's a great feeling to know that you're doing something that has an actual impact, of a small one. I do worry a little bit about Forest's long run funding for those trees, but we'll have to see, I guess. 

Two criticisms:
 I would personally find if more helpful if you could set a time limit superior to two hours (as opposed to setting reminders to plant a tree, or getting the phone that buzzes once the tree is planted mid-study session). Along that vein, it would be helpful to get extra coins for surpassed time, up to a cap at least. One of the two options would certainly provide great motivation.

My second criticism is that the app only provides a reminder that you're about to kill your tree on select occasions. If your phone is already past the locked screen and on the app, it will give a reminder at the top of the screen. But if you swipe into another app from the lock screen (easily happens if you forgot you had planted a tree), you don't get that reminder/notification. Figuring that kink out, and perhaps increasing the clemency delay to about 10 seconds instead of 3-5 (I'm not sure what it currently is) would be great.

title: An easy way to make a feel-good impact
body:
I'm a medical student (with ADHD) and I've been using Forest for 2-3 months to help me stay focused while studying. It's a win-win: you accomplish more AND help plant real trees. Highlights:
(1) SIMPLE/EASY: you merely dial how many minutes you'd like to stay off your phone, then put it down. The app will alert you when the countdown has finished and you can use your phone again. 
(2) EFFECTIVE: having a tangible goal (i.e. planting a REAL tree) helps motivate you to use the app and to not bail/fail. I used to constantly grab my phone to text someone or Snapchat something funny, but this app prevents me from doing that without feeling like a punishment.
The timer is very flexible (you can turn it on for as little as 5 minutes!) so it's easy to incorporate into your life, e.g. while studying/working, while driving (you  shouldn't be touching your phone anyway), during meetings, during meals, etc. It'll quickly become an easy and rewarding habit. Also, this is a great option for anyone utilizing the Pomodoro method (cycles of 25 mins working/studying, 5 mins off).
(3) ACCOMMODATING: the app will continue running if you receive/answer a phone call (but not texts). Also, when you set the timer it gives you 10 seconds to cancel it; I've set the timer and then immediately remembered I had to return an important call, and I just cancelled the timer without losing points.
(4) REWARDING: I feel elated every time I accrue enough points to plant a REAL TREE. It's a perpetuating feel-good cycle: I feel happy when I use the app, so I want to use it more, so I feel happier, so I use it more, etc etc. 

Overall, I can't say enough about this app! I recommended it to everyone in my med school class, and I absolutely recommend it to you.

title: Get it!
body:
This is one of my favorite apps and I highly recommend getting it. It's worth every penny. 

I felt compelled to write a review because it's succeeded not only on a basic level of strengthening my focus and heightening my productivity — and is beautifully and thoughtfully designed to boot, offering a delightful experience — but I love that the developers didn't program it to goad you into writing a review every other time you open it unlike most apps out there; thank you, developers. 

I definitely have a healthy amount of discipline to not be on my phone all the time, but find that once I go down a rabbit hole, it's sometimes difficult to dig myself out of it. Then, half an hour later, when I surface for airI, I wonder what I've done and if it was at all worth it; usually the answer is "no." 

But with this app in my digital tool belt? Well, give it a whirl yourself— you may just find that you become even more addicted to being off your phone than on it. And you may just find yourself becoming more and more connected to the moment, being more present, and enjoying all that life off of a phone has to offer — a welcome respite in today's world of faster turnarounds, quarterly profit earning reports, and the "faster is better" mentality.

title: Am I missing something?
body:
I really wanted this app to work for me. Unfortunately, it fell short by a lot. 

When a tree is growing, you can't use your phone at all. There isn't a way to designate certain apps as productive. And you can't pause the app, so you have to wait or lose your tree. For this reason, I kept having to change my workflow to do tasks that were legit. That left me resenting the app. 

And I had a really hard time remembering to continuously reset the app (trees only take 25 minutes to grow), leading to frustration when I didn't get credit for the productive time I actually accomplished. I mean, isn't that the whole point? Or is it more about focusing on this company? 

It honestly feels like a pointless app in practice even though I think the idea behind it is great. They need to add settings options that allow users to set their own parameters for success. If you need your phone for work, this app definitely isn't for you. If you want to use it with family members or friends to encourage less phone distraction, it's probably more fun.

title: LOVE but 1 question
body:
I LOVE this app!  I was recently diagnosed with ADHD and a big issue I have is that when I take meds I can focus but sometimes I go a bit over and hyperfocus on the wrong things. This app helps me stop doing that. The most important things one has to do in life is not related to a phone-cooking, cleaning, taking care of kids, work,etc. like many, however, I make my phone the center of my world at times which is esp bad for someone with ADHD.  This has made it possible for me to get a positive reward for doing what I should do anyway. Plus, I love the fact that a real tree  will be planted when I reach 2500 credits. That's a real-world reward I can be proud of!!

I DO HAVE ONE QUESTION, HOWEVER...

Is it possible to add more tags?  I'd rather have the ability to add tags for things I do often so they can be properly tracked over time rather than being able to write in the notes. The "work" tag isn't relevant to me nor does it completely relate to what I do because my work is all over the place. I think many people's jobs are like that these days. I've re tagged as much as I can but it only seems to allow for 5. Can I aad more?  Am I missing it?

Also, I agree with another reviewer who said we sometimes don't get credit for additional time because we get focused and don't realize it's shut off. I'd rather get additional credit if one keeps going.

title: Fantastic app for those who need focus, structure, and productivity
body:
I'm a medical student and for a very, very long time I had trouble focusing for long hours and getting my studying done. My severe lack of productivity was becoming such a strong source of stress for me on top of the demand for school, and feeling discouraged and unmotivated didn't help.

Then I discovered this app a week ago. I've already turned my productivity around. The fun and cool, and no-nonsense way this app makes sure you're productive is incredibly creative and simple. Grow trees, and if you distract yourself, it dies. It's a great concept that builds structure and focus because, let's face it, the dead trees in your forest are such a turn off. The app /makes/ you want to be productive and play by it. 

I love it and I'm such a fan of this app. I would pay 10x the price for it. Its aesthetics are nice, the motivational quotes are great, and it functions well. I get excited for every update for this app now!

Keep up the great work!!

Wow I rambled... Sorry. But you won't be sorry for getting this app!

title: A Great Motivational App for Writing, Studying, Everything!
body:
This is a GREAT app to keep you motivated and focused. I'm a writer, blogger, and student. I use Forest to track my writing and see how much time I've put into the app. I love the feature that allows you to see how much (and when) you spend your time; the pie chart that lists all your activities for the day, week, and year; and best of all: the trees.

The trees motivate me most of all because I'm such a visual person. There are different species that you must unlock, making every hour spent on this app worth it when you see your vast, sprawling forest of pine trees, cherry blossoms, and bushes. You can set a timer for as little as 10 minute bushes (I have a lot of these) to a tree of 120 minutes. The trees change appearance according to how much time you put in. The more time you put in, the prettier the trees are. 

This app helped me write a book. I'm a huge procrastinator, but focusing for 2+ hours a day honed my time to writing my book. I can't wait to see what it will do for me in college.

Forest is worth all the time and money I put into it.

I am now more motivated to do everything around the house (I am a teenager with depression and anxiety) and also to work on my summer assignment. I could not have done it without this app. Being addicted to your phone is something a lot of us can't really admit to since phones are so popular nowadays and it almost seems normal to be so focused on them. This app is a blessing! I will keep on using it for as long as possible.

title: Lacks flexibility
body: This app is really cute and the idea of growing your own forest is great. I've downloaded other focus timer apps and this one was the only one that really motivated me to be focused. Despite its creativity, it lacks flexibility. The timer is only limited to max 2 hours. Not that I would want to focus for 10 hours.. But wish I had the flexibility to choose greater number of hours if I wanted. However, I understand why the creators have limited it to two (simplicity of the dial and most people probably won't need to focus for more than 2 hours..) Perhaps the option can be included in the settings to set your own maximum hour? Also note that the timer can only go in increments of 5 min. Additionally, as one reviewer mentioned, it does not kill the tree if I use another app while using the timer. It will only kill if you choose "give up". Otherwise than these, I would give it 5 stars!

title: Nice app but needs more tree options
body:
This is a sweet idea but it needs to refine to its "game" element to hold interest/charm. For example, have a graduated price scale for tree purchases (rather than every option being worth 500 coins). Also, it would be great if some of the trees generated more coins at a very slow rate, as extra incentive to plant/tend the trees. I would pay good money for an even slightly more complex version of this that felt more game-like. 

Finally, it would be great if after a certain threshold you could purchase coins to plant real-life trees. You'd still have incentive to be productive, but more real trees would also get planted. Which is important and a great side-outcome.

title: Sheer Genius
body: This is one of those apps that has become so essential and transformative in my life - both because *it* works so well, and because it inspires *me* to work well - that I'm always worried the people behind it will either get bought out or simply not get enough traction to keep going. Essentially, the genius of it is that it creates an emotional and literal landscape for the time we invest in ourselves. In today's world, when everything we do has become so abstracted, this is the perfect disruption through a child-like, visual metaphor that not only feels good, feels real, but also (apparently?) makes a real difference in doing good for the environment (your virtual trees can add up to a real tree being planted!). Please don't ever stop! This should be the top app.

title: Game Theory and The Silent Game
body: Do you remember playing the silent game when you were a child? A parent would say "Ok, let's play the silent game" as you guys were in the car or out shopping. Everybody would try to stay silent and the one who stayed silent the longest would win. The goal for the parents being that the children stay silent and well behaved while providing the children with a challenge, or a game, to be as silent as possible for as long as possible. This app is kind of like your mom telling you to stay off of your phone for "X" amount of time. X = Time you set. If you  stay off of your phone for the time you set for yourself then you get a beautiful virtual tree and some coins to put towards new species of virtual trees or towards planting a real tree in real life. I love this app and I think it was worth the $3. Kudos to the developers for devolving an app that you literally do nothing but wait.

I have never been so satisfied with an app purchase. You set the time you want to study and during that time a tree grows. And if you leave the app your tree dies. And every time you complete the cycle that you set, your tree is added to your "forest". It sounds silly because it's virtual, but it actually works since you feel guilty if you touch your phone and killed the tree. It's like a game!

I had an organic chemistry exam and my phone distracts me very easily, so this app was perfect. Thanks Forest!

title: Functional, Hardly Plants Tree However
body: Everything is functional, I would suggest this fun way if you want help focusing. There is also a feature to help plant real trees in India or Zambia. It costs 2500 in game currency, which is generated by planting virtual trees. The formula for obtaining this currency is 4+X+5Y where X is every 5 minutes and Y is every 30 minutes spent growing an in game tree (this is the function by, which you are expected to focus on work while you wait 15-120 minutes on the virtual tree to grow). If you only grow the max timer tree, 120 minutes, you obtain 4+(120/5)+5(120/30) currency, which amounts to 48. The minimum cost of a planting real tree is 2500. That is 52 two hour tree, or 104 hours of using this app to generate enough currency to plant a real tree. You do start game with 500 currency, which if you don't spend in the in game store, could reduce that cost of a real tree to 84 hours of using this app. If you're extremely dedicated you may plant a tree in two months maybe. For those out there striving for that, I applaud your effort, but you could also work a part time job and earn enough money to outright purchase trees in less hours. So this feature that allows you to plant real trees in parts of the world is very cool, but not actually practically achievable for the majority of people who want to try this app.

title: Almost amazing!
body:
Love this concept. I'm a huge fan of the "self-control" app for Mac, and this is a great iPhone analog. Unfortunately, lots of work happens on the phone, and the app's design does not take this into account. Work on your phone is often hindered by notifications and excessive app switching. 

Recommendation (and please forgive me, app designer, if this is not a trivial feature to implement)... 
1. Plant a tree (with phone work activated)
2. Move to the WorkApp where you need to spend a good amount of time focusing, eg reading a book or long article. 
3. If user switches from the WorkApp, kill the tree using the same mechanism Forest uses to track if you leave the Forest app (with the drop down notification to switch back to WorkApp)

Also, the login is silly. Use OAuth. No one wants to make a new account.

title: Effective for studying with ADD
body:
Being someone who has ADD, I have a hard time staying focused on tasks and am easily distracted by even the tiniest things. Once distracted, it takes a long time get back on track. Forest has all the right incentives for making me stay off my phone. Planting a tree for the purpose of doing a specific task really makes me feel like I NEED to follow through on it, and I get rewarded for doing so. I feel the need to focus more because I get to collect a forest and even unlock different kinds of trees including real ones! 
So far I've used it for getting ahead of school work and helping myself get to sleep at night by eliminating the distraction of the phone. Forest works so much better than just turning it off because it makes you feel like you CAN'T use the phone.
Thanks for this great app!

title: Not worth paying for
body:
The features in this app are basic and not worth paying for. The concept of this app is great and the interface is beautiful, but there are fundamental flaws that wouldn't be acceptable for a free app, let alone one you're paying for. 

1. There needs to be timer options for less than 30 minutes.

2. The app should have much vaster options to allow a user to expand their forest. Grow a variety of trees, plant flowers, add animals, expand land...etc. Your forest should not be limited as your personal growth and goals are not limited either.

3. Apple watch integration is a must.

Those three suggestions would make this app worth paying for. Don't waste your money like me.

title: Near perfect
body:
I just downloaded this app and I adore it. It's gorgeous and The developers did an EXCELLENT job. Bravo!

Some suggestions:

1)

As others said more flexibility with time options. I know that presents a problem of how do you present this in an image format. Smaller timed accomplishments =smaller trees perhaps? 

2)

As others have said, the ability to use the other apps while using this app. For example, I try to watch Netflix while I take care of the dishes. Currently, I can't do this AND use this app. 

3) 

The ability to have more than one profile. (I could use this to motivate my kids to use this to complete their chores. 

4) I say the developers should really go to town on their forest theme. More varieties of trees, flowers, birds, fairies, trolls, mushrooms, brooks, springs, waterfall etc. An entire forest, with different themed areas (enchanted snow forest, magical forest etc.) kinda like building your own city. I'm cheap but I will pay for this (a low price please). 

Lastly, I look forward to using this daily. I also look forward to your updates. Great job!!

title: Great concept but lacking features
body:
After a solid few days of use, I can honestly say that this app works. From a psychological level, the sense of achievement one gets from successfully planting a tree is quite satisfying. Knowing that you've set aside time where you can be productive and free of distractions is a wonderful thing.
In terms of functionality, different plants for different time increments would be nice. There is beauty in simplicity, but there is also beauty in lilacs. And daisies. And various shrubs. Would be nice to see that sort of thing in my forest.
Also, I'd like it if there was an ability for custom tags, rather than sticking with the vague "working, studying, etc." tags. 
Other than that, this app is a job well done.

body:

🔻 Keeps your phone out of your hand 
🔻 Helps you chart what each tree is for
🔻 Cute graphics. 
🔻 You can lock your phone while planting trees. 

Cons:
🔻 Each day is its own forest.

The app obviously still does what it's supposed to, but I see opportunity for so much more. You could add different trees, (5 normal trees, turn into one larger different tree). title: Gamification to Get Work Done
body:

Everything runs seamlessly, it's responsive, the colors are beautiful, etc. My only complaint is that there aren't more features. Luckily, the developers are hard at work implementing these and have even created a news feature within the app, allowing users to follow along and see what will be added/changed in upcoming versions based on customer feedback.

author: Nick2553

title: Excellent focus app
body: I'm always in the market for productivity apps, and this one's a gem. Like the pomodoro method, you take bursts of focus in order to slowly but surely tackle a project. Unlike the pomodoro method, this app gives you visual feedback as you make progress, growing a forest as you exercise your focus. This app is a great tool to ignore that distracting phone and get work done!
